description: Pair entries, theme lines and feeling links drafted on 16 October 2026 so every combination of blocks gets feedback, and on 6 November 2026 for the blocks added from the rule books. Not reviewed; no example games, since none were checked. The curated entries in interactions.json come first.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move around the board, and the spaces you land on let you pick from a shared row of cards.
pros: The dice decide where you go, the cards give you a choice.
Easy to start, with something to think about each turn.
cons: A low roll can leave only poor cards to pick from.
Picking can slow down a game that feels quick.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and some spaces start an auction where everyone offers to pay for a prize.
pros: Auctions give everyone a reason to pay attention on other turns.
Money matters, not only lucky rolls.
cons: Landing on auction spaces is still down to the dice.
Players who are low on money can feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: You keep rolling to move further, but one unlucky roll can send you back.
pros: Every roll is a little gamble you choose to take.
Loud, exciting turns.
cons: A long run of unlucky rolls can feel unfair.
Careful players may move very slowly.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move pieces around a board and try to hold spaces before others reach them.
pros: Big moments when a roll lands you right where you need.
The board changes as people take ground.
cons: The dice can decide who gets the key spaces.
Players far behind can find it hard to catch up.

pairs.tendency: Dice decide how far you move or how many workers you get, then you place them on actions.
pros: Mixes luck and planning in one turn.
Every turn offers a few real options.
cons: A poor roll can block your plan.
Two systems to learn at once can feel heavy.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and where you land gives you pieces to build a shape or pattern.
pros: Puzzle-building with a bit of surprise.
Each piece you collect matters.
cons: You might not land where the piece you need is.
Players can end up waiting for one lucky space.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and cards in your hand let you change the roll or do something extra.
pros: Cards give you some control over the dice.
Saving a card for the right moment feels clever.
cons: Tracking cards and dice together takes some care.
A hand of weak cards does not help much.

pairs.tendency: Players win card tricks, and each trick won lets them move forward on a track.
pros: Every hand of cards pushes the race on.
Card skill turns into movement you can see.
cons: The movement part can feel like an extra step.
One player who wins many tricks can run away.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and you can make deals with others to swap spaces, money or favours.
pros: Talking and dealing make every turn social.
Clever deals can make up for poor rolls.
cons: Long talks can slow the game down.
Quieter players can get left out of deals.

pairs.tendency: You roll around the board, and each space gives you a card towards a matching set.
pros: Simple to learn, with a clear goal.
Each roll can bring the piece you need.
cons: Finishing a set can depend on luck.
Players can collect without ever meeting each other.

pairs.tendency: You roll to see which tile you take or how far you go, then place tiles to grow the board.
pros: The map grows differently every game.
Placing tiles gives you something to plan.
cons: The dice can hand you tiles that do not fit.
Moving and placing can make turns long.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the right to pick first, then choose cards from a shared set.
pros: Going first costs something, so every choice matters.
Lots of small decisions each round.
cons: Two steps every round can slow things down.
Players short on money pick last again and again.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing cards to pick from, but if you draw one too many you lose the round.
pros: Picking feels tense because you might stop too late.
Every draw is a small risk.
cons: Stopping too late can wipe out a whole round.
Players who never take risks can fall behind.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards that let them place pieces on a map to hold areas.
pros: The cards you pick shape the map.
Watching what others pick tells you what they want.
cons: Taking a card just to block someone can feel mean.
The game can get crowded and slow.

pairs.tendency: You pick cards that give you more workers or new action spaces to use.
pros: Your choices build up how strong your turns are.
Lots of ways to plan ahead.
cons: Many options can freeze younger players.
Early picks can decide too much.

pairs.tendency: You pick tiles or cards from a shared pool and fit them into your own pattern.
pros: Calm, puzzle-like turns.
Taking a piece someone else needs is a quiet move.
cons: Little talking between players.
Looking at everyone's pattern takes time.

pairs.tendency: You pick cards into your hand, then choose when to play them.
pros: Picking and saving cards gives a lot of control.
Planning a few turns ahead pays off.
cons: Many cards to think about at once.
New players can find it slow.

pairs.tendency: Players pick their hand from a shared pile before playing tricks with it.
pros: You get some say over the cards you play with.
Knowing what others took helps you guess their tricks.
cons: The picking part adds time to each hand.
Experienced players can plan far ahead of new ones.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards and can trade or promise them to each other.
pros: Lots of talking about who takes what.
Deals can change what everyone picks.
cons: Promises can be broken, which may upset some players.
Talks can make picking very slow.

pairs.tendency: You pick cards from a shared row to build matching sets, watching what others collect.
pros: Every pick moves your sets forward.
Taking a card someone needs is a quiet move.
cons: The card you need may be taken first.
Little talking between players.

pairs.tendency: You pick tiles from a shared offer and place them to build the board.
pros: The board grows from everyone's picks.
Each pick is a little puzzle.
cons: Taking tiles just to block others is easy and can feel unkind.
The offer can run out of tiles you need.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on rewards, and the winner then risks pushing for more or stopping safely.
pros: Big moments when someone wins a bid and goes for more.
Paying more means taking a bigger risk.
cons: Losing a costly bid and then busting can sting.
Cautious players may never win anything big.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the right to place pieces or take control of areas.
pros: Every area has a price you decide.
Spending carefully is part of the plan.
cons: Players short on money can lose all the main areas.
Bidding over and over can feel slow.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the top action spaces before placing their workers.
pros: The top spots cost more, so everyone thinks about value.
No one gets the top action for free.
cons: Two steps each round can drag.
Rich players keep getting the top spots.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on pieces and then fit the pieces they win into their own pattern.
pros: You decide how much a piece is worth to you.
Puzzles stay personal even when bids are shared.
cons: Losing a piece you needed can break a pattern.
Bidding wars can take a while.

pairs.tendency: Players use cards from their hand as bids, so every bid uses up a card.
pros: Spending cards wisely is the whole game.
Saving strong cards for later feels clever.
cons: One wasted card can hurt for a long time.
Planning the whole hand takes focus.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on how many tricks they will win, then try to win exactly that many.
pros: Guessing your own hand makes every trick matter.
Close guesses feel very satisfying.
cons: Being one trick off can feel harsh.
It takes a few rounds to understand.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on prizes and can make deals to stop bidding against each other.
pros: Deals and promises shape every auction.
Lots of talking and laughing.
cons: Broken deals can cause arguments.
Quieter players can be left out.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on cards and collect them into matching sets.
pros: You know exactly why each card matters to you.
Watching what others collect changes your bids.
cons: Paying too much for one card can ruin a set.
Bidding for every card takes time.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on tiles and place the ones they win to build the board.
pros: The board grows from what people chose to pay for.
Each tile has a different value to each player.
cons: Losing bids can leave you with nothing to place.
Many rounds of bidding can slow the game.

pairs.tendency: You keep pushing to take more areas, but stretching too far can lose them all.
pros: Big swings when someone takes a risk and it works.
Every push is a choice.
cons: One failed push can knock you out of the running.
Careful players can feel left behind.

pairs.tendency: You can place extra workers on risky spaces that might pay off or might lose them.
pros: Risky spots give everyone a tempting choice.
Safe and risky plans can both work.
cons: Losing workers can leave you with little to do.
Luck can undo careful planning.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing pieces to finish a pattern, but one wrong piece can spoil it.
pros: Every draw feels exciting near the end of a pattern.
Stopping early is a real choice.
cons: A spoiled pattern can feel like wasted work.
Some players stop too early to enjoy it.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing cards into your hand, but going over a limit loses them.
pros: Deciding when to stop is the main thrill.
Cards you keep can help later.
cons: Busting loses a whole round of work.
Players who never risk can be slow.

pairs.tendency: Players can bid to win more tricks than is safe, earning more if they make it.
pros: Bold calls make every hand exciting.
Getting exactly what you called feels clever.
cons: Big risks can backfire badly.
Players who always play safe can fall behind.

pairs.tendency: Players can make risky deals, promising more than they are sure they can give.
pros: Lots of bold promises and laughter.
Deals carry real risk.
cons: Broken promises can upset people.
Players who avoid deals can miss out.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing cards to finish a set, but a wrong card can make you lose what you drew.
pros: Every draw could finish your set.
Stopping safely is always an option.
cons: Losing a nearly complete set stings.
Luck can matter more than planning.

pairs.tendency: You keep drawing tiles to place, but one that does not fit can end your turn.
pros: The board grows in sudden bursts.
Tense moments with each new tile.
cons: Turns can end with nothing placed.
Long lucky turns can leave others waiting.

pairs.tendency: Placing workers on action spaces lets you send pieces to hold areas on the map.
pros: Two kinds of competition: for actions and for land.
Planning both at once feels deep.
cons: A lot to keep track of.
Losing the key action can cost you an area.

pairs.tendency: Players hold areas on a board that score more when they form a shape or pattern.
pros: Thinking about shapes makes the map more interesting.
Blocking someone's pattern is a clear move.
cons: Reading the whole board can be slow.
One broken pattern can be hard to recover from.

pairs.tendency: Cards in your hand let you move or place pieces to take areas.
pros: Playing the right card at the right time feels clever.
Saving cards for a big move is a real plan.
cons: A poor hand can leave you unable to fight back.
Many cards and pieces to manage.

pairs.tendency: Winning a trick lets you take or hold an area on the map.
pros: Each trick has something you can see on the board.
Card play and the map connect.
cons: The map can feel like an extra layer to track.
Strong hands can win many areas at once.

pairs.tendency: Players make deals about who gets which areas, and can break them.
pros: Lots of talking, alliances and surprises.
Peace deals and betrayals keep the game lively.
cons: Broken deals can lead to real arguments.
Quieter players can be pushed out.

pairs.tendency: Holding areas gives you cards or pieces towards a matching set.
pros: The map and the sets support each other.
Choosing which area to take is a real decision.
cons: Losing an area can break a set.
Two goals at once can confuse new players.

pairs.tendency: Players place tiles to build the map and put pieces on them to claim areas.
pros: The board you fight over is one you built together.
Placing a tile can open or close an area.
cons: Busy boards can be hard to read.
Early tiles can decide a lot.

pairs.tendency: Placing workers gets you pieces to fit into your own pattern or shape.
pros: Steady, puzzle-like turns.
Planning which pieces you need is satisfying.
cons: Someone taking your action can break your plan.
Little direct contact between players.

pairs.tendency: Cards in your hand change what your workers can do on action spaces.
pros: More ways to plan each turn.
Cards let you make surprise moves.
cons: Many options can slow turns.
Hard for new players to see what to do.

pairs.tendency: Winning tricks earns you workers or the first pick of action spaces.
pros: Card play feeds your plans on the board.
Every trick matters.
cons: Two different games to learn at once.
A run of weak cards can leave you with few workers.

pairs.tendency: Players can make deals to let each other use blocked action spaces.
pros: Deals open up actions that seemed closed.
Talking is part of every round.
cons: Deals can take a long time.
Players who do not deal can feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: Placing workers gets you items to collect into matching sets.
pros: Clear goals for each turn.
Watching others' sets helps you block them.
cons: Losing the action you need can stall a set.
Quiet turns with little talking.

pairs.tendency: Workers collect tiles, and you place the tiles to build your area or a shared board.
pros: Your board grows from your choices.
Lots of ways to plan.
cons: Long turns as players think.
Early mistakes can be hard to fix.

pairs.tendency: You choose which cards from your hand to use to complete a pattern.
pros: Deciding what to keep and what to play feels thoughtful.
Patterns reward planning ahead.
cons: A hand without the right cards can stall you.
Quiet, slow turns.

pairs.tendency: Tricks you win give you cards to fit into a pattern.
pros: Winning tricks feeds a bigger puzzle.
Choosing which trick to win is a real decision.
cons: Two things to think about each hand.
Losing tricks can leave patterns unfinished.

pairs.tendency: Players trade pieces with each other to finish their own patterns.
pros: Trading gives everyone a reason to talk.
Helping someone can help you too.
cons: Players can refuse to trade and stall others.
Talks can take a while.

pairs.tendency: You collect matching items and arrange them in a pattern for extra points.
pros: Two kinds of matching in one game.
Calm, puzzle-like play.
cons: Rules for scoring can get complicated.
Little interaction between players.

pairs.tendency: You place tiles to form shapes or patterns that score points.
pros: Very visual and satisfying.
Each tile is a little puzzle.
cons: Running out of space can end your plans.
Players can go quiet while thinking.

pairs.tendency: You plan which cards to keep and when to play them across a hand of tricks.
pros: Playing the right card at the right time feels clever.
Every hand is different.
cons: Weak hands can feel hopeless.
Takes a few games to learn well.

pairs.tendency: Players trade cards from their hands and make deals about what to play.
pros: Lots of talking about cards.
Clever trades can turn a weak hand around.
cons: People may hold back cards others need.
Trading can slow the game.

pairs.tendency: You hold cards in your hand and choose when to play them into sets.
pros: Waiting to play a full set feels tense.
Planning ahead pays off.
cons: Holding too many cards can cost you.
A hand that never matches can be frustrating.

pairs.tendency: Cards in your hand show which tiles you can place and where.
pros: Planning where tiles go feels thoughtful.
Each card gives a few choices.
cons: A poor hand can leave few useful moves.
Turns can be slow.

pairs.tendency: Players can talk and make deals about which tricks they will try to win.
pros: Talking adds a social layer to card play.
Deals can help a weak hand.
cons: Promises can be broken.
Takes longer than plain trick-taking.

pairs.tendency: Cards you win in tricks go into sets that score points.
pros: Every trick could finish a set.
Choosing which trick to win matters.
cons: Your hand may not let you win what you need.
Scoring at the end can take a while.

pairs.tendency: Winning a trick lets you place a tile on the board.
pros: Card play builds something you can see.
Each trick has a clear reward.
cons: Two systems to learn.
Strong hands can control the board.

pairs.tendency: Players trade cards to finish their own matching sets.
pros: Constant trading and talking.
Helping others can help you too.
cons: Some players may refuse to trade.
Trading talks can drag.

pairs.tendency: Players make deals about where tiles go on a shared board.
pros: Deals shape how the map grows.
Lots of talking.
cons: Broken promises can upset people.
Decisions can take a long time.

pairs.tendency: You collect tiles and place them in matching groups to score.
pros: Matching and building in one.
Visual and calm.
cons: You may not get the tile you need.
Little direct contact between players.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move around the board and collect points from the spaces you land on.
pros: Simple to learn and quick to play.
Every roll might bring points.
cons: Luck can decide who scores most.
Players can feel they have few choices.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and landing on some spaces knocks players out until one is left.
pros: Every roll can change the game.
Easy to understand.
cons: Players knocked out early have to wait.
Luck can knock out a careful player.

pairs.tendency: Everyone rolls to move together, trying to reach safety before the danger catches up.
pros: Shared hope on every roll.
Easy for groups to play together.
cons: Unlucky rolls can sink the whole team.
Little to decide beyond rolling.

pairs.tendency: Players roll to move as a team towards one shared goal on the board.
pros: Everyone cheers each roll.
Simple and friendly.
cons: The dice decide most of the game.
Some players can feel they did nothing.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, each player secretly trying to reach their own places on the board.
pros: Guessing what others are after adds mystery.
Your path matters to you alone.
cons: Dice can stop you reaching your goal.
Others may never notice what you were doing.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move along a story path, and the game ends when the story is told.
pros: The board feels like a journey.
Easy to follow.
cons: Rolls can feel like they do not matter to the story.
The ending can come suddenly.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards that move them forward, racing to be first to the end.
pros: Each pick is a step in the race.
Taking a card someone needs slows them down.
cons: Early picks can decide who wins.
Fast players can pull away.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards that attack or protect, until only one player is left.
pros: Every pick is about staying in.
Choosing between attack and defence is a real decision.
cons: Players knocked out early have to wait.
Ganging up on one player can happen.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards together to fight off a danger that threatens everyone.
pros: Choosing cards as a team means lots of talking.
Every pick helps the group.
cons: One player can end up deciding for everyone.
A weak set of cards can doom the team.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards to help the group reach one shared goal.
pros: Picking for the team feels generous.
Lots of planning together.
cons: Some players can feel their picks did not matter.
Strong players may tell others what to pick.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards, each secretly working towards their own goal.
pros: Guessing why someone took a card is fun.
Taking a card can quietly block someone.
cons: Your goal may need cards others take first.
Little open talking.

pairs.tendency: Players pick cards that add scenes to a story, and the game ends when the story is complete.
pros: Picks shape where the story goes.
Creative and calm.
cons: Choosing for the story and for yourself can clash.
The end can feel loose.

pairs.tendency: Players bid to move forward, racing to the finish line.
pros: Spending money to move fast is a real choice.
Close races near the end.
cons: Players who spend early can run out.
Rich players can rush ahead.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on prizes worth points, and the most points at the end wins.
pros: Every auction is about value.
Watching others' bids helps you plan.
cons: Overpaying once can cost you the game.
Lots of maths for some players.

pairs.tendency: Players bid to attack or defend, and anyone who runs out is knocked out.
pros: Tense bidding when someone is close to out.
Spending carefully keeps you in.
cons: Players out early have to wait.
Rich players can push others out.

pairs.tendency: Players pool or bid resources together to hold off a danger.
pros: Deciding who pays builds teamwork.
Everyone has a stake.
cons: Arguments about who pays can start.
Running out of money can doom the team.

pairs.tendency: Players bid to decide who takes on which part of a shared goal.
pros: Fair ways to split work.
Lots of talking.
cons: Some players may never win a bid.
Bidding can slow down a team game.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on items, each secretly wanting different things.
pros: Bids give hints about secret goals.
Bluffing with bids is possible.
cons: Your goal may cost more than you can pay.
Hard to read for new players.

pairs.tendency: Players bid on story parts, and the story finishes when all parts are taken.
pros: Deciding what a story piece is worth is unusual and fun.
The story grows from everyone's bids.
cons: Bids can matter more than the story.
The ending can feel random.

pairs.tendency: You keep taking risks to grab more points, but going too far loses them.
pros: Every turn has a big choice.
Exciting scoring moments.
cons: Bust turns can feel harsh.
Lucky players can run away with it.

pairs.tendency: Players take risks to stay in, and those who push too far are knocked out.
pros: Tense moments near the end.
Easy to follow who is still in.
cons: Players out early have to wait.
Luck can knock out a careful player.

pairs.tendency: The team decides together how far to push towards a shared goal before stopping.
pros: Group choices about risk lead to lively talk.
Everyone feels each push.
cons: One cautious or reckless voice can take over.
A failed push hurts everyone.

pairs.tendency: You take risks to reach your own secret goal without others seeing what you need.
pros: Risky moves can reveal your goal.
Mystery and tension together.
cons: Busting can expose your plan.
Others may not notice your risks.

pairs.tendency: Players push their luck to move the story forward, risking setbacks.
pros: Every risk adds a twist to the story.
Exciting turns.
cons: Setbacks can make the story stall.
The ending can feel random.

pairs.tendency: Players race to take a set number of areas first.
pros: A clear target keeps everyone focused.
Blocking someone near the finish is tense.
cons: Early leaders can be hard to stop.
Turns can be about blocking more than building.

pairs.tendency: Holding areas scores points, and the most points at the end wins.

Players far behind can lose interest.

pairs.tendency: Players work together to hold areas against a spreading danger.

Clear shared goal.

One player can direct everyone.

pairs.tendency: Players work together to take control of a set of areas.

Planning who goes where leads to lots of talk.

Little tension between players.

pairs.tendency: Players fight over areas, each secretly needing certain ones.

Secret goals can make fights confusing.

pairs.tendency: Holding areas moves a story forward, and the game ends when the story is done.
pros: The map tells a story.
Every area matters to the plot.
cons: Story and map can pull in different directions.

Little suspense between players.

pairs.tendency: Players place workers, each secretly working towards their own goal.

Blocking without knowing why.

Calm, thoughtful turns.
cons: Nobody can plan the whole shape.
A piece that ignores the last one can feel rude.

pairs.tendency: You keep cards in your hand and choose which one answers the last card played.
pros: Saving the right answer feels clever.
Players think a few turns ahead.
cons: A hand with no fitting answer can stall you.
Tracking the chain and your hand takes focus.

pairs.tendency: Each card played answers the card that led the trick, as in following suit.
pros: A familiar rhythm of lead and answer.
Reading the lead is a skill.
cons: Answers are limited by the cards in hand.
Some players lead every trick and others only answer.

pairs.tendency: Every offer answers the last offer, so deals build up like a conversation.
pros: Lots of talking and laughing.
Players learn how others think.
cons: Talks can go round in circles.
Quieter players may never start a chain.

pairs.tendency: You answer the last card played with one from the same set, and the sets build up.
pros: Clear reasons for each card you play.
Every answer moves your sets forward.
cons: An answer you need may never come.
The chain can stop when nobody holds a match.

pairs.tendency: Each tile answers the last tile, so the map grows as a chain of replies.
pros: The board tells the story of who answered whom.
Each tile is a small puzzle.
cons: A tile that fits nowhere ends the chain.
The map can grow in odd directions.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other only by what they play, with no words at all.
pros: Every move is a message.
The table feels quiet and focused.
cons: Answers can be misread with no way to explain.
New players may not know what counts as an answer.

pairs.tendency: A player can answer the last move by changing a rule, and the next player answers that change.
pros: The game itself becomes the conversation.
Players invent as they go.
cons: The rules can drift far from where they started.
Keeping track of every change takes care.

pairs.tendency: Each answer moves you forward, and the first to reach the end wins.
pros: Quick answers push the race on.
Every turn has a clear purpose.
cons: Slow thinkers can fall behind.
Racing can rush the answers.

pairs.tendency: Answers earn points, and whoever scores the most wins.
pros: Players try to make each answer count.
Clever answers get noticed.
cons: Scoring answers can turn play into a contest of who is cleverest.
Players may copy what scored last time.

pairs.tendency: A player who cannot answer the last move is out, until one remains.
pros: Every answer feels tense.
The chain gets harder as it grows.
cons: Players who are out early wait a long time.
Shy players can go out first.

pairs.tendency: Everyone answers each other to keep the chain going, and the group loses if it breaks.
pros: The whole table listens.
Players help each other find an answer.
cons: One stuck player can feel blamed.
Loud players may answer for others.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other to build one thing together, such as a story or a picture.
pros: What gets made belongs to everyone.
Friendly and open.
cons: Nobody controls where it ends up.
The goal can be hard to judge as finished.

pairs.tendency: Each player answers the chain while steering it towards a secret aim of their own.
pros: Answers carry a second meaning.
Spotting someone's aim is fun.
cons: Hidden aims can pull the chain apart.
Players may answer to steer rather than to listen.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other line by line until the story reaches an ending.
pros: A story grows from everyone's lines.
Endings can surprise everyone.
cons: Some stories never find an ending.
One player can take the story over.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other with no winner, and simply stop when the chain feels done.
pros: Nothing to lose, so people try odd answers.
The chain itself is what you keep.
cons: Some players miss having something to aim for.
Knowing when to stop can be unclear.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other, and each decides afterwards what a satisfying chain was for them.
pros: Each player can value different things.
Talking after the game is part of it.
cons: Players may not agree on how it went.
Some players want the game to decide.

pairs.tendency: The chain goes on until one player cannot answer, and only that player loses.
pros: Everyone else stays safe together.
Light tension on every turn.
cons: The one who loses can feel singled out.
Players may answer just to avoid losing.

pairs.tendency: Each player answers a shared prompt on their own, and the answers are compared at the end.
pros: Everyone answers the same thing in their own way.
No waiting for others.
cons: Players do not really answer each other.
The chain idea gets weaker.

pairs.tendency: Each answer is aimed at the last player, trying to top or undo what they did.
pros: Fast, lively exchanges.
Players react to each other all the time.
cons: Answers can turn into put-downs.
Gentle players may avoid answering.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other through moves on the board rather than by speaking.
pros: The board shows the whole exchange.
Answers can be subtle.
cons: Answers on the board can be missed.
It can take time to read who answered what.

pairs.tendency: All players answer each other to keep one chain going against the game.
pros: Shared rhythm and shared risk.
Everyone helps find answers.
cons: One player can answer for everyone.
Mistakes are felt by the whole group.

pairs.tendency: Players keep a shared chain going, but each answer also helps the one who gives it.
pros: Players cooperate and compete in one move.
Answers carry small private reasons.
cons: Players may answer only for their own gain.
Trust can wear thin.

pairs.tendency: Teams take turns answering each other, back and forth across the table.
pros: Team members help shape each answer.
Clear sides make it easy to follow.
cons: One team can answer much faster.
Team talk can slow the chain.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other, but one player's answers quietly push the chain off course.
pros: Every odd answer raises a question.
Spotting the traitor is part of listening.
cons: Honest odd answers can look suspicious.
The traitor's answers can confuse new players.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other by letter, so each reply arrives days after the last.
pros: Each answer has time to be thought about.
Waiting for the reply is part of the fun.
cons: The chain can lose its rhythm.
Players may forget what they were answering.

pairs.tendency: Players answer moves left by someone not at the table, such as a player from an earlier game.
pros: The chain reaches back to someone who is not there.
Old moves get a new reading.
cons: The absent player cannot explain.
Answers can drift from what was meant.

pairs.tendency: A draw or roll gives each player the word or move they have to answer with.
pros: Funny answers from cards nobody chose.
Anyone can do well.
cons: Players have little say in their answer.
Luck can make the chain feel random.

pairs.tendency: A draw gives you something to answer with, but you can swap or change it to fit.
pros: Luck starts each answer, choice finishes it.
Players feel some control.
cons: Swapping takes time.
Some draws are still hard to use.

pairs.tendency: Answers depend on how well you read the last move, with a small draw adding surprise.
pros: Skill matters, but surprises keep it light.
Clever answers stand out.
cons: Skilled players can dominate the chain.
The luck can feel tacked on.

pairs.tendency: How well you answer depends only on how well you read the last move.
pros: Players can get noticeably sharper.
No luck to blame.
cons: New players can struggle against practised ones.
The chain can feel like a test.

pairs.tendency: A thrown die or drawn card is read as a sign, and players answer what the sign seems to say.
pros: Each throw opens a new thread.
Players hear different meanings in the same sign.
cons: Signs can feel vague.
Some players want a clear answer to aim for.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other by sensing when and how the others will respond.
pros: Moments when everyone answers together feel striking.
Players watch each other closely.
cons: Hard to explain what went wrong.
New groups may take a while to settle.

pairs.tendency: Every answer is on the table, so everyone can see the whole chain.
pros: Easy to follow what happened.
Players can plan their next answer.
cons: Nothing is hidden to surprise anyone.
Players may spend long turns studying the chain.

pairs.tendency: Players answer from cards nobody else can see, so each answer is a small reveal.
pros: Every answer brings something new.
Players guess what others might answer with.
cons: You may hold no fitting answer.
Others cannot help you find one.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other while some hide who they really are.
pros: Answers become clues.
Reading answers is part of finding out.
cons: Players may answer only to hide.
The chain can turn into accusation.

pairs.tendency: Each answer gives a clue, and players work out a hidden fact from the chain.
pros: Every answer carries information.
Listening closely pays off.
cons: Missing one answer can lose the thread.
Players may answer only to test a guess.

pairs.tendency: Players answer with claims that may not be true, and the next player can doubt them.
pros: Lively back-and-forth.
Every answer can be challenged.
cons: Bluffs can upset some players.
Honest players can feel at a loss.

pairs.tendency: One player knows a secret rule about which answers count, and others learn it by answering.
pros: Each answer tests a guess about the rule.
The moment someone finds the rule feels big.
cons: Being told no again and again can sting.
The rule keeper has to stay patient.

pairs.tendency: One player knows the answer and can only reply with hints, while others answer the hints.
pros: A chain of hints and guesses.
Players read each other closely.
cons: Hints can be misread.
The player who knows can feel stuck.

pairs.tendency: Each player's move answers the last change in a model of a real system.
pros: Players see how one action leads to another.
The system's links become clear.
cons: The chain can get hard to trace.
Real systems rarely answer in turns.

pairs.tendency: Each player answers the last move as their role would, such as a farmer answering a factory.
pros: Players hear how different people respond.
Roles give each answer a voice.
cons: Players can fall into easy stereotypes.
Some roles get fewer chances to answer.

pairs.tendency: Each player answers the last player's use of a shared resource with their own use of it.
pros: The resource shows the whole conversation.
Players notice how their taking affects others.
cons: One greedy answer can spoil the resource.
Quiet players may answer last when little is left.

pairs.tendency: Each answer shows its effect only some turns later, so players answer what they cannot yet see.
pros: Players think about consequences.
Surprises when old answers come due.
cons: Hard to tell which answer caused what.
Players may lose track of the chain.

pairs.tendency: Players answer a new rule with moves that test it, and the next player answers the result.
pros: Rules get tested from several sides.
Players learn how one change spreads.
cons: The test can drift from the rule.
It can take many turns to see an effect.

pairs.tendency: Afterwards, players trace the chain of answers and talk about why each one followed.
pros: The chain gives the talk a clear order.
Players see how moves led to each other.
cons: Remembering every answer is hard.
Talk can turn into blame.

pairs.tendency: Each answer is written into the game permanently, so the next game starts from the chain you left.
pros: Answers carry weight across games.
The game grows a history.
cons: A careless answer cannot be taken back.
New players inherit choices they did not make.

pairs.tendency: Players answer each other once a day or once a week, so the chain grows slowly.
pros: Time to think about each answer.
Something to look forward to.
cons: The chain can lose its thread.
Players can drop out between answers.

pairs.tendency: Players roll and move without speaking, so nobody can plan out loud.
pros: Quick, quiet turns.
Easy for anyone to join.
cons: Players cannot warn each other about danger.
Little to do between rolls but watch.

pairs.tendency: Players pick from a shared row without speaking, reading each other only from what they take.
pros: Each pick says something.
Players notice what others want.
cons: Picks can be misread.
Quiet tables can feel tense.

pairs.tendency: Players bid without words, by placing coins or cards, so nobody can talk up a price.
pros: Bids speak for themselves.
Hard to bully anyone with talk.
cons: Players cannot explain why they bid.
Bidding wars can feel cold.

pairs.tendency: Players decide in silence whether to keep going or stop, with no one to egg them on.
pros: Each choice is your own.
The quiet makes each risk feel heavy.
cons: Nobody can help you decide.
Long pauses can drag.

pairs.tendency: Players take areas on the map without discussing it, so every move is a silent claim.
pros: The board shows what everyone wants.
No talking players out of areas.
cons: Silent attacks can feel unfriendly.
Players cannot make deals.

pairs.tendency: Players place workers without speaking, reading plans only from the board.
pros: Each placement is a quiet message.
Players watch the board closely.
cons: No way to agree who takes which space.
Blocking can feel personal.

pairs.tendency: Players build their patterns in silence, side by side.
pros: Calm and focused.
Easy to settle into.
cons: Little contact between players.
Some groups miss the chatter.

pairs.tendency: Players manage hidden hands without speaking, so the only clues are cards played.
pros: Each card played says a lot.
Players learn to read timing.
cons: Hard to recover from a misread.
New players may not know what to watch for.

pairs.tendency: Players take tricks without table talk, as many card traditions require.
pros: Every card played carries meaning.
Partners learn to read each other.
cons: Signals can be missed.
Silence can feel strict to new players.

pairs.tendency: Players negotiate without words, by offering and pushing back pieces.
pros: Funny and strange to try.
Gestures and offers do the talking.
cons: Deals can be misunderstood.
Slow when nobody can explain.

pairs.tendency: Players collect sets in silence, so nobody can ask for what they need.
pros: Calm, quiet turns.
Players read what others collect.
cons: You cannot ask for the card you need.
Little contact between players.

pairs.tendency: Players place tiles without speaking, building one board from silent choices.
pros: The board becomes the conversation.
Quiet, puzzle-like turns.
cons: A tile placed against your plan cannot be argued.
Players can lose track of shared plans.

pairs.tendency: Players change the rules without speaking, so others work out each change from what happens.
pros: Puzzling and surprising.
Players watch every move.
cons: Changes can go unnoticed.
Confusion can spread fast.

pairs.tendency: Players race without speaking, focused only on their own moves.
pros: Fast and focused.
No arguing about moves.
cons: Little sense of playing together.
Players far behind may feel alone.

pairs.tendency: Players score points without talking, so each choice is made alone.
pros: Quiet concentration.
Easy to think.
cons: Little contact between players.
Scoring can feel like a test.

pairs.tendency: Players knock each other out without words, so each attack comes as a surprise.
pros: Tense, quiet turns.
Every move is watched.
cons: Being knocked out in silence can sting.
Players who are out sit and watch.

pairs.tendency: The group tries to survive together without speaking.
pros: Moments of silent agreement feel striking.
Players learn to read each other.
cons: Losing without being able to explain is hard.
One misread can end the game.

pairs.tendency: Players work towards one goal without speaking, guessing what others plan.
pros: Everyone shares the win.
Silent teamwork feels special.
cons: Plans can clash with no way to sort them out.
Some players feel lost.

pairs.tendency: Each player chases a secret goal in silence, so the only clues are moves.
pros: Moves carry hidden meaning.
Guessing others' goals is fun.
cons: Little contact between players.
Goals can be impossible to read.

pairs.tendency: A story is told only through moves and pieces, with no spoken words.
pros: The story is left to each player to read.
Strange and quiet.
cons: Players may see different stories.
Hard to know when it is complete.

pairs.tendency: Players play in silence with no winner, and stop when it feels done.
pros: Calm, like sitting together.
Nothing to argue about.
cons: Some players may feel the point is missing.
Hard to know when to stop.

pairs.tendency: Each player sets their own aim and plays towards it without speaking.
pros: Everyone plays their own way.
A quiet, personal game.
cons: Little contact between players.
Players may not share how it went.

pairs.tendency: Players play in silence until one of them loses.
pros: Everyone else is safe together.
Quiet tension.
cons: The one who loses cannot explain.
Silent losing can feel lonely.

pairs.tendency: Each player plays their own game in silence, side by side.
pros: Very calm.
Easy to concentrate.
cons: Players hardly meet.
It can feel like playing alone.

pairs.tendency: Players attack each other without words, so every attack lands without warning.
pros: Sharp surprises.
Nobody can talk their way out.
cons: Attacks can feel cold.
Hurt feelings cannot be smoothed over.

pairs.tendency: Players affect each other only through the board, and never speak.
pros: The board says everything.
Moves are read closely.
cons: Effects on others can go unnoticed.
Quiet players can be pushed around.

pairs.tendency: The whole group works against the game without speaking.
pros: Silent teamwork feels special.
Players learn each other's timing.
cons: Mistakes cannot be explained.
One player may hold back from fear.

pairs.tendency: Players cooperate in silence while each keeps a private aim.
pros: Every move can be read two ways.
Trust grows or breaks without a word.
cons: Silent betrayal can sting.
Hard to sort out misunderstandings.

pairs.tendency: Teams play without speaking, so teammates read each other only from moves.
pros: Teammates grow close.
Strong feeling of a team.
cons: Teams can fall apart from one misread.
Hard for new team members.

pairs.tendency: A traitor hides among silent players, so suspicion comes only from moves.
pros: Every move is a clue.
Tense and quiet.
cons: Accusations cannot be discussed.
The traitor may be easy to miss.

pairs.tendency: Players send moves by post with no words attached, only the move itself.
pros: Each letter is a small mystery.
Slow and thoughtful.
cons: Moves can be misunderstood for weeks.
Players may drift away.

pairs.tendency: Players play alongside an absent player who gives no words, only moves left behind.
pros: A quiet sense of someone else being there.
Old moves get careful attention.
cons: Hard to know what the absent player meant.
Some players find it eerie.

pairs.tendency: Players roll and draw without speaking, so chance does all the talking.
pros: Simple and quick.
Nobody to blame.
cons: Little to decide.
Quiet can turn into boredom.

pairs.tendency: Players soften unlucky draws in silence, choosing alone how to fix a poor draw.
pros: Each fix is a quiet choice.
Players feel some control.
cons: No help from others.
Choices can be slow.

pairs.tendency: Skilled play in silence with a little luck mixed in.
pros: Focused, quiet thinking.
Luck keeps it from being too serious.
cons: Little contact between players.
Skilled players can pull away quietly.

pairs.tendency: Pure thinking with no talking, as in a quiet game of chess.
pros: Deep concentration.
No luck to blame.
cons: Can feel like a test.
Little warmth at the table.

pairs.tendency: Players throw dice or draw cards in silence and each reads the sign alone.
pros: A quiet, thoughtful mood.
Each player finds their own meaning.
cons: Meanings are never shared unless talked about after.
Some players feel lost.

pairs.tendency: Players act without speaking, sensing the moment the others will move.
pros: Silent moments of agreement feel striking.
Players grow very aware of each other.
cons: Losing can feel mysterious.
Hard to teach.

pairs.tendency: Everything is visible, and nobody speaks, so players read the board instead of each other.
pros: Easy to see everything.
Calm and clear.
cons: Little sense of playing together.
Long thinking turns.

pairs.tendency: Players hold hidden cards and cannot talk, so timing and choices are the only clues.
pros: Each play carries meaning.
Players learn to read each other.
cons: Many plays are misread.
New players may feel lost.

pairs.tendency: Players hide their roles without speaking, so only actions give them away.
pros: Every action is a clue.
Tense and quiet.
cons: No arguing over suspicions.
Hard to find the hidden player.

pairs.tendency: Players work out hidden facts in silence, from what others do.
pros: Deep thinking.
Quiet focus.
cons: No sharing of ideas.
Players may get stuck alone.

pairs.tendency: Players bluff without words, only through what they play and how.
pros: Faces and timing matter.
Funny moments of silent bluff.
cons: Hard for players who cannot keep a straight face.
Bluffs can be invisible.

pairs.tendency: Players find a secret rule in silence, learning only from which moves are refused.
pros: A strange, puzzling mood.
Finding the rule feels big.
cons: Being refused without words can feel cold.
Some players never find it.

pairs.tendency: One player knows the answer, nobody may speak, and hints come only as moves or pictures.
pros: Every hint is read closely.
Quiet tension.
cons: Hints can be misread.
The player who knows can feel frustrated.

pairs.tendency: Players act in a model of a real system without speaking, as people often do in real life.
pros: Players see effects without being told.
A quiet way to watch a system.
cons: Players cannot coordinate.
Lessons can be missed without talk.

pairs.tendency: Each role acts without speaking, showing its side only through choices.
pros: Roles are shown, not argued.
Players watch what each role does.
cons: Roles cannot explain themselves.
Misunderstandings can grow.

pairs.tendency: Players take from a shared resource without talking, so nobody can agree limits.
pros: Players see how silent taking adds up.
A clear lesson about shared things.
cons: The resource can run out fast.
Players may feel blamed.

pairs.tendency: Players act in silence, and the effects come later, so nobody can explain what they planned.
pros: Surprises when effects arrive.
Players think ahead.
cons: Hard to know who caused what.
Confusion can build.

pairs.tendency: A new rule is tried in silence, and players work out its effect only by watching.
pros: Players notice effects closely.
A fresh way to test a rule.
cons: Effects can be missed.
Players may disagree later about what happened.

pairs.tendency: Players play in silence, then talk it all through afterwards.
pros: The talk after feels full of discovery.
Players learn what others meant.
cons: Some moments are forgotten by the time of the talk.
Players may feel misread.

pairs.tendency: Players make lasting changes to the game without speaking, so each one is a silent decision.
pros: Each change feels serious.
The game keeps a quiet record.
cons: Nobody can object before a change is made.
Regret cannot be talked out.

pairs.tendency: Players make one silent move a day, with no messages between them.
pros: A slow, quiet game.
Something to think about each day.
cons: Players can forget the game.
Long waits with nothing said.

pairs.tendency: You roll to move, and some spaces let you change a rule, such as how far a roll takes you.
pros: The dice can lead to changing the dice.
Easy to start, with surprises later.
cons: Landing on rule spaces is down to luck.
Too many changes can make moving confusing.

pairs.tendency: Some cards in the shared row are new rules, and picking one puts it into play.
pros: Players choose which rules arrive.
Taking a rule someone wants is a quiet move.
cons: The row can fill with rules nobody understands.
Picking rules can slow the game.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the right to change a rule, so each change has a price.
pros: Changes feel valuable.
Players think hard about what a rule is worth.
cons: Rich players can rewrite the game.
Bidding over rules can take long.

pairs.tendency: You can keep adding rule changes on your turn, but a change that backfires costs you.
pros: Bold changes feel exciting.
Every change is a small gamble.
cons: One mistimed change can undo a turn.
Careful players may never change anything.

pairs.tendency: Holding an area gives you the power to change a rule, so the map decides who rewrites the game.
pros: Areas matter for more than points.
Players fight over the right to make rules.
cons: The leader can lock in their lead with rules.
The rules can drift towards one player.

pairs.tendency: One action space lets a worker change a rule, so players compete for it.
pros: Rule-making is one choice among many.
Players watch who takes the rule space.
cons: The same player can keep taking it.
New rules can upset everyone's plans.

pairs.tendency: Players can change what counts as a scoring pattern while they build.
pros: Patterns stay surprising.
Players adapt as they build.
cons: A change can ruin a nearly finished pattern.
Hard to plan ahead.

pairs.tendency: Some cards in your hand change rules, and you choose when to play them.
pros: Saving a rule change for the right moment feels clever.
Players plan around possible changes.
cons: Others may change the rule first.
Many changes are hard to track.

pairs.tendency: Winning a trick lets you change a rule, such as which suit is strongest.
pros: Each trick can reshape the next hand.
Familiar play with a twist.
cons: Players may lose track of the current rules.
Winners can change rules to keep winning.

pairs.tendency: Players make deals to support or block rule changes,.
pros: Lots of talking and persuading.
Players learn how agreements work.
cons: Deals can turn into long debates.
Quieter players may lose influence.

pairs.tendency: Completing a set lets you change a rule, so collecting brings power.
pros: Clear reasons to collect.
Each set can reshape the game.
cons: The first to collect can rewrite things in their favour.
Rules can pile up.

pairs.tendency: Some tiles carry new rules, so the board grows with its own laws.
pros: The map and the rules grow together.
Each tile is a decision about the game.
cons: Rules spread across the map can be hard to see.
Players may forget which rule applies where.

pairs.tendency: Players race to the end, but anyone can change the rules of the race on their turn.
pros: The race keeps shifting.
Clever changes can help a player catch up.
cons: Leaders can change rules to stay ahead.
The race can stall in debate.

pairs.tendency: Players score points and can change how points are scored,.
pros: Scoring stays surprising.
Players think about how rules shape winning.
cons: Scoring can become hard to follow.
Players may argue over each change.

pairs.tendency: Players knock each other out, and can change the rules that decide who is out.
pros: Tense and changeable.
Players fight with rules as well as moves.
cons: Being ruled out can feel unfair.
Players who are out wait a long time.

pairs.tendency: The group survives together and can change rules to make the game easier or harder.
pros: Players think about what the rules do.
Shared changes build teamwork.
cons: Easy rules can make the game too simple.
Arguments over changes can split the group.

pairs.tendency: Players work towards one goal and agree changes to the rules on the way.
pros: Rule-making becomes teamwork.
Everyone has a say.
cons: Agreeing can take a long time.
The goal can shift as rules change.

pairs.tendency: Each player secretly changes rules to help a hidden aim.
pros: Every change is a clue.
Spotting hidden reasons is fun.
cons: Changes can seem to come from nowhere.
The rules can get messy.

pairs.tendency: Changing a rule changes the story, such as a rule that lets the dead return.
pros: The story and the rules grow together.
Endings can surprise everyone.
cons: The story can lose its thread.
Some players want stable rules.

pairs.tendency: Players change the rules with no winner, just to see what the game becomes.
pros: Free and playful.
Players invent without pressure.
cons: It can feel aimless.
Hard to know when to stop.

pairs.tendency: Each player changes the rules towards what they want the game to be.
pros: Players shape the game around their aims.
Talking about aims comes naturally.
cons: Changes can clash.
Players may not agree on how it went.

pairs.tendency: Players change rules to avoid being the one who loses.
pros: Every change is a defence.
Clever changes can save you.
cons: Players may gang up on one person with rules.

cons: Overwhelming.
Stress.

pairs.tendency: Stakeholders have to decide faster as events speed up.
pros: Realistic.
Tense.
cons: Rushed.
Quiet roles lose.

pairs.tendency: Demand on the shared resource speeds up.
pros: Shows how depletion speeds up.
Tense.
cons: Collapse.
Harsh lesson.

pairs.tendency: Effects arrive faster as the game goes on.
pros: Clear arc.
Exciting.
cons: Overwhelming.
Hard to learn.

pairs.tendency: Rule tests speed up.
pros: Fast results.
Exciting.
cons: Rushed.
Shallow.

pairs.tendency: A debrief with less time for each person.
pros: Quick.
Focused.
cons: Rushed.
Shallow.

pairs.tendency: Permanent changes come faster and faster.
pros: Dramatic.
Exciting.
cons: Regret.
Chaotic.

pairs.tendency: The speeding up is part of the point the rules make.
pros: Shows acceleration in the world.
Clear message.
cons: Stressful.
Rushed.

pairs.tendency: Real stakes, decided faster and faster.
pros: Intense.
Exciting.
cons: Stressful.
Rushed.

pairs.tendency: Value trade-offs come faster as play speeds up.
pros: Shows how speed changes priorities.
Tense.
cons: Rushed.
Values blur.

pairs.tendency: A future rehearsed at a quickening pace.
pros: Realistic.
Exciting.
cons: Rushed.
Stress.

pairs.tendency: Some moments go round the table in order and others are chosen by everyone at once, as in Werewolf's talk and vote.
pros: Each phase has its own rhythm.
Order where it helps, surprise where it counts.
cons: Players have to learn when each applies.
The switch can confuse.

pairs.tendency: The game moves between ordered turns and free-for-all moments.
pros: Calm phases and frantic ones.
Variety of pace.
cons: Hard to explain.
Players miss the change.

pairs.tendency: Turns go in order, each with a clock.
pros: Keeps every turn moving.
Fair to all.
cons: Pressure on slow players.
The clock can feel like a nag.

pairs.tendency: Turns go in order, but each one is a day or a week apart.
pros: Time to think.
Fits busy lives.
cons: Very slow.
Players forget the game.

pairs.tendency: Turns go in order, slowed down on purpose.
pros: Calm.
Thoughtful.
cons: Slow.
Restless players.

pairs.tendency: Turns go in order but get faster as the game goes on.
pros: Builds excitement.
Clear arc.
cons: Late turns are rushed.
Stress at the end.

pairs.tendency: Some moments everyone reveals together; others are open to whoever is quickest.
pros: Varied pace.
Lively.
cons: Confusing.
Hard to explain.

pairs.tendency: Everyone chooses at once before the clock runs out.
pros: Fast.
Fair.
cons: Rushed choices.
Stress.

pairs.tendency: Everyone sends a choice by a set day, and all are revealed together.
pros: Fair rounds over time.
Fits busy lives.
cons: Slow.
Players drift away.

pairs.tendency: Everyone chooses at once, after a long pause to think.
pros: Thoughtful.
Calm reveal.
cons: Slow.
Little energy.

pairs.tendency: Everyone chooses at once, with less time each round.
pros: Rising tension.
Exciting reveals.
cons: Rushed.
Mistakes.

pairs.tendency: Free play within a timed round: act as often as you like until the time is up.
pros: Frantic and bounded.
Clear end to each round.
cons: Chaotic.
Stress.

pairs.tendency: Players act whenever they like over days or weeks.
pros: Flexible.
Fits busy lives.
cons: Hard to follow.
Uneven play.

pairs.tendency: No turns, but everyone moves slowly and deliberately, as in The Mind.
pros: Tense calm.
Deep focus.
cons: Slow.
Hard to start.

pairs.tendency: Free play that speeds up as the game goes on.
pros: Exciting.
Thrilling end.
cons: Chaotic.
Overwhelming.

pairs.tendency: Each turn has a real deadline, such as a move by tomorrow.
pros: Keeps the game alive.
Fair.
cons: Players miss deadlines.
Pressure over days.

pairs.tendency: Each turn has a long, generous clock that slows the game down.
pros: Calm.
Time to think.
cons: Slow.
Little pressure.

pairs.tendency: The clock for each turn gets shorter as the game goes on.
pros: Rising tension.
Clear arc.
cons: Stress.
Rushed end.

pairs.tendency: A game spread over real days and slowed further on purpose.
pros: Deep reflection.
Fits slow living.
cons: Very slow.
Hard to keep going.

pairs.tendency: A game over real days in which moves come more often as it goes on.
pros: Builds over weeks.
Exciting end.
cons: Hard to keep up.
Drop-outs.

pairs.tendency: The game starts slow and calm, then speeds up.
pros: Clear arc from calm to rush.
Strong finish.
cons: Hard to judge the change.
Some prefer one pace.

pairs.tendency: Each throw of the dice takes your piece along the path, and the space you land on says which card you may ask another player for.
pros: The dice give every question a reason.
Players learn what a landing space is worth.
cons: A low throw leaves you with nothing to ask for.
The questions get lost between the moves.

pairs.tendency: Cards pass round the table one at a time, so when you ask a player for a card you also see what they kept from the pass.
pros: Every pick shows what a player wants.
You can ask for what you saw go by.
cons: The cards you pass tell others what to ask you for.
Players need long memories.

pairs.tendency: Before you ask for a card you pay for the right to ask, and the player who offers most gets to go first.
pros: Asking has a price.
Players see how much a card is worth to someone.
cons: A high offer shows what you hold.
Someone can pay a lot and still hear no.

pairs.tendency: You keep asking for cards while the answers are yes, and the first no ends your turn and may cost you what you gathered.
pros: A run of yeses feels like a streak.
Each ask is a small bet on one player's hand.
cons: One no can lose the whole turn.
Players may stop early and ask very little.

pairs.tendency: Each region of the map is held by whoever collects the most cards of its kind, so you ask other players for the cards that win a region.
pros: Cards have a clear use on the map.
Players aim their questions at their rivals.
cons: A question shows which region you are after.
A player holding many cards is asked all the time.

pairs.tendency: You send a worker to a spot on the board, and the spot lets you ask one player for a card.
pros: Spots on the board decide who gets to ask.
Workers and cards both have a job.
cons: A taken spot means no asking this turn.
Players wait while others work out their questions.

pairs.tendency: You need certain colours or shapes in a row, so you ask for the card that fills the gap in your pattern.
pros: Each ask has a plain aim.
Others can see what you are building.
cons: A watching player can hold back the card you need.
A pattern with many gaps needs many asks.

pairs.tendency: Your hand is both what you play and what others ask about, so each card you keep or lay down changes what you can answer.
pros: You choose what to keep from view.
Cards in hand are worth something to others.
cons: A full hand is asked about more often.
Hiding a card can mean giving up a play.

pairs.tendency: When you ask for a card, you also learn which suits others hold, and that helps when the tricks start.
pros: Questions work as scouting.
Players plan their tricks with more knowledge.
cons: Asking tells others which suit you lack.
The scouting adds time before the tricks.

pairs.tendency: Before you ask, you can offer something back, such as a card of yours or a promise for later.
pros: Players trade instead of only asking.
Deals build up between friends.
cons: A player can agree and then break the deal.
Talking slows the turn.

pairs.tendency: You want four of a kind, so you ask for the one you lack, and a yes brings you a step closer.
pros: Every ask points at one missing card.
Sets are easy to count.
cons: Everyone sees which sets you are chasing.
A player with a nearly full set is asked about at once.

pairs.tendency: You lay tiles to build a shared map, and a tile you need that you do not have is something to ask another player for.
pros: Tiles move between players.
The map grows from trades as well as draws.
cons: Others can tell from the request where you plan to build.
A tile may be handed over just when you needed it too.

pairs.tendency: One player calls a card and the next player answers by handing it over or saying no. The answer becomes the next call.
pros: A game of questions runs in a chain.
Each answer gives the next player a clue.
cons: The chain can drift away from the cards.
Players who answer slowly stop the chain.

pairs.tendency: Nobody may talk, so you ask by pointing at a player and holding up a card shape or a rank with your fingers.
pros: A game of gestures replaces speech.
Players have to watch faces and hands.
cons: A question can be misread.
Quiet tables can feel slow.

pairs.tendency: On your turn you can alter the rule for asking, such as who you may ask or how many cards one yes can win.
pros: The game changes shape from round to round.
Players can write rules that help their own hand.
cons: Old plans stop working.
Arguments start about which rule is on the table.

pairs.tendency: You speak as a character, so every ask is in their voice, and the other player answers as theirs.
pros: Asking turns into a short scene.
A character can ask in ways a player would not.
cons: The acting takes more time than the asking.
Shy players may go quiet.

pairs.tendency: Before you may ask for a card you have to pass a small test of the hands, such as flicking a coin into a cup.
pros: Hands and memory both get used.
Players watch each other's tries.
cons: A missed flick means no asking.
The game stops while a try goes on.

pairs.tendency: Players draw the map as they go, and a card you ask for may add a road or a river to the drawing.
pros: Cards and drawing build the same picture.
Everyone owns a part of the map.
cons: Asking for a card can show where you will draw next.
The drawing slows the turns.

pairs.tendency: The bank holds the cards, and the others place their bets before asking, so a yes pays at fixed odds.
pros: Odds are known before anyone asks.
Players can compare the price of each ask.
cons: The bank sees many bets before it answers.
A player who holds the bank passes it on slowly.

pairs.tendency: Players put coins on the table before the dice land, then the throw says who may ask whom for a card.
pros: A throw makes the asking order.
Bets add a stake to each ask.
cons: A lost bet takes away a turn of asking.
A big pot can end with a short round.

pairs.tendency: You put chips in while you think your hidden cards can win, and your questions tell others which cards you are chasing.
pros: Each question works like a bet.
Chips show how sure each player feels.
cons: A question can give your hand away before you bet.
Players who drop out stop asking.

pairs.tendency: Before play you pick the side you will use, and your questions then ask for the cards that suit your side.
pros: Each player asks for different cards.
Sides keep their own style.
cons: Questions show which side a player picked.
A side that needs rare cards can wait a long time.

pairs.tendency: You say before play what you will win, and then you ask the others for the cards that make your promise true.
pros: The aim is spoken aloud at the start.
Every ask from the first turn serves the promise.
cons: Players can ask to stop you.
A promise that is too big can fail early.

pairs.tendency: When you capture a piece it joins your side, and you may ask for a card that helps you hold it.
pros: A catch brings more than one gain.
Cards can protect the new piece.
cons: A player who is behind can hit back quickly.
Asking for the same card twice can look repetitive.

pairs.tendency: A caught player waits in jail, and a teammate who reaches the jail may ask for a card that opens it.
pros: Teammates have a reason to go back for friends.
Cards become keys.
cons: A player in jail can only watch.
Rescuers who ask for the wrong card get caught themselves.

pairs.tendency: You trap pieces by placing yours on both sides, and a card you win by asking can add one more stone to the ring.
pros: A won card counts as one more stone.
Players plan a ring before they ask.
cons: Your question gives away which piece you are circling.
The player being circled can ask for the card that breaks the ring.

pairs.tendency: Players who are behind may ask twice, or ask for more than one card at a time.
pros: A lead can be cut down in a turn or two.
The last player still has something to do.
cons: The leader waits while others catch up.
The player in front may ask very little.

pairs.tendency: The cards turn over by luck, and asking is only a way to hear the result, so no question changes what you get.
pros: The game moves fast.
Anyone can win, whatever they know.
cons: Asking does not change the outcome.
Players stop thinking about their questions.

pairs.tendency: The player who is It chases the rest, and when a runner is touched they have to hand over a card if It asks for one.
pros: A touch makes a trade.
Runners keep moving with cards in their hands.
cons: Running with cards is awkward.
A player who is tagged often loses most of their hand.

pairs.tendency: You pick which player to ask, and the player you pick may have no card at all.
pros: The choice of who to ask is a decision of its own.
Players watch who has been asked before.
cons: A player who is asked often can feel picked on.
Three players or more make the choice slow.

pairs.tendency: You need an unbroken chain across the board, and you ask for the card that adds the next stone to it.
pros: Cards move the chain forward.
The other side tries to cut it.
cons: The other side learns from your question where the chain is going.
One cut can undo many turns.

pairs.tendency: Each card beats one other and loses to a third, so a question for a card also tells the other player which card to beat it with.
pros: No card wins every time.
Players read each other's habits.
cons: A question gives away your next card.
A player who never asks for the same card is hard to read.

pairs.tendency: You show a pair or a run you hold for points, and your question may be a way to finish a pair you want to declare.
pros: A declared pair earns points while the game goes on.
A question can set up a pair to show.
cons: Declared cards tell the table what you still hold.
A pair you have shown is easy to ask about.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a power nobody else has, such as asking two players at once or taking a card without being asked.
pros: Players play the same game in different ways.
A power changes who is asked.
cons: The table has to remember several powers.
A power that is hard to answer ends turns quickly.

pairs.tendency: Part-way through, you may offer to double what the game is worth, and the other player answers with a yes or a drop-out.
pros: Asking and doubling both put pressure on a rival.
A leader can end the game early.
cons: A drop-out loses the points already at stake.
A player who doubles shows they are sure.

pairs.tendency: If you can capture, you have to, and a question for a card may be the only way to avoid a capture that is waiting for you.
pros: A rival can force your move.
Asking becomes a way to escape.
cons: A forced capture can ruin a plan.
Cards may be asked for in a rush.

pairs.tendency: Each card you win by asking makes your character more able, so your later questions are backed by a stronger character.
pros: Early asks pay off later.
Players can see their characters change.
cons: A player ahead gets further ahead.
A late joiner has little to ask with.

pairs.tendency: Each player recites the list so far and adds one item, and the item added can be the name of the card they are asking for.
pros: Memory is part of the asking.
The list grows with every turn.
cons: Players forget the list.
Late turns take a long time.

pairs.tendency: The more experienced player starts with fewer cards or fewer asks, so a weaker player has a real chance of a yes.
pros: Players of different ages can sit down together.
The weaker player gets more chances to ask.
cons: The more experienced player may feel held back.
Both players wait longer for the first yes.

pairs.tendency: Someone hides a card or a token, and the hunters ask others questions to narrow down where it went.
pros: Questions help the search.
The hunt has a clear end.
cons: A hider can say no for a long time.
Hunters repeat the same questions.

pairs.tendency: Your piece hops over another and lands behind it, and the hop lets you ask the player you jumped for a card.
pros: A hop has a second reward.
Cards and pieces both move.
cons: The player who was jumped gives up a card and a place.
A long run of hops can empty a hand.

pairs.tendency: You roll your dice, keep the ones you like, and roll the rest again, and the numbers you keep tell you which card to ask for.
pros: The dice give each ask a number to chase.
Players keep some control over the roll.
cons: Others see what you kept.
After three rolls you are stuck with your result.

pairs.tendency: If your piece lands where another stands, theirs goes back to the start, and you may ask for a card from the player you sent back.
pros: A landing earns a card.
The sent-back player has a reason to catch up.
cons: A piece can lose many moves in one turn.
Safe spaces stop the asking.

pairs.tendency: A mill of three pieces lets you take one from the other side, and the player who loses a piece may be asked for a card as well.
pros: A row has two rewards.
Players break each other's rows.
cons: A player with one row may take a second.
Losing a piece and a card in one turn hurts.

pairs.tendency: Cards carry letters, and you ask for the letter that completes a word you are building.
pros: Letters become something to trade.
A dictionary ends any argument.
cons: Others can guess your word from your question.
A rare letter may never come.

pairs.tendency: You add a tile only if its number matches an open end, and if you do not have one, you may ask another player for it.
pros: A missing tile can be replaced by a question.
Open ends tell everyone what is needed.
cons: A turn can pass with no match.
A request for a tile tells everyone which ends are blocked for you.

pairs.tendency: You lay a finished set face up, and from then on you may ask for cards that match what is already on the table.
pros: The table grows with each laid set.
Other players can add to it.
cons: A laid set shows your plans.
Cards in hand get fewer and easier to guess.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a special power that works once, and you can use it to ask a question that has to be answered.
pros: A power can be saved for the right question.
Choosing the moment is a decision.
cons: A used power cannot come back.
A power held too long may never be used.

pairs.tendency: You offer a question, and the other player can turn it down or choose between two questions you offer.
pros: Both players shape each ask.
Offers show what a player is willing to ask.
cons: A turn-down wastes the ask.
Two players can get stuck going back and forth.

pairs.tendency: A question travels from player to player by whisper, and by the time it arrives the card asked for may have changed.
pros: Questions change on the way.
Nobody can check a message until it is answered.
cons: A card may be handed over by mistake.
Long chains of players make the message less clear.

pairs.tendency: Before play begins you choose cards to hand over, and later you ask for cards you remember passing.
pros: You know a little about what you gave.
Early passing sets the first asks.
cons: You cannot see what you will get when you pass.
Players ask for cards they handed away.

pairs.tendency: One player sets out the first hands, and the other player picks which side to take, so the setter makes both sides about the same.
pros: The start is hard to bend in your favour.
Both sides get a fair chance to ask.
cons: The setter spends a long time planning.
The picker may need to guess which side holds the cards they want.

pairs.tendency: A piece that reaches the far end turns into a piece with more moves, and you may ask for a card to help it get there.
pros: A long walk ends with a prize.
Cards can help the piece along.
cons: A piece far from the end gets no help.
Players guard the last row.

pairs.tendency: Your team runs in legs, and each runner hands over a card as well as a flag to the next.
pros: Teammates share cards through the race.
The hand-over is a moment to ask.
cons: A dropped flag costs the team time.
One slow runner holds everyone back.

pairs.tendency: Stones that make a certain shape cannot be taken, and you ask for the card that finishes that shape.
pros: A goal to build towards.
Safe stones stay put.
cons: The other side tries to surround you.
A shape half done is easy to see.

pairs.tendency: The prizes are named cards, so you ask for the one named card that wins most, and a yes can end the round.
pros: One card can carry the whole round.
Everyone knows which cards matter.
cons: The holder of a named card is asked at every turn.
Holding that card back can turn the round.

pairs.tendency: Some cards sit face up in the middle, and each question you ask is about what your hand adds to them.
pros: Players share a base to build on.
Asking is cheaper because you can see part of the answer.
cons: A shared card helps your rivals as much as you.
Your hand is easy to guess from the middle.

pairs.tendency: Everyone puts a counter in the middle, and a yes to your question can win you the pot.
pros: The prize grows if no one wins.
Players ask for the card that takes it.
cons: A big pot makes the next ask matter more.
A player who is dry has nothing to add.

pairs.tendency: You scoop seeds from a pit and drop them round, and where the last one lands says which player you may ask for a card.
pros: The seeds decide who gets asked.
Players count ahead before they scoop.
cons: A long scoop can land you on a useless pit.
Counting takes time.

pairs.tendency: An extra hand is dealt face down, and the player who takes it can later ask others about the cards they swapped out.
pros: A mystery hand sits on the table.
One player gets an early advantage.
cons: Swapped cards show what a player wanted.
The spare hand may hold fewer useful cards than the first.

pairs.tendency: Some spaces on the track hold a rule, and landing on one lets you ask for a card or sends you back a turn.
pros: The track has places to look forward to.
Landing sets the next ask.
cons: A penalty square can cost a turn.
A safe square keeps a player in front for long.

pairs.tendency: Each card has a price, and a card you ask for still costs you when you play it.
pros: Cards are worth different amounts.
Players think about what they can afford.
cons: A costly card may sit in hand for many turns.
Asking for a dear card can drain you.

pairs.tendency: You share a set amount between several places, and your questions pick up cards that help in the place where you are short.
pros: Spare cards fix gaps.
The other player is splitting too.
cons: The place you have left bare is the one you ask about.
Too many places leave each one thin.

pairs.tendency: Everyone keeps moving until the signal, then freezes, and whoever is slowest has to hand over a card when asked.
pros: Movement and asking mix.
The signal gives a clear stop.
cons: Slow players give up cards.
Quick players can ask repeatedly.

pairs.tendency: You put cards back and take new ones to build a hand, and you may ask a player for a swap as well as a draw.
pros: Hands improve through trades.
Players have more than one way to get a card.
cons: A swap needs the other player to agree.
A swap shows which cards you gave up.

pairs.tendency: Every discard goes on one pile, and on your turn you may pick it up or ask a player for a card instead.
pros: A pile gives a second choice.
The whole table sees what was thrown.
cons: A big pile makes taking it a big decision.
A pile can be taken just when it hurts another player.

pairs.tendency: One suit is named trump and beats the rest, so you ask for trump cards first and others ask you for the same.
pros: The named suit is the one to chase.
A low trump can still win.
cons: Each request for trump hints at how many you hold.
Trump cards are hard to get.

pairs.tendency: You play two boards at once, so a card you win on one board can be asked for again on the other.
pros: One question can serve two games.
Players attack and defend in the same turn.
cons: Players lose track of which board is which.
Turns take twice as long.

pairs.tendency: A wild card can stand for any card, so players ask for it first and others pretend not to have it.
pros: One card can finish many sets.
Everyone wants the same card.
cons: A player with a wild card is asked about it each turn.
A wild card can end a round suddenly.

pairs.tendency: The edges of the board are joined, so a piece that runs off one side comes back on the other and may land beside a player you want to ask.
pros: Distance means less.
A rival can appear from behind.
cons: Chasing is harder to plan.
Players lose track of where the pieces are.

pairs.tendency: One player knows a secret and the others ask yes or no questions, and a question about a card gets only a yes or a no.
pros: Each answer cuts the list of choices.
A short answer is quick to give.
cons: A question that wastes an answer is hard to take back.
The player with the secret does most of the answering.

pairs.tendency: The first to reach the end wins, so each card you ask for needs to help you move faster.
pros: The goal is plain.
Each card is wanted for how far it moves you.
cons: Asking slows the player who asks.
A leader can look out of reach.

pairs.tendency: Whoever has the highest score wins, so every question is about which cards add the most to your total.
pros: Players count points as they ask.
A late card can change the score.
cons: Asking tells others what you value.
Counting can fill the end of the game.

pairs.tendency: Players are knocked out one by one, and the cards you ask for decide who goes next.
pros: A question can decide who goes out.
The table gets smaller.
cons: Players who are out have to watch.
A player who is asked too often can drop out early.

pairs.tendency: Everyone wins or loses together, so you ask your teammates for the cards the whole table needs.
pros: Asking is a way of helping.
