pairs.tendency: The group uses the other side's duty to pull its pieces toward the shared goal. One player's bait can help the group and block another player's path.
pros: The group can use the duty as a tool.
Players plan baits together.
cons: One player's bait can spoil another's path.
Talking it through takes time.

pairs.tendency: Others watch who you capture and guess what you want. A forced capture gives them a clue, and it can also drag you away from your goal.
pros: Forced moves give away hints.
Players hide their goal behind a forced move.
cons: A duty can drag you away from your goal.
Reading others turns into guessing.

pairs.tendency: Each capture the rules force becomes an event in the story. The story turns where players did not choose to take it.
pros: The rules write part of the story.
Players tell what each capture meant.
cons: The ending may come from the duty and not the players' wish.
The story is hard to steer.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, but the duty still moves pieces about. At the end players look at the board and talk about what the forced captures left behind.
pros: The board shows a record of duties.
Players talk about what the rule did.
cons: Players cannot aim at a result.
The game may stop with no clear end.

pairs.tendency: One player aims to lose no piece, so the duty is what they avoid. Another aims to capture as many as possible, so the duty is their tool.
pros: Goals show up in how a player handles the duty.
Players compare different aims.
cons: A forced capture can break a goal someone chose.
Results are hard to compare.

pairs.tendency: The game goes on until one player loses, and a forced capture can push the last piece towards one player. Everyone else is safe once that player is chosen.
pros: Players use the duty to push one player towards losing.
Everyone else is safe once the loser is known.
cons: The player with a piece in reach is always at risk.
Players may gang up on one person.

pairs.tendency: Forced captures use pieces up, so a game that has to continue gets closer to its end with each capture. Players pace the captures to keep pieces on the board.
pros: Careful play keeps pieces on the board longer.
Captures can be spread out.
cons: Captures wear down the pieces.
An end appears even though nobody wants one.

pairs.tendency: The duty keeps taking pieces whatever the players want, and no one can stop it. The game shows how a rule can act without any reward behind it.
pros: Players meet a rule that acts whatever they want.
The result shows what the rule does to wishes.
cons: Captures happen with nothing to gain.
Players may walk away.

pairs.tendency: The layout shows cards, and when you can take one you have to, even a card you would rather keep. Playing alone, you meet the same duty at every turn.
pros: The duty is the same every time.
The duty makes the game quick to learn.
cons: A forced take can block the way to clearing the table.
A stuck position comes quicker.

pairs.tendency: In a series of short games, a forced capture shortens each game. A player who learns a trap in the first game uses it in the second.
pros: Players learn traps between games.
Short games run fast.
cons: One trap can win the series.
An early loss can decide the series.

pairs.tendency: A capture adds points to the one who takes it, and the fewest points win. So the duty to capture becomes a penalty, and players bait each other into taking pieces.
pros: Players bait each other into captures.
The duty turns into a penalty.
cons: A player who cannot avoid capturing collects points.
Plays look backwards to newcomers.

pairs.tendency: A capture you are forced to take may push your count past the target. Players track their numbers and bait each other towards the wrong total.
pros: Players track their counts.
Baits are aimed at counts.
cons: A forced move can break an exact finish.
Scores need close watching.

pairs.tendency: A player who wants to give pieces away offers them, and the other side has to take every one. The one who is meant to lose pieces forces the other to take them.
pros: The giver forces the other to take.
Moves run the opposite way from most games.
cons: The taker cannot refuse.
It takes a while to get used to.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a board and the duty applies on their own board, so players rarely force each other. They play side by side with their own captures.
pros: Players work at their own pace.
A forced capture only touches its owner.
cons: There is little to bait.
Players seldom look at the other boards.

pairs.tendency: Players hit and steal on purpose, and the duty lets an attacker choose a bait that the other has to capture into a trap. Attacks are plain to see.
pros: Everyone sees who attacked whom.
Players target one another.
cons: The duty gives the attacker control.
Targeted players can feel picked on.

pairs.tendency: Players change the board, not each other, and a piece left in reach changes what the next player has to do. The board pushes players quietly.
pros: Players are steered without being attacked.
Effects show up without a clash.
cons: A player can be forced by a trap on the board that they did not see.
It is hard to say who set it.

pairs.tendency: The whole team plans around a fixed rule, and the duty can draw the game's pieces where the team wants them. A team can trade a piece for a path.
pros: The team shares plans around the duty.
The team can trade a piece for a path.
cons: A forced capture can hit the team's own piece.
One mistake affects everybody.

pairs.tendency: The group works together, and one player slips in a private gain. A forced capture can serve the team and also give that player a bonus.
pros: The duty can serve the team and one player.
Team talk mixes with private plans.
cons: A forced capture can favour one player.
Trust gets shaky.

pairs.tendency: One teammate leaves a piece in reach so the other team has to capture and lose their place, and the second teammate captures back. Teams plan these traps together.
pros: Teammates set up traps together.
Teams talk plans through.
cons: A bait piece is lost for the team.
Teammates wait on each other.

pairs.tendency: The traitor leaves a piece in reach on purpose, and the duty makes an innocent player capture it. The capture looks like an ordinary move.
pros: The traitor uses the duty as cover.
A forced move gives an excuse.
cons: Others cannot tell a forced capture from a plot.
Suspicion rises.

pairs.tendency: A letter names a move, and if it leaves a piece in reach the reply has to capture. The writer knows part of what will come back.
pros: Replies can be guessed.
Each move has a wait attached.
cons: A forced reply can waste a long wait.
A long game can go stale.

pairs.tendency: The absent player's pieces take captures by rule, so the duty acts for someone who is not at the table. Players can lay bait for a side that never changes its mind.
pros: The absent side moves by rule.
Players can predict it.
cons: Players can bait the absent side.
The absent side cannot change its mind.

pairs.tendency: The game master runs the other side, and the duty tells the master which monsters take captures even when the master would rather hold back. Players can lead the master's pieces about.
pros: The master has a fixed rule to follow.
Players can lead the master's pieces.
cons: The master has less choice.
The master may bend the rule.

pairs.tendency: Anyone passing can join, and a new player has to take a capture if one is open, so a stranger's first move can be set. Chalk lines on the ground show where the pieces sit.
pros: Strangers learn the duty at once.
The game is quick to explain.
cons: A passer-by may be caught by the duty.
The rule needs saying again for each newcomer.

pairs.tendency: The lone player has to capture whenever possible, while the others work together to leave bait. The group can steer the lone player from move to move.
pros: The group can plan around the duty.
The lone player's moves can be read.
cons: The lone player can be steered.
The group has to talk it over.

pairs.tendency: Playing alone against the pack, you take a capture when one is open, so the pack's order sets many of your moves.
pros: The rule decides some moves for you.
The game is easy to run alone.
cons: Play can turn into habit.
Few real choices are left.

pairs.tendency: Dice bring pieces into reach and the duty settles the rest, so players do little but watch.
pros: There is little to plan.
Turns are quick.
cons: A forced turn plays itself.
Skill barely shows.

pairs.tendency: A reroll or a card can lift the duty when a throw brings a capture you did not want. Players keep a card back for that moment.
pros: A card can lift the duty.
Players keep cards for this moment.
cons: A reroll may bring another capture.
Saved cards may go unused.

pairs.tendency: Players plan baits and traps, while a small amount of luck shifts what is in reach. A trap built over several turns can fail on one draw.
pros: Planning shows in the result.
Luck shifts a trap now and then.
cons: A planned trap can fail on a single draw.
Luck can undo a long plan.

pairs.tendency: With no dice, every forced capture can be seen in advance. Players count the forced moves many turns ahead and build traps far in front.
pros: Traps can be built far ahead.
Mistakes show plainly.
cons: One slip gives the other side a forced chain.
Players think for a long time each turn.

pairs.tendency: A throw is read as a message, and if the sign points at a piece the reader has to capture it, whatever the reader thinks.
pros: The throw gives a duty.
Players discuss the sign.
cons: A sign can force a capture nobody wanted.
Players may disagree on the reading.

pairs.tendency: Players sense when the others are about to act. With the duty in place, they can sense who will capture and when, and move at the same moment.
pros: Players match their timing.
The duty makes timing readable.
cons: A forced capture can break the shared timing.
It is hard to explain what is being sensed.

pairs.tendency: A roll on the table says a monster appears in reach, and the duty makes you fight it. The dice write the fight and the rule writes what you do next.
pros: The dice write the fight.
The story takes sharp turns.
cons: The player is forced into fights.
Forced fights start to repeat.

pairs.tendency: Everything is open, so both players see each forced capture coming. A bait is a plain offer that the other side cannot refuse.
pros: Traps are in plain sight.
Players plan long chains.
cons: Nothing hides a trap.
Long plans slow the game.

pairs.tendency: Whether a player can capture depends on the cards they hold, so a player may say they have no capture when they do. Others ask to see.
pros: Players watch each other's claims.
A player can bluff about the duty.
cons: A false claim can be caught on a check.
Players dispute what someone held.

pairs.tendency: A secret role hides who gains from a forced capture. When a player takes a piece, others wonder if they had to or wanted to.
pros: The duty gives cover to a role.
Players guess roles from captures.
cons: A forced capture may give a role away.
Every capture gets questioned.

pairs.tendency: What a player captures is a clue. A forced capture tells the others what that player could take, and so what they hold.
pros: A capture gives a clue.
Players list what each person could have taken.
cons: A forced capture is a clear sign.
Wrong guesses pile up.

pairs.tendency: A player says "I have no capture" when they do, and the others ask to check. The duty gives the lie something to hang on.
pros: The duty gives a bluff something to cover.
Players test each other's claims.
cons: A caught bluff costs a piece.
Each check holds up play.

pairs.tendency: Newcomers learn that a capture has to be taken when they skip one and are told no. The knowing player holds the secret and watches the mistake.
pros: The duty teaches itself.
Newcomers learn by being told no.
cons: A newcomer may miss it again.
The knowing player holds the power.

pairs.tendency: The one who knows sees that a capture is open but can only hint. The others have to read the hint and guess which capture is meant.
pros: Hints can point to a capture.
The others guess.
cons: A hint can mislead.
The knower cannot stop a wrong move.

pairs.tendency: Turning an area over can show an enemy within reach, and the duty makes you capture it at once. Exploring has a price you only see when you pay it.
pros: Exploring has a price.
Each new tile is a gamble.
cons: A reveal can force a capture you did not want.
Careful players stall.

pairs.tendency: One hand lies face up, so everyone can see which captures it forces. The player who controls that hand has to take them, and the others plan around it.
pros: The open hand shows the duties.
Players plan around it.
cons: The player who runs the open hand has no choice.
The secret hands stay secret.

pairs.tendency: Nobody knows the exact scores, so a forced capture can shift the count without anyone seeing how far. Players guess who is ahead from what was taken.
pros: Captures hide inside the score.
Players guess who is ahead.
cons: A forced capture shifts the count unseen.
Nobody knows the true standing.

pairs.tendency: One player acts at a time, and each turn starts by looking for a capture. The next player waits to see if the duty has set a move for them.
pros: The order is clear.
The duty is easy to see.
cons: Players wait on each other.
With many players the wait is long.

pairs.tendency: All players choose in secret and reveal together. Two of them may be forced to capture the same piece at the same moment.
pros: Many captures come out in one reveal.
Players check for clashes.
cons: Two players can be forced onto one piece.
The result is hard to sort out.

pairs.tendency: Anyone may act at any moment, and the first to spot a capture has to take it before another player does.
pros: Quick eyes get rewarded.
Players keep their eyes on the board.
cons: A faster player can take the capture first.
Constant watching is tiring.

pairs.tendency: A clock runs while the duty tells you what to do. Sometimes you are forced to capture before you have had time to think.
pros: The clock and the duty narrow the choices.
Turns stay quick.
cons: A forced move can be made in a rush.
Mistakes come from hurry.

pairs.tendency: One move a day, so a piece left in reach overnight makes tomorrow's reply known. The other side can see the forced move a day ahead.
pros: The reply is known a day early.
A bait can be set slowly.
cons: Waiting for a forced move is slow.
Days pass between moves.

pairs.tendency: A pause before every move gives the player time to see the capture they will be forced to take. The slow pace makes the duty feel heavy.
pros: There is time to see the duty.
The pace is calm.
cons: A pause before a forced move can feel long.
The game runs slowly.

pairs.tendency: As the game speeds up, forced captures follow one another faster. A chain that took a minute in the first round takes seconds in the last.
pros: Chains speed up.
Players think in short bursts.
cons: There is less time to avoid a capture.
The end comes in a rush.

pairs.tendency: A capture can earn another go, so a forced capture can also start a run of moves. A lucky player can capture again and again.
pros: Runs of captures are possible.
A bait can pay off many times over.
cons: One player can run away with a lead.
Others wait through a long run.

pairs.tendency: In the first stage you set up your pieces and in the second the duty applies. The set-up decides which captures come, and a flaw in it shows only later.
pros: Set-up decides the later captures.
Players plan for the second stage.
cons: A flaw in the set-up shows only later.
It is hard to fix a set-up once the stage ends.

pairs.tendency: The board works like a village, and a forced capture is like a rule that applies to everyone whatever they want, such as a fine for a late payment. Players see how a fixed rule moves the whole system.
pros: Players see how a fixed rule acts.
Effects follow the rule.
cons: A rule can hit people who did not choose.
Real life is not so fixed.

pairs.tendency: Each player is a group, and the duty falls on some groups more than others, such as a council that has to act on a complaint. The players explain what their group had to do.
pros: Roles feel the duty differently.
Players explain their group's position.
cons: Some groups have less choice.
Groups quarrel with each other.

pairs.tendency: Everyone draws from one stock, and a capture takes from the stock. Because the capture is forced, a player cannot leave the stock alone.
pros: The duty drains the stock.
Players watch the stock.
cons: A forced take leaves less for all.
Players blame each other.

pairs.tendency: The effect of a capture shows a few rounds later, but the duty to take it is at once. A player is forced today into trouble that arrives later.
pros: Players see the result late.
Early choices matter.
cons: A forced capture now can cause trouble later.
It is hard to trace what caused what.

pairs.tendency: The players agree to try the duty as a new rule, play on and see what it changes. A few rounds show how pieces move when every capture is forced.
pros: The rule can be tested safely.
It is quick to compare with a game without the duty.
cons: The rule may need to be taken out again.
A short test may mislead.

pairs.tendency: After the game everyone talks about which captures were forced and which were chosen. The table goes back over the board move by move.
pros: The talk covers each forced capture.
Players learn how the rule worked.
cons: The talk can run long.
Memory of each move fades.

pairs.tendency: A captured piece is torn up or a sticker goes on the board, and because the capture is forced the board changes whether you want it or not.
pros: The board keeps a record.
Each capture stays.
cons: The duty cannot be undone.
The board runs out of room.

pairs.tendency: A game where captures are compulsory says something about pressure to act. The argument is the rule itself, and players feel it as they follow it.
pros: The rule makes a point.
Players feel the point in play.
cons: The argument may be missed.
Players may disagree about what it says.

pairs.tendency: Real money rides on the game, so the duty can cost a player real coins when a capture is forced. A friend baits you into losing a few rupees and you cannot refuse.
pros: The duty has a real cost.
Players think harder about baits.
cons: A forced move can cost real money.
Friends may fall out.

pairs.tendency: Points stand for health or kindness, and the duty takes points from someone even when the player would rather spare them. The game shows what happens when a number stands in for a value.
pros: Players see a value turned into a count.
Players see the duty cost points.
cons: A forced capture can take a value someone cared about.
Players chase the number.

pairs.tendency: Players practise a way of living where one duty applies to everyone, and a forced capture shows how that feels in practice. They try it for an evening before anyone tries it for real.
pros: Players feel how a shared duty works.
The duty can be tried and dropped.
cons: A forced capture shows who it falls on.
One evening cannot show effects that take longer.

pairs.tendency: Your piece walks the path by dice, and each space it lands on adds a little to what the character can do. A long roll means more spaces and more gains in one turn.
pros: A long roll pays twice, in distance and in gains.
Players watch the piece change as it travels.
cons: A lucky early run can leave the others behind for keeps.
Players who roll low gain slowly.

pairs.tendency: Every card taken from the shared row adds to the character you are building. Later rounds bring harder cards, and your early picks decide whether you can meet them.
pros: Early picks shape what the character can do later.
Players choose cards to match the build they want.
cons: A player who misses the key cards early falls behind.
Cards passed on hand rivals what you left.

pairs.tendency: Players bid for the items and powers that raise their characters, so how much you grow depends on what you were willing to pay. A bid for a sword is a bid for next round's fights.
pros: Players decide what a gain is worth to them.
Everyone can see what each coin bought.
cons: A player who wins the early bids gets a head start.
Players who spend everything may have nothing left for later.

pairs.tendency: One more risk can earn one more gain, so the character grows while the player keeps going. If the push fails, the gains held so far are lost.
pros: Risk can turn into power.
Players choose for themselves how far to go.
cons: A failed push can wipe out recent growth.
The player who loses often falls further behind next round.

pairs.tendency: Holding a region of the map adds to what your side can do, and a bigger side can hold more regions. Growth and land feed each other round after round.
pros: Each region held adds strength.
Players know what they are fighting for.
cons: The leader holds the most land and gains the most.
Losing a region takes its gain away too.

pairs.tendency: Some jobs on the board raise your character, and everyone wants those first. The player who gets there takes the gain, and the others have to find another way to grow that turn.
pros: Players race for the jobs that raise them.
Each placement has a clear return.
cons: A taken spot shuts rivals out for the turn.
Turn order decides who grows first.

pairs.tendency: Finishing a row or a mosaic of shapes unlocks a new power for the character. Each pattern is a small goal, and the character gets more able as patterns are done.
pros: Patterns give players a clear goal.
Each finished pattern is something to show.
cons: A half-built pattern gives nothing yet.
Rivals can block the tiles you need.

pairs.tendency: A hand of cards decides when the character grows. Some players play a card at once for a small gain; others hold cards back for one large jump.
pros: Players choose when to grow.
Saved cards can make one big jump.
cons: Holding cards back means slow growth early on.
A full hand is hard to plan around.

pairs.tendency: Each trick won adds a step of growth for the winner, so a round of cards becomes a round of levelling. The player who wins early starts the next trick with more power than the rest.
pros: Winning a trick gives a visible reward.
Players count tricks to plan their growth.
cons: Early winners keep growing while others lag.
A losing hand earns nothing at all.

pairs.tendency: Players trade help across the table, and a deal can hand someone a power-up. A promise made in round two may decide who can face the hard challenge in round six.
pros: Deals can speed up growth for both sides.
Players have a reason to talk to each other.
cons: A deal that helps a rival can come back later.
Long talks slow the game.

pairs.tendency: Each finished set raises the character, so players chase matching cards to level up. A set of three may give a small gain and a set of five a large one.
pros: Players get clear targets.
Gathering things gives steady growth.
cons: One missing card can hold up a whole set.
Players may hoard cards only to keep rivals from growing.

pairs.tendency: The map builds up tile by tile, and the character grows as it crosses new tiles. By the end the table shows both the world and how far the character has come.
pros: The map grows as the character grows.
The table shows the story of the game.
cons: A tile in the wrong place can block a gain.
The map gets crowded late in the game.

pairs.tendency: A player makes a call, the next player answers, and each right answer teaches the character a new skill. Later calls ask for more, and the grown character can reach them.
pros: Answers feed straight into growth.
Calls can get harder as skills build up.
cons: A missed answer stalls growth.
Players waiting for their reply may lose the thread.

pairs.tendency: Nobody talks, so a player shows when to grow only by which card goes down and when. Two players who read each other can both grow, and two who do not may both stall.
pros: Players learn to read each other's timing.
Gains arrive quietly.
cons: A player cannot explain why they are waiting.
A slip in timing is hard to repair.

pairs.tendency: A rule can be changed on your turn, and one rule may decide what growth earns. Change it and the same move gives a larger gain, or none.
pros: Players can bend the path of growth.
The game shifts as the characters change.
cons: A rule change can undo a rival's plan.
Players may argue over what exactly changed.

pairs.tendency: The character speaks and acts in scenes, and what it does in those scenes makes it more able. A brave choice in a market can earn the skill that opens a door later.
pros: Growth follows the story.
Players have a reason behind each choice.
cons: Quiet players may gain less.
The story can slow while players decide.

pairs.tendency: Hands earn the growth: a steady flick or a careful pull gives the character a gain, and later tasks ask for more, like a taller tower. A shaky hand can lose what was gained.
pros: Skill with the hands shows on the character.
Players watch every throw.
cons: A slip can lose a gain.
Players with steady hands pull ahead.

pairs.tendency: Players draw the world as the game goes, and each place drawn holds something for the character to find. The map and the character get bigger together on one sheet.
pros: The world is made as the character grows.
Each place on the map has a reason to be there.
cons: A blank sheet offers little to gain at first.
Drawing takes time away from playing.

pairs.tendency: Each turn adds an item to the spoken list, and the character adds a power to match. By turn ten the list is long and so is the sheet of things the character can do.
pros: Memory and growth rise together.
Every turn says a little more than the last.
cons: Late in the game the list is hard to recall.
Slow with many players.

pairs.tendency: The leading player starts with less, while growth in play pushes every character up. The two pull against each other: the handicap closes the gap and growth can open it again.
pros: Players of different skill start closer.
Growth gives the player who is behind a way back.
cons: Growth can widen the gap the handicap closed.
Players may argue about whether the handicap still counts.

pairs.tendency: Each clue the searchers find gives them a sharper sense or a new tool for the next hunt. The hider has nothing to grow, so the searchers get ahead as the game goes on.
pros: Searchers get tools as they go.
Each find moves the hunt forward.
cons: The hider has no way to grow.
Late hunts end quickly once the searchers have every tool.

pairs.tendency: A piece that jumps gains something, maybe a longer hop next time. A grown piece that is itself jumped is a bigger loss for its owner.
pros: Jumps pay off with growth.
Players plan chains of hops.
cons: A grown piece is a costly one to lose.
A long chain can happen in a single turn.

pairs.tendency: The dice you keep are the gains the character takes, and the ones you roll again are a gamble for more. After the last roll you stop with what you hold and the character grows by that much.
pros: Players pick which dice to keep.
Every roll carries the hope of a big gain.
cons: The last roll may give little.
Many dice slow the turn.

pairs.tendency: Landing on a rival's piece sends it back to the start, and the growth it carried goes with it. A piece that has grown a lot is the one worth landing on.
pros: Landing on a rival has a large effect.
Players value the safe spaces.
cons: All growth can vanish in a single landing.
Players may hold back from growing too early.

pairs.tendency: A mill takes a rival's piece and also lifts your character, so one row gives two gains. The rival loses a piece and sees you move ahead in the same turn.
pros: One row gives two rewards.
Players build rows with a clear aim.
cons: A single mill can swing the game.
The player behind has little to catch up with.

pairs.tendency: Longer words earn bigger gains, so a player with a long word can raise the character far in one turn. Letters turn into power one word at a time.
pros: Each word lifts the character.
Words give players a clear score to chase.
cons: A wide vocabulary gives a lead.
Checking the dictionary slows play.

pairs.tendency: Every tile that fits an open end gives the character a small gain, and a turn missed for lack of a match is a turn without growth. The tiles in your hand decide how fast you level.
pros: Each matched tile gives a gain.
Players plan which tile to keep for later.
cons: Missing a turn means missing a gain.
A hand without the right numbers levels slowly.

pairs.tendency: Laying down a finished set raises the character, and cards added to the set later can raise it again. A set left on the table keeps giving, and sometimes other players add to it too.
pros: Gains can come from the same set more than once.
Players can see each other's growth on the table.
cons: A rival can add cards to a set and share the gain.
Laying a set early shows others what you hold.

pairs.tendency: The character can grow for keeps or keep a single-use power for a hard moment. A player holding a marker has to decide whether to use it now or let the character grow first.
pros: Players decide when to spend a power.
Growth and single-use powers sit side by side.
cons: A power used early is gone when it is needed.
Players may hold markers too long.

pairs.tendency: The other player can turn down the move that would raise your character, or pick one of two you offer. Growth then depends on a rival's answer as much as on your turn.
pros: Your rival shapes your growth.
Players learn to offer moves a rival will accept.
cons: A refusal can stall a plan.
Growth becomes slower to predict.

pairs.tendency: A message goes from player to player, and each one who passes it on earns a small gain. The message may change on the way, and a changed message may give the next player a different gain.
pros: Passing the message gives every player a share.
The table works together on one thing.
cons: The message may change and cannot be checked.
A long chain of players takes time.

pairs.tendency: Before play begins, players pass cards that could have grown their characters, and wait to see what comes back. What you give away shapes the opening of someone else's game.
pros: Players give away cards that help others grow.
The first turns start with a surprise.
cons: A gift can help the rival you have to face.
You cannot look at the incoming cards until you have chosen.

pairs.tendency: One player sets up the starting powers and the other picks a side. The one setting up knows that every gain built in will count for the side the rival chooses.
pros: Both sides start with powers that look close.
The player setting up thinks about both characters.
cons: The setup takes longer to plan.
Growth later can still favour one side.

pairs.tendency: A piece that reaches the far end turns into a more powerful one, so growth comes in one jump. Both rules turn a small piece into a larger one, one slowly and one all at once.
pros: Pieces have a reason to push forward.
A promotion is easy to see on the board.
cons: Growth rules and promotion can pile up on one piece.
A piece close to the end becomes the one to stop.

pairs.tendency: Each runner finishes a leg and hands on something earned, so the next runner starts with more. Later legs are harder, and the team that grew most along the way takes them faster.
pros: Each leg adds to what the next runner can do.
Teams can see whose growth is paying off.
cons: One runner who gains little holds up the whole team.
Growth that falls behind is hard to recover in a race.

pairs.tendency: A shape that cannot be captured works as a goal, and making it raises the character. Once a group of stones is safe, the power it gives cannot be taken away by surrounding it.
pros: Players have a shape to build towards.
A safe group gives lasting growth.
cons: The rival works to stop the shape forming.
Players may spend turns on the shape and not the board.

pairs.tendency: The prizes are named cards, and winning one raises the character. A card that wins more than one prize can give a double jump in a single trick.
pros: Players know which cards give growth.
One card can give more than one gain.
cons: A player who holds the named cards pulls far ahead.
Players spend tricks chasing the prizes.

pairs.tendency: Cards in the middle are open to all, and the character's powers add to what the table gives. Two players with the same middle cards can reach different totals because their characters differ.
pros: The same cards give different results to each character.
Players can compare their options in plain view.
cons: A grown character wins most shared cards.
A player who is behind has little to add.

pairs.tendency: The pot sits in the middle and grows each round it is not won, as the character does. The winner takes the pot and gains power with it, so a long wait makes the prize larger.
pros: The prize gets larger every round.
Players can see what is at stake.
cons: A long run without a winner makes the final round heavy.
The player who wins the big pot may be far ahead.

pairs.tendency: Seeds in a pit are a store that gets bigger as seeds drop in, a little like a character that gets more able. Each turn scoops a pit and spreads it, and where the last seed lands decides what you take.
pros: A pit of seeds shows growth you can count.
Players plan where the last seed will land.
cons: Scooping a pit empties what you built.
Rivals can take a full pit in one move.

pairs.tendency: The spare hand can hold the cards that give a character a leap, and one player gets to take it. That player then starts with a head start the others cannot see.
pros: One player can pick up a large boost.
The opening has a choice in it.
cons: The player who takes the spare hand starts far ahead.
Others learn about it only when it is used.

pairs.tendency: Some squares on the track raise your character and others send it back or make it miss a turn. A grown piece keeps going on the safe squares and loses most on the sending-back ones.
pros: Squares give players places to aim for.
Growth and setback share the same track.
cons: One sending-back square can undo a long run.
The same square can help one piece and hurt another.

pairs.tendency: Every card or unit has a price, and growth gives the character more to spend. A player who grows fast buys the costly items sooner, and one who grows slowly waits.
pros: Growth opens up the costly items.
Players choose what to buy with what they have.
cons: A slow start keeps the costly items out of reach.
Spending on items can slow growth.

pairs.tendency: Power is shared out between several places, and growth adds more to share. A player who puts a lot in one place has less in the others, and the rival is sharing out too.
pros: Growth gives players more to share out.
Each choice shows where a player is putting effort.
cons: A big gain in one place leaves another bare.
Rivals can aim at the thinnest place.

pairs.tendency: Everyone keeps moving until the signal, then freezes, and the character grows in the moments between. The slowest to stop is caught and loses the gain from that stretch.
pros: Growth comes between the stops.
Players watch for the signal.
cons: The slowest player loses a gain.
Short stretches leave little room to grow.

pairs.tendency: Cards can be put back and swapped for new ones, which lets a player aim at the cards that grow the character. A few swaps can turn a plain hand into one that levels up.
pros: Players can aim their hand at growth.
A swap gives a second chance.
cons: Swapping takes turns.
Another player may have to agree to the swap.

pairs.tendency: A big pile of discards can be taken in one go, and every card in it may add to the character. The player who picks it up grows at once, while the others see the pile vanish.
pros: One pickup can give a large gain.
Players watch the pile grow.
cons: The pile goes to one player.
Throwing a card away may help the next player.

pairs.tendency: One suit beats the rest, and the character grows by gaining cards in that suit. A low trump can win a trick, so a small gain can have a large effect.
pros: Players know which suit counts most.
Small gains can still win tricks.
cons: Holding many trumps puts a player in front.
Players with no trump can only wait.

pairs.tendency: One character grows on two boards, so a gain on the first board can help in the second. A move that raises you in one game may leave you open in the other.
pros: A gain can pay off on both boards.
Players attack on one board and defend on the other.
cons: Watching two boards at once is hard.
A mistake on one board can drag the other down.

pairs.tendency: A wild card can fill the one gap that stops the character from gaining a power. Players hold wilds for the moment when one card finishes a set.
pros: A wild card can finish a gain.
Players decide when to use a wild.
cons: A wild used early is lost for later.
A player with many wilds grows much faster.

pairs.tendency: A piece that leaves the right edge comes back in on the left, so growth does not stop at a wall. A grown piece can run round the board and reach any rival from either side.
pros: A grown piece can reach anywhere.
There is no safe corner.
cons: Pieces can be chased in a circle.
The edge no longer protects anyone.

pairs.tendency: Each yes or no shrinks the list, and a character that has grown can ask a sharper question. By the end the questions come from someone who has learned how the secret works.
pros: Each answer adds to what is known.
Questions improve as the player grows.
cons: A wasted question gives little.
Players who ask early have the least to go on.

pairs.tendency: Everyone races for the end, and the character that grows on the way goes faster. A player who stops to grow loses time, and one who runs at once may have nothing for the last stretch.
pros: Players choose between speed now and growth.
The race has a clear finish.
cons: A slow start may be too far behind to catch up.
Growth along the way makes the lead hard to close.

pairs.tendency: The character that grows earns more points each turn, so the score climbs faster as the game goes on. A player who grows early gets points from the first round to the last.
pros: Growth turns into points.
Players can see who is ahead.
cons: An early lead keeps growing.
Players behind find the gap widening.

pairs.tendency: Players are knocked out one by one. The characters that have grown furthest are the ones still in the game at the end.
pros: Growth helps a player stay in.
The ending is clear.
cons: A knocked-out player has nothing to grow.
Players out early wait a long time.

pairs.tendency: The whole table grows against a game that grows harder too. Everyone stays alive only if the characters gain power at about the rate the game does.
pros: All players share the pressure.
Growth is a team matter.
cons: One character who falls behind puts everyone at risk.
The game can end suddenly for all.

pairs.tendency: The team has one goal, and each character grows to help reach it. A player who grows into a certain role can finish the part of the goal that no one else could.
pros: Each player grows into a part of the goal.
The goal is clear to all.
cons: One player who grows slowly holds up the goal.
Players may argue over who grows next.

pairs.tendency: Growth shows others what you are up to. A player who grows in a certain way tells the table what their secret goal might be, so every power gained is a clue.
pros: Growth choices hint at hidden goals.
Players watch each other closely.
cons: Growing in the open gives the goal away.
A player who hides by not growing falls behind.

pairs.tendency: Each chapter of the story gives the character a new ability, so by the end the character can do things it could not do at the start. The story ends when the character has grown into the final scene.
pros: Growth marks the chapters of the story.
The ending has been built up to.
cons: A story that stops early leaves the character unfinished.
Players may rush growth to reach the end.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, but the characters still grow, so at the end players look at what each one has become. The table has the characters to talk about instead of a score.
pros: Players have something to look at when the game ends.
Growth has no finish line to chase.
cons: Players may not know when to stop growing.
The game can end without anyone feeling it is done.

pairs.tendency: Each player decides what a successful game means, and growth is one way to get there. One player may grow the character all the way up, while another is content to stay small and safe.
pros: Players pick how much to grow.
Growth fits what each player wants.
cons: Players may not agree on who came out ahead.
Comparing characters is hard.

pairs.tendency: The game ends when one player loses, and growth is a way to stay safe. A player who grows early can sit back, while one who does not may be the loser.
pros: Growth gives a way to avoid being the loser.
Players know who is at risk.
cons: The player at risk may find it hard to catch up.
Players who are safe have little left to do.

pairs.tendency: The game runs over many sessions and the characters grow with each one. A player can come back after a week to a character with more power than before.
pros: Characters grow across sessions.
Players come back to see what changed.
cons: Late arrivals face characters that have grown far.
A game with no end has no moment to stop.

pairs.tendency: Characters grow and grow, and there is nothing to reach. The game is made so that nobody can win, so growth shows only how far a character has gone, never that it has finished.
pros: Growth carries on with no finish.
Players can reflect on why they grow.
cons: Players may stop growing when they see no goal.
A character with a lot of power has nothing to use it on.

pairs.tendency: You play alone against the cards, and the character grows each time a card is cleared. The layout stays the same size while you get more able, so late cards are easier than early ones.
pros: Clearing the layout gives gains.
The player can see progress on the table.
cons: A stuck game gives no growth.
Late cards may become too easy.

pairs.tendency: Growth can carry over between games or start again each time. If it carries over, the winner of game one begins game two with more power.
pros: Players can build up over several games.
Each game has a stake for the next.
cons: A winner of the first game starts ahead.
A player behind may give up before the series is done.

pairs.tendency: Points count against you, so gaining power can mean gaining points. A player who grows a lot may end with a high total and lose.
pros: Players have to decide whether to grow.
Growth carries a cost.
cons: A grown character can be a losing one.
Players may avoid growing at all.

pairs.tendency: A character that has grown moves further each turn, which makes it easier to overshoot the number. Growth that helps early can get in the way at the end.
pros: Players have to judge their steps carefully.
Growth gives more ways to reach the number.
cons: A grown character can pass the target by too much.
A player may have to stop growing to land exactly.

pairs.tendency: The aim is turned upside down, so a character grows towards giving everything away. Each gain is one more thing to lose, and the game rewards the player who ends up with the least.
pros: Players think about what to give up.
Each gain counts against the player.
cons: Players may gain without wanting to.
The rules take time to explain.

pairs.tendency: Every player grows a character at the same time without touching anyone else. At the end the characters sit side by side and each one shows the choices of its player.
pros: Each player grows at their own pace.
Players can see other characters without being attacked.
cons: Players have little to react to.
Rivals only learn of a lead when they look across.

pairs.tendency: Players attack each other, and the grown character is the biggest target. A player who has levelled up draws attacks from those who have not.
pros: Growth pays off in a fight.
A grown character can fight back.
cons: The leader draws attacks from all sides.
Growth can make a player a target.

pairs.tendency: Players change the board and the character grows as it uses the changes. Nobody is attacked, but a grown character finds a spot taken or a wall built.
pros: Players grow without a direct fight.
The board shows what rivals did.
cons: A taken spot can stall growth.
Players may not notice what slowed them.

pairs.tendency: All players are on the same side and grow together against the game. Each character takes a different part, and the team wins only if every part has grown far enough.
pros: Every player gains from the others' growth.
The team shares the work.
cons: A lost game is lost by everyone together.
One character that falls behind can put the team at risk.

pairs.tendency: The team grows against the game, and each player also wants to grow a little more than the rest. A gain taken for yourself leaves less for the team.
pros: Players grow for the team and for themselves.
Each choice has two reasons behind it.
cons: A player who grows alone can put the team at risk.
Players may doubt each other's reasons.

pairs.tendency: Each team grows its characters and meets the other team with what it has built. Teammates can share gains, so a team can level up faster than a single player.
pros: Teams grow by sharing.
Players plan together.
cons: A team with a slow player lags behind.
One team can grow far ahead of the other.

pairs.tendency: The traitor grows too, in secret, and uses the new power against the team. A character that gains an odd power at the wrong moment may give the traitor away.
pros: The traitor has power to use.
Players watch for odd gains.
cons: A traitor who grows early is hard to stop.
Growth can make an honest player look guilty.

pairs.tendency: The character grows between letters, with a long wait for each reply. By the time the answer arrives the character has changed, so a move sent last month may no longer fit.
pros: Growth shows up between the letters.
Each letter can say what changed.
cons: A move may be out of date by the time it arrives.
The game can take weeks to grow.

pairs.tendency: The player who is not at the table can leave a character that has grown far, which others have to meet. A ghost with a lot of power gives hints from a place no one can reach.
pros: The absent player's growth is felt in play.
The others have something to measure against.
cons: The absent player cannot respond to what happens.
A grown character with no player may be hard to deal with.

pairs.tendency: The game master sets challenges that rise as the characters grow. The master can see how much power each one has and decide what the world sends next.
pros: Challenges can match the characters.
One person keeps track of the whole world.
cons: The master has a lot to prepare.
A master who sets challenges too hard can stop the game.

pairs.tendency: People passing by can join, and each starts from the beginning while others have grown. A newcomer in a street game meets players who have played all afternoon.
pros: Passers-by can join at any point.
Players who stay have more to show.
cons: A newcomer starts behind.
A game that never stops can grow hard to enter.

pairs.tendency: The lone player and the group both grow, and the lone player is paid more for a win. A group that grows at the same rate as the one player can catch them in the end.
pros: The lone player and the group both gain power.
The group has a shared plan.
cons: The lone player has no one to share growth with.
A lone player who grows too slowly is soon outnumbered.

pairs.tendency: You face the pack alone, and the character grows as it clears each part. After the game you can compare how far each of you got with a friend.
pros: Players see their own growth clearly.
Results are easy to compare afterwards.
cons: Nobody else is there to push the player.
An unlucky run leaves the character small.

pairs.tendency: The dice decide the growth, so one character can leap while another stays put. The player who rolls high gains and the player who rolls low waits.
pros: Growth arrives from a single throw.
Players hope for a big roll.
cons: Growth has little to do with choices.
A player can be left behind by luck alone.

pairs.tendency: The dice may help or hinder growth, and a re-roll or a card can soften a low throw. A player with spare cards can choose to grow anyway.
pros: Players have ways to save a low roll.
Growth is still in the player's hands.
cons: Saving a roll uses up a card.
Rerolls slow down each turn.

pairs.tendency: Choices decide most of the growth, and a small amount of luck adds a few surprises. Two players who choose the same way can still end up with different characters.
pros: Choices matter most.
Luck keeps each game different.
cons: A small run of luck can still swing a close game.
Players may blame the dice for a loss.

pairs.tendency: No dice and no surprises: every gain comes from the player's own choice. The player who plans each step of growth closely ends with the most able character.
pros: Growth follows careful planning.
Players can see why a character grew.
cons: Early mistakes are hard to recover from.
A player who plans slowly slows the table.

pairs.tendency: The throw is read as a message, and what it says tells the player how the character might grow. A throw read as a warning can lead a player to wait, and a throw read as an opening can lead to a leap.
pros: Throws give a reason to grow in a certain way.
Players talk about what a throw means.
cons: Players may read the same throw differently.
The meaning of a throw is not settled by the rules.

pairs.tendency: Players grow by sensing when the others will act, and two players in step grow together. A group that acts at the same instant lifts every character at once.
pros: Growth comes from timing.
Players learn each other's habits.
cons: A player out of step grows alone.
Nobody can say exactly what went right.

pairs.tendency: A roll on the table says who the character meets, and meeting that person can raise the character. The dice write the road, and what the character learns on it makes it more able.
pros: The dice give the character new events to grow from.
Each meeting adds to the story.
cons: The dice can send a character to a quiet road.
A table lookup slows the game.

pairs.tendency: Everyone sees every character and every gain, so a rival can tell exactly how far you have grown. A player can plan against the next gain because it is already on the table.
pros: Players can plan against what they see.
There are no hidden gains.
cons: A leader is easy to spot.
A rival can copy a plan in full view.

pairs.tendency: Cards held in secret decide how the character will grow, and rivals can only guess. A player who plays a growth card shows the table what they were saving.
pros: Players can hide their plans.
A big gain can come as a surprise.
cons: Players can only guess at rivals' growth.
A card played shows what you held.

pairs.tendency: A secret role can decide how a character grows, so players cannot tell who is who from their gains. A player who grows too fast or too slowly may be asked why.
pros: Gains give players clues about roles.
Roles stay secret for a while.
cons: A sudden gain can point at the wrong person.
Growth can expose a secret role.

pairs.tendency: Each gain is a clue, and players read the clues to work out hidden facts. A character that has suddenly got a new power tells the others where it has been.
pros: Gains become clues.
Players watch every change.
cons: A player who hides growth gives few clues.
Misreading a gain can lead the search the wrong way.

pairs.tendency: A player can claim a power the character has not yet got, and others have to guess. A character that really has grown can be taken for a bluff.
pros: Players can claim more than they hold.
Real growth can be hidden.
cons: A bluff that is called loses ground.
A player who grows slowly may be thought to be hiding something.

pairs.tendency: The rule for growth is a secret that players find by trying and being told no. A newcomer grows slowly until they learn what the game rewards.
pros: Players learn what earns growth.
Those who know the rule grow first.
cons: Newcomers get stuck.
Being told no again and again wears on a player.

pairs.tendency: One player knows the way to grow but cannot say so, and gives hints. The others try ideas, and the right hint lets the character leap.
pros: A clear hint can speed up growth.
The group works on one puzzle.
cons: The hinting player has to hold back.
Wrong guesses give nothing.

pairs.tendency: The map starts hidden, and each turned-over area may hold something that raises the character. The grown character goes further into the map than a new one could.
pros: Exploring can pay off in growth.
Nobody knows what is ahead.
cons: A turned area may hold nothing.
A bold player can meet a place that is too hard.

pairs.tendency: One open hand lies on the table and a player may play it besides their own. Everyone sees what could be gained from it, so growth through that hand is public.
pros: Everyone can see the open hand.
A player can use two hands to grow.
cons: Rivals plan around the open hand.
The player who handles the open hand carries more.

pairs.tendency: Some points are secret, so nobody knows who has grown most. A character may be far ahead and nobody can tell until the end.
pros: Players cannot be sure who leads.
A big gain can stay hidden.
cons: Players have to guess at rivals' growth.
A player may stop growing out of doubt.

pairs.tendency: One player acts at a time, and each turn is a chance to grow. Everyone else waits and watches how the character changes.
pros: Each turn is a clear step.
Players can watch each other's growth.
cons: Long waits with many players.
The first to play grows first.

pairs.tendency: Everyone chooses in secret and reveals together, so growth happens at the same moment. A player cannot wait to see what the others gain.
pros: Growth is even at each reveal.
Nobody waits.
cons: Players cannot react to a rival's gain.
A wrong guess loses the round.

pairs.tendency: Anyone can act at any moment, and the quickest player takes the gain. The character that grows first gets to the next gain first.
pros: Quick players gain first.
The game never waits.
cons: Slower players can fall far behind.
Everyone is busy at once.

pairs.tendency: Each turn has a clock, so a player has to choose a gain before time runs out. A move made for you when the clock ends may not be the one you wanted.
pros: The clock pushes players to choose.
Growth steps are short.
cons: A hurried choice can miss a gain.
Players who think slowly lose gains.

pairs.tendency: The game runs for days or weeks, and the character grows a little each day. A player who comes back each morning sees the character change slowly.
pros: Growth shows over days.
Waiting becomes part of the game.
cons: A missed day is a missed gain.
The game can fade if players lose interest.

pairs.tendency: The game slows players down, so each gain is made after a pause. A character grows in small, careful steps.
pros: Each gain is thought over.
The pace gives time to see the change.
cons: The game is slow to start.
A long wait can feel like nothing is happening.

pairs.tendency: The game speeds up as the character grows. Later turns bring more gains and more danger, and the end comes in a rush.
pros: Growth speeds up with the game.
The ending comes quickly.
cons: Late turns are hard to follow.
A slow starter has little time to catch up.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn lets a player gain twice in a row. A lucky player can grow many times before anyone else moves.
pros: An extra turn gives a double gain.
Players hope for the chance.
cons: One lucky run can end the game.
Others wait while a player takes many turns.

pairs.tendency: The first stage picks the cards, the second plays them, and growth in the first stage sets up the second. A character that grew in stage one starts stage two with more.
pros: Early growth carries into the next stage.
Each stage has its own aim.
cons: A slow first stage is hard to mend.
Players may spend too long on stage one.

pairs.tendency: The board works like a real system, and a character's growth changes how the system responds. A village that grows can use more water, and the wells feel it.
pros: Growth changes the system.
Players see cause and effect.
cons: A grown character can strain the system.
The model takes time to learn.

pairs.tendency: Each player is a group with its own needs, and the group grows in its own way. A farmer grows by water and a council grows by votes, so each reads the same problem differently.
pros: Each group grows in its own way.
Players see the problem from other sides.
cons: Groups that grow fast can crowd out others.
Players may disagree on what growth means.

pairs.tendency: Everyone draws from one limited store, and each character that grows draws more. If players take too much, the store runs out for everyone.
pros: Growth uses the shared store.
Players see what taking too much does.
cons: A grown character takes more.
The store can run out before anyone is ready.

pairs.tendency: A choice made now shows its effect a few rounds later, and growth is one of those effects. A player who grows early may only feel it when the hard rounds come.
pros: Growth pays off later.
Players plan ahead.
cons: The reward for a choice is far from the choice.
Players may not link a gain to what caused it.

pairs.tendency: Players agree a rule and play on to see what it changes, and growth shows its effect. A rule that gives more to each win can be tested over a few rounds.
pros: Players can test a rule on growth.
The result is shown in the game.
cons: A rule can change growth in ways nobody expected.
A rule that does not work wastes a round.

pairs.tendency: After the game players talk about how the characters grew and why. They ask what helped growth and what slowed it.
pros: Players look back at their growth.
The talk links the game to real life.
cons: Players may remember growth differently.
A debrief adds time after the game.

pairs.tendency: What the character gains stays for keeps, and cards torn or stickers added carry to the next game. A character does not start again from nothing.
pros: Growth cannot be undone.
The next game starts where this one ended.
cons: A mistake stays with the character.
New players join characters that have grown far.

pairs.tendency: If the rules give growth only for one kind of move, the game says something about what is worth doing. A game about a city that grows only by building roads says that cities are roads.
pros: The rules show what growth is for.
Players can see what the game values.
cons: Players can disagree with what the rules reward.
Rules that reward one move leave out others.

pairs.tendency: Growth in the game can carry into real life, so a character's power may mean real money or a promise. A player who grows the character is also growing something outside the game.
pros: Gains count outside the game.
Players take care over each choice.
cons: A loss in the game can hurt a friendship.
Players may stop playing if the stakes get large.

pairs.tendency: The game turns something that matters into points, and the character grows by getting more of them. Players start to chase the points instead of the thing they stand for.
pros: Growth is easy to count.
The game shows what a number can hide.
cons: The aim gets lost behind the score.
A number can stand in for the real thing.

pairs.tendency: Players practise a way of living, and the character grows into the new life. A village that shares everything shows what a shared house or field might feel like after a few seasons.
pros: Players try a future before it exists.
Growth shows how a change might feel.
cons: The practice may not match real life.
A future that grows too fast can seem unreal.

pairs.tendency: Before each roll you say the whole list and add a word, then the dice carry your piece along the path. The walk around the board slows down as the list gets longer.
pros: Memory work sits beside plain dice luck.
Easy for any age to start.
cons: Turns get longer as the list grows.
A wrong recital can hold up a player's move.

pairs.tendency: Each time you take a card from the shared row, you say the list so far and add the name of your pick. Everyone hears what has been taken.
pros: Picks are spoken, so players know what is gone.
The list doubles as a record of the draft.
cons: Reciting before every pick slows the row.
Late picks get rushed once the list is long.

pairs.tendency: Every bid is called out and added to the list, and the group repeats the list before the next offer. By the end it holds every price that was named.
pros: Players recall old offers when they price a new one.
A shared record of what was offered.
cons: If someone forgets a bid, the auction stops.
Quiet players lose the thread of the prices.

pairs.tendency: After saying the list and adding a word, you choose whether to risk another round. The longer the list, the more there is to get wrong in a single go.
pros: Two risks sit together, one from luck and one from memory.
Players watch each other's recital closely.
cons: A slip can lose everything you have gathered.
The pressure rises with every turn.

pairs.tendency: When a player moves into a region, they name it and add it to the list. The list ends up as the order in which the map was claimed.
pros: Players learn the order of the claims.
The list is a short history of the map.
cons: On a large map it is hard to check a recital.
Talking about the list can take more time than placing pieces.

pairs.tendency: Each worker you place adds a job to the list, so the list reads like a day's work from the first job to the last.
pros: Players remember which jobs are already taken.
Early jobs come back up again and again.
cons: A late worker has a hard time finding a free job.
Players argue about who took which job.

pairs.tendency: As you lay a tile you name its colour and add it to the list, so the spoken list copies the pattern on the table.
pros: Slips are easy to spot, since the tiles on the table hold the same colours.
Players can check each other by looking.
cons: The pattern is already on the table, so the list adds little to it.
Naming the same colours again and again repeats a lot.

pairs.tendency: Cards you play are called out and added to the list, while the cards in your hand stay hidden. Others hear what has gone but never what is left.
pros: Players can count which cards are gone.
Held cards stay secret.
cons: Players who forget the list lose track of what remains.
Your recital shows your habits.

pairs.tendency: After each trick, the cards that were played join the list. A player who recalls the list knows which high cards are already out.
pros: Remembering the list tells you what is left in the pack.
Counting cards becomes part of play for everyone.
cons: Each trick needs a pause to recite.
Players who forget fall behind fast.

pairs.tendency: Every deal is added to the list, saying who offered what to whom. When two people disagree about what was agreed, the list is the record.
pros: A shared record of promises.
Everyone can check a deal.
cons: Old deals get raised at awkward moments.
Reciting every deal gives away private offers.

pairs.tendency: Each time you take a piece for your set, you name it and add it to the list, so everyone hears what the others are gathering.
pros: Players can guess each other's sets.
Collecting stays out in the open.
cons: Naming your pieces gives your plan away.
The list grows faster than the sets do.

pairs.tendency: When a tile joins the map, you describe it and add it to the list. After a while the spoken list describes the whole map.
pros: Players picture the map in their heads.
Every tile gets noticed.
cons: Long descriptions slow each turn.
The spoken map and the real map can disagree.

pairs.tendency: One player calls a word and the next answers with a word that goes on the list. The group then chants the whole chain back from the start, one word longer each round.
pros: The rhythm helps players remember.
Everyone joins in the chant.
cons: One wrong word sends the chant back to the start.
A long chain can be too much for younger players.

pairs.tendency: Nobody can speak, so the list cannot be said out loud. Items are shown by gesture or by the cards laid down, and the group tries to recall the order.
pros: Players watch hands and faces.
A calm table.
cons: Unclear gestures lead to arguments about what was shown.
With no speech, nobody can correct a missed item.

pairs.tendency: A player can change how the list works, such as saying only the last five items or running it backwards. The game and the list shift together.
pros: Players tune the memory task to their group.
New rules stay in mind because they are spoken.
cons: A rule change can wipe out a list others have learned.
Players quarrel over which rule applies now.

pairs.tendency: Each item you add is something your character would say or carry, so the list turns into a pile of details about the story.
pros: Items hang on characters, so they are easier to keep in mind.
The story gains small details.
cons: Players spend time on the character instead of the list.
Players invent items in very different styles.

pairs.tendency: You say the list and add an item while your hands do something tricky, such as balancing a block on your palm. Speaking and keeping steady happen together.
pros: Two tasks at once draw the whole table's attention.
Every attempt is watched closely.
cons: A shaky hand makes you lose your place in the list.
Younger children may find both together too hard.

pairs.tendency: Items you add are drawn on the shared sheet as places or features. The list is spoken and also seen.
pros: Drawing helps recall.
The map records the order the items came in.
cons: The sheet fills up and drawings overlap.
Slow drawers hold up everyone else.

pairs.tendency: A player with a handicap might say fewer items, or be allowed to read the list from a sheet. Each person starts the memory task at a different level.
pros: Younger and older players can sit together.
Players choose their own help.
cons: Others can see who needs the help.
Agreeing the size of the handicap takes time.

pairs.tendency: The hider adds an item that stands for a hiding place each round, and the seekers recall the list to know which places they have already tried.
pros: Seekers rely on memory to avoid searching twice.
The list works as a search record.
cons: A seeker who forgets a place goes back to it.
The hider hears every guess and cannot keep a secret.

pairs.tendency: Each hop is announced and added to the list, so a chain of jumps turns into a spoken string of spaces.
pros: Multi-jump turns leave a clear record.
Players can follow the path of a piece.
cons: A long chain of jumps means a long recital.
Players check the list against the board and stop to argue.

pairs.tendency: The dice results you set aside become the next items on the list, and the dice you roll again stay out until you decide.
pros: Every face you keep is spoken aloud, so your choices are public.
Players track which values have been set aside.
cons: Reciting after each re-roll slows the throw.
A lot of numbers to hold in mind.

pairs.tendency: If you land on another player's piece, that piece goes back to the start, and the player hit has to start the list again from the first item.
pros: A hit costs a piece and a recital.
Players watch where they land.
cons: One landing can undo a long recital.
The hit player has to repeat a lot.

pairs.tendency: When you make a mill, you announce it by adding an item to the list, and the player who loses a piece names which one it was.
pros: Mills are remembered.
Taken pieces are recorded.
cons: Players track two things, the board and the list.
Arguments start over whether a mill was announced.

pairs.tendency: The items on the list are words made from the letters, and a dictionary can settle whether each one is real.
pros: Spelling and memory in one task.
A dictionary ends arguments.
cons: Looking up words stops play.
Players who know fewer words add less to the list.

pairs.tendency: The list follows the line of tiles: each tile's number is added to the list, and the next tile has to match the end.
pros: The list repeats the numbers in the line of tiles.
Players know which numbers are still open.
cons: A player with no matching tile still has to recite.
Missing a turn leaves a long list to rehearse.

pairs.tendency: A meld laid on the table is added to the list as a set, and anyone who adds to a meld says the full set again.
pros: Sets are public, so players recall them.
Adding to melds builds a longer recital.
cons: Reciting long melds takes time.
Players lose count of which cards sit in which meld.

pairs.tendency: When someone uses their one-time power, it goes on the list with their name. The list shows which powers have gone.
pros: Players can see which powers remain.
Timing is remembered.
cons: A forgotten power gets used twice by mistake.
Players reason about who still holds one.

pairs.tendency: Before you add an item, you offer it to the other player, who can turn it down or pick between two items you name. Two people build the list together.
pros: Both players shape the list.
An offer shows what each person thinks the other remembers.
cons: Offering takes extra time.
A refused item leaves the turn with no progress.

pairs.tendency: The list is whispered from player to player and grows as it goes. It changes on the way, and the last player says what arrived, which may differ from the first.
pros: Mistakes change the list on its way.
Everyone hears something different.
cons: Nobody can tell where an error began.
Players at the end hear something far from the start.

pairs.tendency: Before play, each player names the cards they pass, and those names start the list. Everyone knows what moved but not what was kept.
pros: The starting list is shared.
Players learn something about each other's hands.
cons: Naming passed cards gives away part of the secret.
The list is already long before play begins.

pairs.tendency: One player sets out a starting list, and the other chooses to take it or hand it over. The first player tries to make a list that is even for both sides.
pros: The starter aims for an even list.
The chooser gets a real choice.
cons: A misjudged starting list favours one side.
Both sides read a long list before choosing.

pairs.tendency: When a piece reaches the far end, you add an item to the list for its new form, so the list records every promotion in order.
pros: Players can see how many pieces have changed.
Reaching the end gets a spoken marker.
cons: A promotion stops play for a recital.
Late in the game the list is long.

pairs.tendency: Each runner in the relay says the list, adds an item, then hands the baton on. The team's list has to be correct when the last leg ends.
pros: The team shares one list.
Running and remembering both count.
cons: One forgotten item stops the whole team.
Players wait around while their runner recites.

pairs.tendency: When your stones make a safe shape, you announce it and add it to the list. Once it is there, nothing can capture those stones.
pros: Players know where the safe areas are.
Shapes become named things.
cons: Naming a shape shows your plan.
The other player can aim at shapes not yet on the list.

pairs.tendency: Players recite the named prize cards at the start, and the list of who won which prize grows through the hand.
pros: Prize cards stay in mind.
Winners are remembered.
cons: A card that carries several prizes tangles the list.
Players lose track of which prize went where.

pairs.tendency: Cards in the middle are added to the list as they are turned, so everyone says what is on the table before building a hand.
pros: Everyone starts with the same facts.
Table cards are rarely missed.
cons: Reciting open cards adds a step each round.
Some players use the recital to stall.

pairs.tendency: The size of the pot is added to the list each round. When nobody wins it, the pot is said again, and it is bigger.
pros: Players know how much is in the pot.
Carry-overs are remembered.
cons: Numbers get large and hard to recite.
Players add up counters instead of listening.

pairs.tendency: Pits are named as the seeds land in them, and each name goes on the list. It traces the path of the seeds round the board.
pros: The trail of a sowing is spoken.
Players check each other's counts.
cons: Many pits make a long list.
A wrong seed count gives a wrong list.

pairs.tendency: The spare hand is read out card by card once, and those cards start the list. The player who takes it has to recall it all.
pros: Players learn what the spare hand held.
The list begins with shared facts.
cons: Reading it out removes the secret from the spare hand.
A player who leaves it alone knows less than the rest.

pairs.tendency: A special square joins the list the first time a piece lands on it, with its rule. The list slowly becomes a guide to the track.
pros: The rules of the board are learned as the list grows.
Players remember squares they have already hit.
cons: New players do not know a square until someone lands there.
Saying the names of squares slows the track.

pairs.tendency: Every purchase is added to the list with its price, so at any moment the list shows what has been bought.
pros: Spending is public.
Players plan their money with the list in mind.
cons: A forgotten price causes an argument.
Small purchases crowd the list.

pairs.tendency: Players read out each split as a short line of how much went where, and the next player adds their own split to the list.
pros: Players compare splits.
The sizes become known.
cons: Reading a split shows the plan behind it.
Rows of numbers are hard to hold in mind.

pairs.tendency: Players keep adding to the list until the signal comes, then freeze. Whoever is halfway through a word when it stops is caught.
pros: Players listen for the signal while they speak.
The signal can come at any point in the list.
cons: Players rush and mumble.
The signal can cut a recital in half.

pairs.tendency: When you put cards back, you name them as you add to the list, so everyone hears what has gone back to the pile.
pros: Players learn what is in the pile.
Swaps leave a record.
cons: Your swap shows what you were missing.
Reciting every swap slows down the swapping.

pairs.tendency: Each discard is added to the list. When someone picks up the pile, the list is read out for them, and they hold every card on it.
pros: The pile's contents are known.
Taking the pile becomes an informed choice.
cons: The list grows with every discard.
A long list makes the pile risky to read out.

pairs.tendency: The trump suit heads the list, and each card you add is said with its suit. The recital shows how the trump has been played.
pros: Trumps are easy to pick out in the recital.
Players hear which suits are used.
cons: Saying suit and value doubles the words.
A trump played early is forgotten by the end.

pairs.tendency: You keep two lists, one for each board, and add to the one that matches the board you moved on.
pros: Two lists need two kinds of attention.
Players watch both boards.
cons: The two lists get mixed up.
The memory work is doubled.

pairs.tendency: A wild card can go on the list as any item you name, so the list may hold a word that is not on the card.
pros: One card can stand for many items.
Others have to remember what you called it.
cons: Players disagree about what the wild card stood for.
A forgotten name for a wild card breaks the list.

pairs.tendency: Pieces walk off one edge and come back on the other, and the list loops the same way: after the last item, the first comes round again.
pros: The list and the board both go round.
There is no dead end.
cons: It is hard to tell where the list begins.
Players lose the first item in the circle.

pairs.tendency: Two lists pull against each other: the list of questions grows every turn, while the list of things the secret could be shrinks with each answer.
pros: Players track what is left.
Each question has a clear purpose.
cons: Players mix up which list is which.
Answers drop items from a list that others are still reciting.

pairs.tendency: The race is to be first to say the list to the end without an error. Speed and memory are both tested.
pros: Speed and memory count together.
The finish is easy to see.
cons: A fast speaker who slips is caught.
Slow reciters cannot catch up.

pairs.tendency: A correct recital scores a point for the turn, and the highest score at the end wins.
pros: Every turn scores.
Scores stay close for a while.
cons: Players count points and items at once.
A player who errs early trails for the rest of the game.

pairs.tendency: A player who gets the list wrong is out. The last one still reciting wins.
pros: A memory slip knocks a player out.
The list grows harder as players drop.
cons: Early exits wait a long time.
Late in the game nearly everyone fails.

pairs.tendency: The whole table keeps the list going together and helps each other say it, against a limit the game sets.
pros: Players help each other.
The list is held by the group.
cons: One person's slip hurts everyone.
Prompting can turn into saying the item for someone.

pairs.tendency: The group aims for a list of an agreed length. Each player adds an item and the group counts towards the target.
pros: Players know the goal number.
Effort is shared.
cons: Players argue about which item to add.
A high target means a long way to go.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a secret aim for what the list will hold, and nudges the list that way with the item they add.
pros: Items carry a hidden meaning.
Players watch each other's choices.
cons: Everyone recites, so secrets leak.
A secret goal is hard to chase when earlier items have fixed the list.

pairs.tendency: The list is the story: each item is the next event or object, and the story is told back from the start every turn.
pros: The story is told in order.
Everyone knows the story so far.
cons: The story gets long and details drop out.
The ending is hard to reach before the list is too long.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins. The list grows until the players stop and look at what it holds.
pros: The final list is read as a record.
No score hangs over any turn.
cons: There is no clear point to stop.
Players disagree on when to end.

pairs.tendency: One player aims to say twenty items, another to beat their last try. The shared list serves each of them.
pros: Each player measures themself.
Different ages can play together.
cons: There is no shared result.
Players cannot compare easily.

pairs.tendency: The first player to get the list wrong loses, and everyone else is safe.
pros: There is only one result to watch for.
Everyone else is safe the moment someone slips.
cons: One person carries the loss.
The game ends at the first error.

pairs.tendency: The list grows with no end in sight, and players help each other keep it alive across many sittings, the way a campaign runs over weeks.
pros: The list becomes a long record.
Players come back to it.
cons: New players join a list they do not know.
In time the list is too long to say in one sitting.
