pros: A power can stop a line coming round.
Players watch both edges.
cons: Using it at the wrong edge does nothing.
A board that was closed stays closed.

pairs.tendency: One question from the guesser can get a longer answer if a power is spent on it. The marker is then removed.
pros: A power can save a question.
It tends to be held for the final guess.
cons: A long answer can mislead.
The power may be spent on a question that needed none.

pairs.tendency: A power jumps a piece forward one time, and the marker is gone. Players choose when to jump.
pros: A power can win a close race.
Players watch each other's markers.
cons: A jump too early leaves the finish open.
A leader may be caught by a late power.

pairs.tendency: A power doubles a score or steals points, after which its marker leaves.
pros: A power can swing a total.
Players hold it for the last round.
cons: The moment to use it can pass.
Players may sit on it and score little.

pairs.tendency: A power keeps a player alive through one more hit before its marker is taken away.
pros: A power buys one more turn.
Players watch who still has one.
cons: Others aim at players whose power is spent.
A player with no power becomes a target.

pairs.tendency: Each player holds a power that works once, and the team has to use them in the right order to survive.
pros: Powers form a plan.
The team can see all the powers.
cons: A power used out of order can fail the team.
One spent power can end the plan.

pairs.tendency: Spent once, a power adds a big step towards the shared goal, and its marker goes.
pros: A power pushes the goal forward.
The team picks who uses what.
cons: A power used early may not be needed.
Players may argue over whose power goes first.

pairs.tendency: A power helps a secret goal, and using it can show others what you want.
pros: A power fits a goal.
Players try to guess goals from power use.
cons: Using a power can give away the goal.
A spent power cannot hide you again.

pairs.tendency: A power marks a turning point in the story, such as a rescue, and works once.
pros: A power gives a scene its high point.
Players pick the scene.
cons: A power spent on a minor scene loses the effect.
The story may end before it is used.

pairs.tendency: Powers are used for what they do, since nobody wins. Players look at what the table made.
pros: Powers become small experiments.
Players talk about what each did.
cons: Nothing says when to use a power.
Some players keep theirs till the end.

pairs.tendency: Each player picks a goal, and a power that works once can help reach it.
pros: Powers fit the goals.
Players compare how they used theirs.
cons: A power may not suit the goal chosen.
Two players may use theirs for very different ends.

pairs.tendency: A power passes the loss to another player, and that uses up its marker.
pros: A power moves the blame.
Players watch who is exposed.
cons: Without it, the loss can land on you.
Others wait for you to spend it.

pairs.tendency: A power that works once keeps the game from ending, such as by undoing a final move, and its marker is then removed.
pros: A power can extend a game.
Players spend powers to keep playing.
cons: Powers run out over time.
The game still ends when the last one is used.

pairs.tendency: A power works once but the game cannot be won, so players use it to see what happens.
pros: Using a power is a way to find out what it does.
Players watch what each one does.
cons: There is no prize for useful timing.
Some players spend powers to be done with them.

pairs.tendency: You play alone, with one power to save a stuck layout a single time. The marker goes after.
pros: A power can clear a stuck layout.
You decide when the layout is stuck enough.
cons: A power used early leaves the last stuck moment alone.
Nobody else is there to see the use.

pairs.tendency: Each player has one power for the whole match, to be used in any single game.
pros: A power belongs to one game.
Players plan across games.
cons: A power used in game one is gone for game three.
A player behind may spend it in a panic.

pairs.tendency: A power wipes out the points you have picked up, or passes them on, and is then gone.
pros: A power cleans a score.
A heavy hand is when it pays off.
cons: On a light score it saves almost nothing.
Rivals dump points just before it is used.

pairs.tendency: A power adds one to the number you need or takes one away, a single time, and the marker is removed.
pros: A power fixes an overshoot.
Players save it for the final step.
cons: Before the last step it does nothing.
A near miss leaves the power unused.

pairs.tendency: A power helps you lose faster or push a win onto someone else. It works once and the marker goes.
pros: A power helps you give things away.
Players hide their intent.
cons: Others may refuse what you push at them.
Players may use the power too soon.

pairs.tendency: Each player holds a power but works alone, so powers only help their own build.
pros: A power helps one build.
Players watch what others do on their own boards.
cons: Powers cannot be used on a rival.
Players rarely react to each other.

pairs.tendency: A power can hit another player once, such as a steal or a block. The marker leaves after use.
pros: A power gives one strike.
Players know who is carrying one.
cons: Once it is spent, you can be hit back.
A player with a power left is a target.

pairs.tendency: A power changes the board once, so others feel it through the layout, and the marker goes.
pros: A power reshapes the board.
Players read the board for changes.
cons: The result may reach someone you did not aim at.
Others may not see where the change came from.

pairs.tendency: Every player holds a power, and the team shares them against the game. Each works once.
pros: Powers are shared tools.
The team sees who has what.
cons: A power in the wrong hands is wasted.
A lost power cannot be replaced.

pairs.tendency: Powers help the team but a player may use theirs to get ahead, once.
pros: A power serves two aims.
Players watch for private motives.
cons: A power used for self may cost the team.
Others may keep theirs in case.

pairs.tendency: Each team holds a few powers, and teammates agree when to use them.
pros: Teams plan their powers.
Players see the other team's markers.
cons: A team may spend its powers too early.
A team that talks about powers gives them away.

pairs.tendency: A power can unmask a traitor, or help the traitor hide, a single time. The marker is then gone.
pros: A power can expose a lie.
Players watch who uses theirs.
cons: A wrong accusation costs the power.
A traitor can use a power to sow doubt.

pairs.tendency: A power sent by post works once, and the other player has to wait to see its effect.
pros: A power can arrive with a letter.
Players think carefully about when to send.
cons: A power may arrive too late.
The wait for a reply is long.

pairs.tendency: A power left by the absent player works once, and the others decide when it fires.
pros: An absent player still has a say.
The group decides together.
cons: The power cannot be changed.
The wrong moment may waste it.

pairs.tendency: The game master gives each player one power and decides when it can fire.
pros: A power is part of the story.
The master controls the pace.
cons: The master may be asked to rule on each use.
Players rely on the master to be fair.

pairs.tendency: A power is shown in a public place, and passers-by can use it one time before the marker leaves.
pros: Anyone can have a turn with it.
Onlookers see how it works.
cons: A passer-by may waste it.
The marker can be lost in the crowd.

pairs.tendency: The lone player holds one big power, and the others each hold a small one. Each works once.
pros: A power helps the lone player hold on.
Players see who has used what.
cons: The group may spend powers all at once.
The lone player may wait too long.

pairs.tendency: Playing against the pack, you hold one power. Once it is used, the marker goes.
pros: A power can rescue a run.
You choose the moment alone.
cons: Spend it early and the rest of the game has no rescue.
Nobody can tell you when to use it.

pairs.tendency: A power fixes a single throw or draw. Luck does the rest.
pros: A power is a small shield.
Players watch for the lowest throw.
cons: The power may never be needed.
A used power leaves the dice in charge.

pairs.tendency: A power adds one more way to soften a low roll, on top of the usual fixes. It works once.
pros: A power is a spare fix.
Players choose among the fixes.
cons: The fixes pile up and slow the turn.
A power kept too long may be forgotten.

pairs.tendency: A power can undo one piece of ill luck, once, in a game of mostly choices.
pros: A power guards against ill luck.
Players hold it back for a big swing.
cons: Using it on a small loss leaves nothing for a big one.
Skilled players may never need it.

pairs.tendency: A power is the only thing that bends the rules, once per player, in a game with no luck.
pros: A power is the only surprise.
Rivals watch for the turn it comes.
cons: A power spent early gives the other player the rest.
Players spend their thinking on the power.

pairs.tendency: To read the sign again, a power can force one re-throw or re-draw, and its marker is taken away.
pros: A power lets a player ask again.
Players talk about the two readings.
cons: The second reading may differ.
A power used on a clear sign wastes the chance.

pairs.tendency: A power calls the group back into step one time, and the marker goes.
pros: A power helps the group sync.
Players feel the shift.
cons: A power used when everyone is in step does nothing.
A used power leaves the group to find its own way.

pairs.tendency: A power can change one roll on the story table or ask for a second, once.
pros: A power edits the story.
Players choose the roll to change.
cons: A second roll may be no closer.
Changing a small roll gains little.

pairs.tendency: All powers are visible, so everyone knows who can still use one and when.
pros: Powers are open.
Players plan around the markers.
cons: Nobody gets a surprise.
Players may hold on until others spend theirs.

pairs.tendency: A power may be kept face down beside the cards, so nobody knows who still holds one.
pros: A hidden power adds a surprise.
Players guess who holds one.
cons: A hand may hold a power that is never played.
Players cannot tell when a rival is bluffing.

pairs.tendency: A power belongs to a secret role, and using it can show the role.
pros: A power may hide a role.
Players try to match powers to roles.
cons: A power used in the open gives away the role.
Others hold back until a power is shown.

pairs.tendency: A power reveals one clue or hides one, and the marker is taken away afterwards.
pros: A power turns up a clue.
Players weigh when to ask.
cons: A clue that was hidden is not recovered.
A power used on the wrong thread is lost.

pairs.tendency: A player can hint at a power they do not have, or hide one they do. A real power works only once.
pros: A power can back a bluff.
Players watch for a bluff.
cons: A false claim is caught when the power fails.
Players may not believe a real power.

pairs.tendency: A stuck player can spend a power on one hint about the secret rule, and the marker goes.
pros: A power opens a rule.
Players use it when stuck.
cons: A hint may be too small to help.
Without another hint, the rule stays hidden.

pairs.tendency: The player who knows can say one plain word by spending a power, and the marker is gone.
pros: A power breaks the silence.
The guessers hear a clue.
cons: The word may be used too soon.
Without it the player is back to hints.

pairs.tendency: A power turns over a hidden region or lets a player look ahead, and then its marker goes.
pros: A power opens the map.
Players choose which region to see.
cons: The look may show nothing of use.
Others see where the look was taken.

pairs.tendency: With one power, a player can swap into the open hand or peek at a closed one, after which the marker is gone.
pros: A power links two hands.
Players know one hand fully.
cons: A swap may hurt the owner of the open hand.
The power is easy to plan against.

pairs.tendency: A power shows a player one rival's score, and the marker is then taken away.
pros: A power peeks at a score.
Players choose whom to look at.
cons: A look at one score says little about the rest.
Others may guess who used it.

pairs.tendency: A power can be played on your turn or between turns, but only once, and then the marker leaves.
pros: A power is a plan for a turn.
Players watch for its timing.
cons: A turn spent on a power is not spent on a move.
Others wait while you decide.

pairs.tendency: Powers are revealed at the same moment, so everyone learns who used one.
pros: Powers appear together.
Players see how many were played.
cons: Two players may use powers that cancel.
Choices have to be made without seeing the others.

pairs.tendency: A power can be used at any moment, so the quickest hand wins the chance.
pros: A power may arrive without warning.
Players keep a hand ready.
cons: A slow player misses the moment.
Players may trigger it by mistake.

pairs.tendency: A power can add some seconds to the clock or stop it, once. The marker goes afterwards.
pros: A power buys time.
Players use it on a tight turn.
cons: Using it on an easy turn is a waste.
Others see the clock stop and know a power was used.

pairs.tendency: A power can be used on one day of a long game, and then the marker goes.
pros: A power marks a day.
Players wait for the right day.
cons: A day may pass without using it.
A forgotten power is lost by default.

pairs.tendency: A power shortens one pause or lengthens it, and the marker is taken away.
pros: A power bends the slow pace.
Players think before breaking the calm.
cons: Using it breaks the calm.
The slow rhythm can make the power feel out of place.

pairs.tendency: For one round, a power slows the game down. After that the marker is gone.
pros: A power gives a breath.
Players save it for the rush.
cons: The rush returns after the round.
Used before the rush, it is gone when the pace peaks.

pairs.tendency: A power gives a player an extra go, or takes one away, and its marker leaves.
pros: A power adds a turn.
Players plan a chain of moves.
cons: A power used on top of a lucky turn is easy to waste.
Others stop you from reaching your next turn.

pairs.tendency: A power belongs to one stage and works once there. Then the marker is gone.
pros: A power marks a stage.
Players plan across the stages.
cons: A power for the first stage is gone for the second.
A stage may end before it is used.

pairs.tendency: A power stands for a rare event in the system, such as a flood, and works once.
pros: A power is an event.
Players see its effects on the system.
cons: The event cannot be repeated.
Players may argue about when it would really occur.

pairs.tendency: Each group has a power tied to its role, such as a farmers' strike, that works once.
pros: Powers fit the roles.
Players see what each group can do.
cons: A group that spends its power is left with nothing.
A group with little power is easy to overlook.

pairs.tendency: One player can take more from the shared pool by spending a power, which then goes.
pros: A power takes extra.
Players watch the pool drop.
cons: Others may take extra too.
A power used late finds an empty pool.

pairs.tendency: A power used now shows its effect some rounds later, and the marker is gone at once.
pros: A power plants a delayed result.
Players wait to see what it does.
cons: The effect may come when it is no use.
It is hard to link the effect to the power.

pairs.tendency: A power lets a player try a new rule for one round, and the marker leaves after.
pros: A power runs a test.
Players see a rule at work.
cons: A rule tried for one round may not show much.
Players may not agree on what the test showed.

pairs.tendency: After play, players talk about when they used their powers and what happened.
pros: Powers give players something to talk about.
The talk turns timing into a lesson.
cons: Some powers were never used.
Players may remember choices differently.

pairs.tendency: A power makes a change that cannot be undone, such as tearing a card. The marker is gone too.
pros: A power leaves a mark.
Players see the result for the next game.
cons: An error carries into the next game.
A power used on a whim cannot be taken back.

pairs.tendency: The powers in the rules make a point, such as who gets a one-time rescue and who does not.
pros: Powers say who counts.
Players may notice who got which.
cons: Some players never see the point.
Players who get less may complain.

pairs.tendency: A power is tied to a real promise, such as a favour owed, and works once.
pros: A power carries a real cost.
Players think before using it.
cons: A used promise has to be kept.
Friends may feel strain over a power.

pairs.tendency: A power turns a value, such as kindness, into points a single time, and its marker is removed.
pros: A power turns a value into a score.
Players notice what the score misses.
cons: Players may track the score and forget the value.
Players may use the power only for the points.

pairs.tendency: A power stands for a change that may come in the future, such as a new law, and works once.
pros: A power tries out a change.
Players see how it feels.
cons: Once used, the change cannot be tried again.
The group may be unsure what the change means.

pairs.tendency: After you roll, you offer two ways to spend the number, and the other player picks one or turns both down. The dice set how far you go and your rival helps set where.
pros: The dice and a rival both shape each move.
A roll always leaves a choice to talk over.
cons: Every move waits on a reply.
A high roll can be undone by a refusal.

pairs.tendency: You hold up two cards you could keep, and the next player picks which one you get before the rest go on. Each pick is made by someone else's hand.
pros: Players learn what their neighbour wants to keep.
Every pick can shape another player's hand.
cons: Each pick takes two steps.
You may end up with the card you wanted less.

pairs.tendency: You name a price for the item, and the other player takes the deal or says no. A refusal tells everyone what that price is worth to them.
pros: Prices come out of real replies.
Refusals show what a player values.
cons: Offers can pile up with no sale.
Slow when several players want one item.

pairs.tendency: Each time you want to stop and keep your points, the other player can tell you to go on, and you have to take another risk. Their no puts your winnings back on the table.
pros: Stopping becomes something to argue for.
A lead can be pushed into danger.
cons: A cautious player loses control of when to stop.
Losing a pile of points to someone else's reply feels sharp.

pairs.tendency: You offer to move into an area, and the other player lets you in or keeps you out. Offering two areas lets them steer you to the one they care about least.
pros: Map fights go through asking.
Players learn which areas matter to each other.
cons: A refused move wastes the turn.
Fights over one area can drag on.

pairs.tendency: You put a worker on a spot and offer a second spot as a swap, and the other player picks which one you keep. A spot someone wants badly can be taken for the price of a favour.
pros: Spots turn into things to trade.
Players see what each other needs.
cons: A turn can stall on one spot.
A player with no spare spot has no way to bargain.

pairs.tendency: Your tile can go in two places, and the other player picks one. They may place you in a spot that breaks your line.
pros: Both players have a hand in each pattern.
Players watch each other's shapes closely.
cons: A neat plan can be spoiled by one pick.
Long thinking before each offer.

pairs.tendency: You show two cards you might play, and the other player picks which one comes down. The one left stays in your hand, and they know it.
pros: Each play tells a rival something.
Saved cards have more weight.
cons: A plan for a card can be taken away.
Your hand is read by the player who picks.

pairs.tendency: To lead a trick you offer two cards, and the other player says which one goes down. A low card they pick can lose a trick you hoped to win.
pros: Leading is a shared choice.
Players watch what the other offers.
cons: Winning a trick can depend on someone else's pick.
Picks cannot be taken back once the trick is out.

pairs.tendency: Your offered move becomes one more deal. The other player can refuse it, then name what it would cost to agree.
pros: Moves can be bought and sold.
Players learn what they will pay.
cons: Talk can run longer than the game.
A player with nothing to offer gets refused.

pairs.tendency: Of the two cards you offer to take, the other player picks one. The card they pick can break the set you were building.
pros: Players see each other's sets.
Choices carry a clue.
cons: Plans for a set can be cut off.
A set can finish late.

pairs.tendency: You show two places where your tile could go, and the other player chooses. The map ends up shaped by two people's ideas.
pros: Both players lay down the map.
Players pull the map towards their own roads.
cons: Roads can end up where nobody planned.
Placing a tile takes two rounds of talk.

pairs.tendency: You sing out a line, and the other player can answer it or ask for another. The chain only grows when both agree.
pros: Each line is a small test of a partner.
Players learn each other's style.
cons: A refusal stops the chain.
Waiting for a reply can break the flow.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move with a card or a gesture, and the other player nods or shakes their head. No word is spoken, so a head shake carries all the meaning.
pros: Every small signal counts.
Players pay close attention to each other.
cons: Offers can be misread.
A shake of the head can end a plan.

pairs.tendency: You offer a new rule, and the other player accepts it, turns it down, or picks the milder of two versions you gave. Two players end up writing the rules together.
pros: Neither player owns the rules.
New rules are tested before they stay.
cons: Rule talk can take over the game.
Players can stop to argue over each word.

pairs.tendency: Your character asks for something, and the other player decides in character whether to agree. The answer shapes the story as much as your request.
pros: Every scene is shared.
Characters can surprise their players.
cons: Scenes can stall on a refusal.
A shy player may find it hard to say no.

pairs.tendency: You offer two feats, such as pulling a block or flicking a striker, and the other player picks which one you attempt. They choose the harder one if they like.
pros: Players pick risks for each other.
Everyone watches every try.
cons: A shaky hand gets the harder job.
The tower can fall because of someone else's pick.

pairs.tendency: You draw a river on the sheet, and the other player can leave it or say where it goes instead. What ends up on the sheet was decided by two people.
pros: The map belongs to both players.
Places get names and reasons.
cons: A drawing can be undone by a refusal.
The map can wander off from where it began.

pairs.tendency: Each time a message is passed on, the next player may refuse it or pick between two forms the sender offers. The message that arrives has been through many hands.
pros: Each player leaves a mark on the message.
Each link of the chain makes a choice.
cons: The message can drift far from the start.
A refused message can stop the chain.

pairs.tendency: You offer two sets of cards to pass, and the other player picks which set they take. The cards you keep depend on their pick.
pros: Players read each other's choices.
Passing becomes a small contest.
cons: You cannot plan what you keep.
The pick takes extra time before play.

pairs.tendency: One player sets up the board and the other picks a side, and then the setter also offers the move to follow. Both rules give the second player a choice, so the first player plans against two choices at once.
pros: Both players aim to keep things level.
The second player has a real voice.
cons: The first player has little room to lean one way.
Setting up can take longer than playing.

pairs.tendency: When a piece reaches the far end, you offer two pieces it could become and the other player picks. A rival can choose the one that least suits your plan.
pros: A promotion is no longer a sure gain.
Rivals watch the far end of the board.
cons: Pieces can turn into something you did not plan for.
A race to the end may not pay off.

pairs.tendency: A runner offers the flag to two teammates and the other team decides who takes the next leg. The race then depends on a rival's guess.
pros: Legs are shared between teams.
Runners are watched with care.
cons: A fast runner can be held back.
The race stops while the choice is made.

pairs.tendency: You offer to put a stone in your shape, and the other player may turn it down and send you elsewhere. They can block the last stone you need.
pros: Shapes get built under pressure.
Blocks and offers sit side by side.
cons: A shape can stay one stone short.
Your plans are open to the other player.

pairs.tendency: You offer which card to lead, and the other player picks the one that wins a prize card. The named cards give each offer a clear price.
pros: Prize cards raise the stakes of each pick.
Players watch for the named cards.
cons: A prize card may go to the player who picks.
A pick can lose a prize you hoped to win.

pairs.tendency: Two of the shared cards are on offer to you, and the other player picks which one you may use. The one you do not get stays in the middle for everyone.
pros: Shared cards become a small bargain.
Each pick gives away a plan.
cons: You may get the card you need less.
Sets can be built on guesses.

pairs.tendency: You offer to split the pot, and the other player accepts, or says no and lets it grow. A refusal makes the next round worth more.
pros: A refusal can build a bigger prize.
Players weigh a sure share against a larger pot.
cons: A no can leave both with nothing this round.
The pot can grow while people wait.

pairs.tendency: You name two pits you could sow from, and the other player picks one. The last seed lands where their pick leads it.
pros: A pit turns into a shared choice.
Players count seeds ahead of the move.
cons: A tempting pit can be taken away.
Counting every option takes time.

pairs.tendency: You offer to swap your hand for the spare one, and the other player can agree or say no. The spare hand stays face down, so both are guessing.
pros: The spare hand becomes a bargaining chip.
Swaps cost a little trust.
cons: A refusal leaves the spare hand unused.
A swap may hand you a hand that scores less than the one you gave up.

pairs.tendency: You offer two routes, and one passes a square that sends pieces back. The other player picks, and the choice shows what they think of you.
pros: Squares gain a second use.
Players learn each other's routes.
cons: A trap can be picked out for you.
Offers get slow when every square has a rule.

pairs.tendency: You want to buy a unit. The other player says yes, says no, or picks the cheaper of two you can afford, so the price list becomes something to argue over.
pros: Spending is open to both players.
Prices say what each side values.
cons: A plan can be stopped at the shop.
Buying takes extra turns.

pairs.tendency: You offer two ways to share out your forces, and the other player picks one. Their pick shows where they plan to split their own.
pros: Players learn where the other is thin.
Splits become guesses.
cons: A split you liked can be taken away.
A lopsided split may show your plan.

pairs.tendency: Before the signal comes, you offer two places to stand, and the other player picks which one you aim for. The signal then catches you where they sent you.
pros: Where you stand is a shared decision.
Players watch each other closely.
cons: A slow player gets sent far.
A refusal wastes the last few seconds.

pairs.tendency: You put back two cards, and the other player says which one you may exchange. Some swaps need their yes as well.
pros: Swaps become small deals.
Players read each other's hands.
cons: A hand can be held back by a refusal.
A swap that is refused wastes the turn.

pairs.tendency: You say you want the discard pile, and the other player can refuse because the top card suits them. The pile grows until someone gets it.
pros: The pile becomes something to fight over.
Players watch every discard.
cons: A big pile can go to the wrong player.
Many cards can sit unused.

pairs.tendency: You offer two suits as trump, and the other player picks. Their pick can make your low trumps useless.
pros: The trump is chosen by both players.
Players show which suit they hold.
cons: A plan can lose its trump.
Naming the suit takes a pause before play.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move for each of the two boards, and the other player picks which board gets it. You attack on one and defend on the other, while they decide which.
pros: Two boards give a lot to pick from.
Players watch both boards.
cons: A move goes to the board you did not choose.
Keeping track of two games takes effort.

pairs.tendency: You play a wild card as one card. The other player can refuse, and then it counts as a different one. A card that can be anything is no longer yours alone.
pros: A wild card becomes a bargain.
Players see how others read their cards.
cons: A set can be ruined by a refusal.
A wild card can lose its value.

pairs.tendency: You offer two lines, and one runs off the right edge to come back on the left. The other player picks, and may send you round the board.
pros: The edges give extra routes.
Players watch both sides of the board.
cons: A line can come back at the wrong place.
Offers get long to explain.

pairs.tendency: You ask a question with a yes or no answer. The other player can answer it, or turn it down and ask you to try another.
pros: Questions can be shaped by the one answering.
Players learn to word questions with care.
cons: A refused question uses a turn.
A secret can stay safe for a long time.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move towards the finish, and the other player lets you go or holds you back. Your lead is only as safe as their next reply.
pros: The leader can be slowed by a reply.
Every move is watched.
cons: A runner can be held back.
The race can stop on a refusal.

pairs.tendency: Offered a scoring move, the other player can take it or pick a smaller one. They can pick the version that gives you the fewest points.
pros: Scores get shaped by both players.
Players learn each other's preferences.
cons: A big score can shrink in an instant.
The total is hard to guess.

pairs.tendency: You offer two moves, and one puts you in danger. The other player picks, and may pick the one that knocks you out.
pros: Every offer hints at who is next.
Players watch each other's pieces.
cons: A trap can be set for you.
A knocked-out player waits a long time.

pairs.tendency: Teammates offer moves to each other and a teammate can say no or pick a different one. The team stays alive only when the replies fit the danger.
pros: Each move gets a second look.
Players share ideas openly.
cons: One refusal can lose the game for everyone.
Debate can eat the time left.

pairs.tendency: A teammate offers a move toward the goal and another says yes or no. The goal gets closer only when both agree.
pros: Everyone has a part in each step.
Plans are talked over.
cons: Firm opinions can slow a turn.
One quiet player can go unheard.

pairs.tendency: Your offers hide what you want, and the other player's replies show what they want. Each yes or no gives a clue about a secret goal.
pros: Goals leak out through choices.
Players try to read each other.
cons: An offer can give your goal away.
A reply can mislead someone for turns.

pairs.tendency: You offer the next event in the story, and the other player lets it happen or picks a different turn. The ending comes from both of you.
pros: The story is made by both players.
Players learn what the other would write.
cons: A turn can be rewritten by a refusal.
The story may circle for a while.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move and the other player replies, and neither is aiming at a win. The talk about offers and refusals becomes the thing to look at afterwards.
pros: Offers can be tried for their own sake.
Players notice how each other decides.
cons: There is nothing to settle a disagreement.
A game can stop without a clear ending.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a goal of their own, and the say lets one player steer another away from it. Someone aiming to save one piece may be offered a way to lose it.
pros: Players learn each other's aims.
Offers carry a goal with them.
cons: A goal can be blocked by a reply.
Two players can end the game with unequal results.

pairs.tendency: You offer moves, and the other player picks the one that keeps them safe. The game goes on until someone loses, so each reply can protect or put someone at risk.
pros: Every pick can push the loss onto someone else.
Players watch who is left exposed.
cons: A safe player can steer the game.
The last few turns can feel slow.

pairs.tendency: A refusal could stop play, so offers get made to be accepted. Players try to keep the exchange alive.
pros: Offers are made with the other player in mind.
The game has no clear end.
cons: A player can lose interest in a game that does not end.
Refusals have to be used with care.

pairs.tendency: Moves are offered and answered, and no answer leads to a win. The offers and refusals go round with no end in sight.
pros: Players find out what a game does without a prize.
Offers can be about the exchange.
cons: The game offers nothing to reach.
Players may feel they have no way to finish.

pairs.tendency: A friend sits beside you and picks which of your two offered moves you make against the cards. You are still playing alone, but with someone else's hand on the choice.
pros: A solo game gets a second mind.
Players talk over the layout.
cons: The friend can steer you into a stuck table.
The choice slows a fast solo game.

pairs.tendency: After each short game, the loser offers how the next one starts and the winner picks or refuses. Over several games, that shapes who is ahead.
pros: Each game sets up the next.
Players pick up each other's habits.
cons: A winner can control later games.
A run of refusals can stretch the match.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move that avoids points, and the other player picks one that gives you some. Each pick can push a point onto you.
pros: Players try to hand points to each other.
Every pick has a reason.
cons: A safe offer can be turned against you.
Points can build up on one player.

pairs.tendency: Of the two moves you offer, one lands exactly on the target. The other player picks the other one, and you miss by one.
pros: A close finish can be pulled away.
Players count each other's steps.
cons: A needed number can be refused.
The last step can take many turns.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move that gives something away, and the other player can refuse it. Keeping a gift you did not want can slow your loss.
pros: A refusal can work against the person who gave.
Players try to hand things over.
cons: A turned-down offer feels backwards.
The aim can be hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: Players build their own things side by side, and the only place they touch is the offer. A move is shown to the neighbour for a yes or no.
pros: Each player has a small link to the other.
Players learn what the neighbour is building.
cons: One neighbour can hold up a build.
The game can feel like two games with a gap.

pairs.tendency: You offer an attack, and the other player picks which of two targets takes the hit. They may send it to a piece that matters least to them.
pros: A hit has a choice in it.
Rivals can bargain over blows.
cons: A planned attack can be turned aside.
A refused attack leaves the turn empty.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move on the board and the other player picks where it lands. Their pick changes the board you both play on.
pros: Players change the board together.
Moves affect others without a direct attack.
cons: A wall may end up in the wrong place.
Players can blame each other for the board.

pairs.tendency: The whole team plays against the game, and each player offers a move to the others. A move happens only when the others agree.
pros: Moves are talked over.
Players share the work.
cons: A loud talker can lead the team.
Time goes on arguing over one move.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move that helps everyone, and the other player can turn it down because it helps you more. The group hears the reason.
pros: Players weigh the group's gain against their own.
Replies tell players about private aims.
cons: A refusal can feel like a hidden aim.
The group can stall.

pairs.tendency: One player on each team holds the say, and the opposing side offers moves to them. Teammates can only urge their player to accept or refuse.
pros: Teams talk through each reply.
One player carries a lot for the team.
cons: The say can feel like a heavy job.
A single reply can turn a team's plan.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move and the other player turns it down. A refusal could be caution or sabotage, and nobody knows which.
pros: Every refusal gets a second look.
Players learn who answers who.
cons: A true team player can be doubted.
Doubt can slow a turn.

pairs.tendency: Your offer goes in a letter, and the reply takes days. The answer comes back as a yes, a no, or a different move.
pros: Each reply is read with care.
Players think before they write.
cons: Waiting for an answer can take a week.
A game can be slow to finish.

pairs.tendency: A ghost or a faraway player has the say, and gives it through a note or a hint. The players at the table have to read it.
pros: The absent player stays part of the game.
Players read each note closely.
cons: A note can be misread.
The say comes late or not at all.

pairs.tendency: The game master hears each player's offer and accepts it, or picks between two. The world answers each move with a decision.
pros: The world responds to players.
A story can go in many ways.
cons: The master can hold up the game.
One person holds a lot of say.

pairs.tendency: A passer-by joins in and has a say about someone's move in the street. Offers are made to whoever is nearby.
pros: Anyone can add a say.
Games draw a small crowd.
cons: Replies come from strangers.
Onlookers can get in the way of play.

pairs.tendency: The lone player offers a move and the group picks one, or turns it down together. Everyone else shares one reply.
pros: The group acts as one voice.
The lone player faces a real answer.
cons: The group may argue over its reply.
The lone player waits while they talk.

pairs.tendency: A friend watches your game against the pack and picks which of two moves you make. Afterwards you compare how it went with a game played alone.
pros: A solo game turns into a pair.
Results can be compared.
cons: The friend's pick can feel like a trick.
Pairs need someone near.

pairs.tendency: The dice decide what you get and the other player decides if you use it. They can refuse the lucky result you rolled.
pros: A game of luck gets a little control.
Players still have something to decide.
cons: A lucky roll can be wasted.
Luck and a refusal can pull in different ways.

pairs.tendency: A low roll can be softened by offering two ways to use it, and the other player picks one. The way to soften luck depends on a rival.
pros: Players can work around a low roll.
Offers show how to handle risk.
cons: The softer option can be taken away.
A rival may pick the harder way.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move that depends on a small lucky draw, and the other player picks between two such moves. Most of the choice stays with skill.
pros: Skill decides most of the offers.
Luck stays a small part.
cons: A skilful offer can be turned down.
Luck can still upset a plan.

pairs.tendency: With no dice to hide behind, you offer two moves and the other player picks. The pick comes from thought alone.
pros: Every pick is down to thinking.
Players read each other's plans.
cons: A wrong offer is easy to see.
Long pauses before each offer.

pairs.tendency: You throw the dice to ask a question, and the other player picks which reading you follow. The throw is fixed, and both of you decide what it means.
pros: Meaning is decided together.
Players talk about what the throw says.
cons: A reading can be argued.
The sign can feel tied to a person's view.

pairs.tendency: You and the other player try to feel when the other will offer or reply. A well-timed yes comes just as the offer is made.
pros: Players learn each other's timing.
A shared rhythm can grow.
cons: A reply that arrives early breaks the feeling.
Offers cannot be worked out by thinking.

pairs.tendency: You roll to look up what happens, and the other player picks between two table results. The dice write part of the story and a rival writes the rest.
pros: The story has more than one author.
Dice and a person both decide.
cons: A roll can be rewritten.
Players may disagree about the result.

pairs.tendency: Every card and piece is in view, so the other player knows what each offer leads to. Their yes or no comes from seeing everything.
pros: Replies are made with open eyes.
Players can plan far ahead.
cons: Nothing is hidden, so surprises are few.
Players can take a long time to reply.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move without showing your cards, and the other player says yes or no with half the facts. Their reply may be a guess.
pros: Offers can carry a bluff.
Replies reveal what players suspect.
cons: A guess can be wrong.
Players may refuse offers that were true.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move, and the other player cannot tell if your role is friend or foe. A refusal can mean they suspect you.
pros: Offers are tested for trust.
Players read replies as clues.
cons: An honest offer can be refused.
Suspicion can build over turns.

pairs.tendency: Each offer and each refusal gives a clue about what the other player knows. A player works out the hidden answer from the replies they get.
pros: Replies are clues.
Players study each other's choices.
cons: A misleading reply can send the search the wrong way.
Clues can be read in more than one way.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move that sounds like a winning one when it is not, and the other player decides whether to believe it. A refusal tells you they doubted.
pros: Offers can be false.
Players study each other's faces.
cons: A bluff can be called early.
A true offer can be doubted.

pairs.tendency: The other player has a secret rule, and their yes or no teaches you what it is. You find the rule by getting refused.
pros: Replies hold the rule.
Players learn by trial.
cons: A refusal gives no reason.
Newcomers can feel lost.

pairs.tendency: The one who knows the answer can only reply to offers with a yes, a no, or a pick between two hints. Everyone else offers guesses and learns from the replies.
pros: Hints come from choosing.
Guesses have a way to be tested.
cons: The player who knows can feel torn.
The answer may take many offers to find.

pairs.tendency: You offer a place to explore and the other player picks where you look first. A refusal sends you somewhere you did not choose.
pros: Exploring becomes a joint plan.
Each reveal is a surprise to both.
cons: The hidden map is uncovered by someone else's pick.
A promising spot can be skipped.

pairs.tendency: One hand lies open, and you offer to play from it. The other player can say yes or no to that card.
pros: Open cards show the offer.
Players can plan around the open hand.
cons: The open hand can be used against its owner.
Offers from the open hand are easy to refuse.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move without saying how much it earns, and the other player says yes without knowing its value. Nobody can add up who is ahead.
pros: Replies are made with some doubt.
Players guess at scores.
cons: A refusal can throw away points.
Nobody is sure who leads.

pairs.tendency: In your turn you offer, and in theirs they answer or offer back. Each turn holds a small exchange of yes and no.
pros: Turns have a clear shape.
Players know when to speak.
cons: Each turn takes longer.
A refusal can run into the next turn.

pairs.tendency: Everyone picks in secret, then reveals together, but one player's pick is held until the other has said yes. So the reveal is not quite all at once.
pros: Picks come out together.
A reveal still has a reply to wait for.
cons: A reveal can stall.
Players cannot all move at the same speed.

pairs.tendency: Anyone can offer a move at any moment, and the other player says yes or no as fast as they can. Quick replies win the offers.
pros: Offers fly back and forth.
Quick thinkers get ahead.
cons: Slower players get left out.
Too many offers can pile up at once.

pairs.tendency: You have twenty seconds to make your offer, and the other player has a short time to reply. A late reply counts as a yes or a no, whichever the rules say.
pros: Offers and replies are quick.
Players decide on the spot.
cons: A hurried reply is easy to regret.
The clock can cut off a plan.

pairs.tendency: An offer sent in the morning gets its reply by evening. A game can run for weeks of offers and replies.
pros: Players think about each reply.
A slow game fits into a busy week.
cons: A reply can arrive after you have changed your mind.
Waiting can last days.

pairs.tendency: A pause comes before each offer and each reply, so each yes or no is taken slowly. The slow pace gives the say more weight.
pros: Replies are given time.
Players notice small changes.
cons: Each exchange takes very long.
A quick player may lose patience.

pairs.tendency: The clock shrinks as the game goes on, so replies come faster and faster. Late in the game a yes or no has to come in a moment.
pros: The game picks up speed.
Players learn to answer fast.
cons: Late replies are rushed.
The end comes in a heap of offers.

pairs.tendency: You land on a space that gives another go, and you offer a move for it. The other player can refuse it, so the extra turn is lost.
pros: A lucky turn can be turned down.
Players weigh each extra turn.
cons: One reply can undo a gain.
A series of extra turns can last a long time.

pairs.tendency: In the first stage you offer picks and the other player replies. In the second stage you play with what you were given.
pros: The first stage sets up the second.
Players learn each other's choices early.
cons: An early refusal can shape the whole game.
Stage one can take as long as stage two.

pairs.tendency: A system such as a village's water has two users, and one offers a use that the other can accept or turn down. Each yes or no sets how the system works.
pros: The system runs on agreements.
Players see how choices carry on.
cons: A refusal can leave a field dry.
The model can grow hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: Each player plays a group, such as farmers or a council, and the other group has a say on your offer. A reply comes from what that group needs.
pros: Replies come from a point of view.
Players see the problem from another side.
cons: A group can be outvoted.
Talk can go on without a choice.

pairs.tendency: You ask to take water from the shared well, and the other player can say no. A refusal protects the well for everyone.
pros: Takers need a reply.
Players talk about sharing.
cons: A no can leave someone short of water.
A shared source can run out in an argument.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move whose effect shows in a few rounds, and the other player replies without seeing the result. Both of you find out later.
pros: Replies are made without knowing.
Players learn from what comes back.
cons: A yes can cause a problem later.
The cause of a result is hard to trace.

pairs.tendency: You propose a new rule and the other player accepts a trial of it. After some rounds both can see what the rule changed.
pros: A rule gets a trial run first.
Players see the effect of a change.
cons: A refused rule is never tried.
A trial rule can be forgotten.

pairs.tendency: After play you talk about the offers and the replies, and why each was made. The refusals are often the first thing people discuss.
pros: Replies can be explained.
Players hear each other's reasons.
cons: A reply can look different in hindsight.
Talking afterwards takes time.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move that tears a card or sticks a mark on the board, and the other player says yes or no. Once they agree, it cannot be undone.
pros: A yes is a serious step.
Players think before replying.
cons: A yes cannot be taken back.
A board can fill with old marks.

pairs.tendency: The offer and the reply are part of the rules, so the game says something about who gets to speak. A game where one player always replies makes a point about power.
pros: The rules show who has a voice.
Players notice how the say is shared.
cons: The argument can be missed.
Players may disagree with it.

pairs.tendency: The other player's reply to your offer can cost a real favour or a real promise. A refusal in the game becomes a refusal in life.
pros: Replies matter beyond the table.
Players take offers seriously.
cons: A refusal can hurt a friendship.
A player may say yes just to stay friendly.

pairs.tendency: You offer a move that earns points for something such as kindness, and the other player says yes or no. Players chase the points and forget the value behind them.
pros: Replies show what a point stands for.
Players see how a number shapes choices.
cons: A refusal can cost points for a kind reason.
Players can offer moves just for the points.

pairs.tendency: You offer a way to share work in a village that does not exist yet, and the other player says yes or no. Each reply shows how that future might feel.
pros: Replies feel like a real meeting.
Players try out a way of living together.
cons: A refusal can end an idea early.
A made-up future can feel odd.

pairs.tendency: A whisper is passed along while pieces move around a path, and each roll sends the next speaker forward. The message and the pieces travel together.
pros: A message gives the dice a story.
Players listen between moves.
cons: The message can reach the end of the path changed.
Players may talk instead of rolling.

pairs.tendency: A note goes round with the cards, and each player adds a word when they pass. The cards a player keeps show in how they change the note.
pros: The note carries clues about picks.
Players pick up hints between turns.
cons: A hint can lead a player astray.
The note slows the passing.

pairs.tendency: A bid is whispered from player to player until it reaches the auctioneer. It can arrive higher or lower than it left.
pros: Bids travel in secret.
Prices can shift on the way.
cons: A bid can arrive wrong.
The seller cannot check the source.

pairs.tendency: You whisper to the next player how far you plan to go, and they pass it on. A rumour of how much someone has risked spreads along the chain.
pros: News of a risk travels.
Players hear who is taking chances.
cons: A rumour can scare a player into stopping.
The truth may be lost before it arrives.

pairs.tendency: Orders for the armies are passed on by whisper from one player to the next. A message about an area may reach a general in the wrong form.
pros: Armies act on word of mouth.
Players learn to send short messages.
cons: A wrong order loses an area.
Nobody can check what was meant.

pairs.tendency: A note about which spot to take goes from worker to worker. By the time it arrives the spot may have gone.
pros: Players pass on tips.
A tip can save a turn.
cons: A tip can be out of date.
A message can send a worker to the wrong place.

pairs.tendency: A description of a pattern is whispered down the line, and the last player builds from what they heard. The builder sees how the pattern changed on the way.
pros: A pattern grows out of a message.
Players see how a shape can drift.
cons: The last tile may not match the first.
A long chain makes the pattern hard to recognise.

pairs.tendency: A whisper about what to keep in your hand passes round the table. A card you saved on a rumour may be one you did not need.
pros: Players trade hints about cards.
Hands can be shaped by a whisper.
cons: A hint can be wrong.
Players save cards for no reason.

pairs.tendency: A signal about a card is whispered along from partner to partner. The trick can be won or lost on how the message arrives.
pros: Partners can pass on news.
Players watch for signals.
cons: A signal can be changed on the way.
The rules may not allow it.

pairs.tendency: An offer is whispered along the table, and each player can change it a little before they pass it on. The deal you agree to may not be the one that was sent.
pros: Deals get passed along.
Players try to read the sender.
cons: A deal can shift by the time it arrives.
Trust in a deal can drop.

pairs.tendency: A whisper tells a player which cards you need for your set. The one at the end of the chain may have heard another colour.
pros: Players hear what others want.
Sets can be helped by a hint.
cons: A message can name the wrong card.
A whisper can reveal your set.

pairs.tendency: A message tells the next player where the road is meant to go. When the tile is placed, the map shows how far the message has changed.
pros: The map comes out of a chain of words.
Players share a plan with the next in line.
cons: A road can end up in the wrong field.
A message can be hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: One player calls a line and the answer is passed down the row before anyone replies. Each player hears only what came before.
pros: The chain gets longer each turn.
Each player adds a bit.
cons: A line can be changed by the time it comes back.
Nobody knows who changed it.

pairs.tendency: Nobody speaks, so the message is passed by a squeeze of the hand or a tap. Each player feels it and sends it on.
pros: A message goes round without a word.
Players learn to read touch.
cons: A squeeze can be misread.
A tap may be lost.

pairs.tendency: A rule change is whispered round the table, and each player passes on what they heard. The rule that arrives may not be the one that was made.
pros: Rule changes spread by word of mouth.
Players hear the rules in different ways.
cons: Players can end up playing different games.
Nobody can look up the real rule.

pairs.tendency: A character sends word to another character, and the players pass it along by whisper. The characters act on what they hear.
pros: A letter in a story can be a real thing.
Players carry news for their characters.
cons: A character can act on a changed message.
Players may lose the thread.

pairs.tendency: A message goes along the line while players balance a tower or flick a piece. Hands are busy while the ears take it in.
pros: Players do two things at once.
The message can be told while hands move.
cons: Hands can shake while listening.
A dropped block can lose the words.

pairs.tendency: A description of a place is whispered along, and the last player draws it. The map shows what the message turned into.
pros: The map grows out of a message.
Players can compare the drawing to the first words.
cons: A river can turn into a road.
Nobody can check against the first message.

pairs.tendency: A secret note goes with the cards each player passes on. The cards you receive may arrive with a hint about what to do.
pros: Notes tell what a pass means.
Players learn who sent what.
cons: A note can say the opposite of the cards.
You cannot check the note against the cards.

pairs.tendency: One player sets up the game and passes a note about it to the other, who then picks a side. The note tells what the setter thinks is even.
pros: The setter can describe their plan.
The second player picks with some knowledge.
cons: A note can bend the setup.
The picker cannot check the claim.

pairs.tendency: News of a piece reaching the far end travels by whisper around the table. By the time it arrives, the piece may have been taken.
pros: News of a promotion spreads.
Players learn who is close to the end.
cons: The message can be out of date.
A rumour of a promotion can scare a player.

pairs.tendency: The flag is handed on and a message goes with it. Each runner carries words along with the flag.
pros: A message can ride with a runner.
Teams have to speak quickly.
cons: A message can change during a run.
A hurried runner can mix it up.

pairs.tendency: A whisper tells your partner which shape to build, and it is passed on. A stone may end up outside the shape because of a changed word.
pros: Plans get passed between teammates.
Players share a goal.
cons: A word can move a stone.
A shape can be left unfinished.

pairs.tendency: A note tells which card is the prize, and it goes from player to player. Some players hear the wrong prize.
pros: Players hear about prize cards.
A hint can steer a trick.
cons: A false message can send a trick the wrong way.
Players may follow a rumour.

pairs.tendency: A message about the shared cards in the middle goes round the table. A player may use a card they heard wrongly described.
pros: Players pass on what they see.
A hint can help with a hand.
cons: A message can describe the wrong card.
Nobody checks until the cards turn.

pairs.tendency: How much each player has put in the pot is whispered from ear to ear. The pot can seem larger or smaller than it is.
pros: Players hear about the pot.
A story can make a pot look worth winning.
cons: Each teller can round it up or down.
A false report can cause a lost bet.

pairs.tendency: A whisper tells you which pit to sow from. It travels down the table and may change on the way.
pros: A message gives a first move.
Players hear about seeds and pits.
cons: A pit can be named wrongly.
The last seed can land somewhere unplanned.

pairs.tendency: A note says what is in the spare hand, and it is passed round before anyone takes it. The note may be right or wrong.
pros: Players hear about the spare hand.
A note can tempt a swap.
cons: A swap can be a mistake.
Nobody can check the spare hand until they take it.

pairs.tendency: A whisper warns of a trap on the track and is passed from player to player. The warning may arrive too late, or too changed to help.
pros: Warnings travel along the track.
Players hear about special squares.
cons: A warning can name the wrong square.
A message can arrive after the move.

pairs.tendency: Before you buy, the price of a unit reaches you by whisper. The price you hear may be higher or lower than the real one.
pros: Price news travels.
Players decide by word of mouth.
cons: You may pay more than you planned.
You may find out the real cost after you buy.

pairs.tendency: Each player passes on how a teammate split their forces. Your own split depends on what you heard.
pros: Players learn about each other's plans.
A message can help you split.
cons: A message can mislead a plan.
Forces may end up in the wrong place.

pairs.tendency: The signal is a whisper that goes round, and each player stops when it reaches them. The slowest to hear is the slowest to freeze.
pros: The signal moves from person to person.
Players listen all the time.
cons: A player at the end hears last.
A changed signal can cause the wrong stop.

pairs.tendency: Which card to put back is whispered down the line. A player who heard it wrong may swap a card they wanted.
pros: Players share swap advice.
Hands can change by word of mouth.
cons: A swap can come from a mistaken word.
A hand can lose the cards you wanted to a rumour.

pairs.tendency: Word of the top card of the pile goes round the table. You may take the pile for a card that is no longer there.
pros: News of the top card travels.
Players pick the pile with a plan.
cons: A card can change before you take the pile.
A message can send you for the wrong pile.

pairs.tendency: A whisper names the trump suit, and it goes from player to player. A player who heard the wrong suit plays a trick wrongly.
pros: The trump suit is learned by word of mouth.
Players listen for the suit.
cons: Players can end up with different trumps in mind.
A wrong trump can lose a trick.

pairs.tendency: A message is passed between the two boards, so what happens on one is told to the other. You hear about one game while you play the other.
pros: The boards are linked by words.
Players keep both games in mind.
cons: A report from one board may be wrong.
A message can come when you are busy with the other.

pairs.tendency: What a wild card stands for is whispered along. A card may arrive as something other than what was said.
pros: Players pass on what a wild card is.
A wild card can be told as a secret.
cons: A word can change a set.
A wild card can mean different things to different players.

pairs.tendency: A whisper tells which way a line will run, including off the edge. The listeners may not agree on where the line comes back.
pros: A message can describe the edge.
Players explain odd paths.
cons: A line can be heard wrongly.
The edge can confuse a message.

pairs.tendency: A question is whispered along to the player who knows the secret, who answers yes or no. The question may change on the way, so the answer fits a different one.
pros: Questions pass through a chain.
The answer is short and clear.
cons: A question can change on the way.
A yes can be about the wrong thing.

pairs.tendency: A whisper tells runners about the course ahead and is passed from player to player. A runner who hears wrongly takes a longer way.
pros: News of the track travels.
Runners can use a tip.
cons: A tip can send a runner the wrong way.
The leader may be the last to hear.

pairs.tendency: A message about a scoring chance goes round, and each player who hears it can use it. Points come to those who get the message whole.
pros: News of a scoring chance spreads.
Players share useful tips.
cons: A message may mislead.
A player may score on a changed rumour.

pairs.tendency: The name of who will be knocked out next goes down the line in a whisper. A rumour can make a player leave before they are in danger.
pros: News of danger travels.
Players use rumours to plan.
cons: A false report can push a player out.
A player may hear too late.

pairs.tendency: The team has to pass warnings about the danger by whisper, and everyone depends on them. If a warning is lost, the whole team can lose.
pros: Warnings go from one to another.
The team trusts its members.
cons: One garbled message can lose the game.
Players cannot check every message.

pairs.tendency: A message about the shared goal is passed round the team. Each player acts on the plan they heard.
pros: Everyone hears the goal.
The team learns to speak plainly.
cons: Someone down the line may hear a different plan.
Players may work towards different goals.

pairs.tendency: A message hints at what you want. By the time it has gone round, others may have learned your secret.
pros: Goals can be hinted at.
Players learn to say little.
cons: A message can give away a secret.
A hint can be misunderstood.

pairs.tendency: A line of the story is whispered round, and each player adds a bit before passing it on. The ending reflects every change.
pros: The story is written by a chain.
Each player adds a part.
cons: The story can drift from its start.
The ending may not match the opening.

pairs.tendency: A message goes round with no prize. At the end, the group looks at how it changed.
pros: The change in the message becomes the thing to see.
Players talk about what happened.
cons: There is nothing to win.
The game may have no clear end.

pairs.tendency: Each player sets a goal, and a message about those goals is passed round. You may find that others heard your goal wrongly.
pros: Players share what they want.
A message can help others help you.
cons: A goal can be changed by the way it is told.
Players may judge each other on a wrong message.

pairs.tendency: Who looks most likely to lose is whispered from player to player. A rumour can push everyone to avoid the player named.
pros: News of the likely loser travels.
Players react to a rumour.
cons: A false report can doom a player.
A player may be left out because of a changed word.

pairs.tendency: The message never ends, and each player takes it and sends it on. The game goes on as long as the whisper does.
pros: The game is a long chain.
Every player has a turn.
cons: The message can drift far.
There is no end to wait for.

pairs.tendency: A message goes round and round with no way to win. The game shows how a message changes when there is nothing to win.
pros: The message is the whole game.
Players see how a message changes.
cons: There is no prize.
Players may wonder what the game is for.

pairs.tendency: You play alone against the cards, and a message is passed to you from an earlier player, such as a note left in the box. You read it before you start.
pros: A note can help a solo player.
Players leave clues for each other.
cons: A note may be out of date.
The note cannot be checked against the cards.

pairs.tendency: After each game, the winner passes a note to the next game's players. The notes grow into a story across the match.
pros: Notes link the games.
A match gets a thread.
cons: A note can mislead.
The thread may fray across many games.

pairs.tendency: Where points are piling up is whispered from one player to the next. A rumour can make a player dodge points that were never there.
pros: News of points travels.
Players avoid danger by word of mouth.
cons: A false report can cost a player.
A player may take points while chasing a rumour.

pairs.tendency: The number you need to land on travels round in a whisper. The last player may hear the wrong number.
pros: Players share the target.
Tips help with the count.
cons: The target can arrive garbled.
A wrong number can overshoot the finish.

pairs.tendency: A whisper tells how to give everything away, and it passes along. A player might follow a changed tip and end up winning by mistake.
pros: Players share tips about losing.
A changed message can turn a plan on its head.
cons: A tip can undo your plan.
The aim can be hard to describe in a whisper.

pairs.tendency: Everyone builds their own thing, and the message is the only link. Each player hears something about the others' work.
pros: The message joins separate games.
Players learn about other builds.
cons: A message can describe the wrong build.
Players may copy what they hear.

pairs.tendency: A threat is whispered along to the player it is meant for. By the time it arrives, the threat may be larger, smaller or about someone else.
pros: Threats travel through the table.
Players choose targets by word of mouth.
cons: A threat can fall on the wrong person.
A rumour can start a fight.

pairs.tendency: News of a change on the board goes round by word of mouth. Players feel the change before they see it.
pros: Players hear about the board.
A tip can warn of a wall.
cons: The message can be wrong.
The board and the message may disagree.

pairs.tendency: Everyone is on one team, and the message is the team's only way to share a plan. A clear word can save the game.
pros: The team shares a plan.
Players speak carefully.
cons: A garbled message can lose the game for everyone.
The team cannot check what the last player heard.

pairs.tendency: A message about a shared plan goes round, and each player may add a private change. The plan that arrives has a little of everyone in it.
pros: The group shares a plan.
A message can carry private aims.
cons: A change may go unnoticed.
Players may suspect each other.

pairs.tendency: A team whispers a plan from player to player, while the other team tries to hear it. A plan that is too loud tells the rivals everything.
pros: A team plans in secret.
Players speak low.
cons: Rivals can overhear.
A plan can be lost between teammates.

pairs.tendency: The traitor is in the chain and can change the message before passing it on. Nobody can tell whether a change was a mistake.
pros: A message becomes a test.
Players look hard at who passed what.
cons: A traitor can twist a plan.
A true player can be blamed for a changed word.

pairs.tendency: Letters carry the moves, and a letter can carry a message for another player too. Each reply can take days to arrive.
pros: Letters carry both moves and news.
Waiting adds to the story.
cons: A letter can be lost.
A game can last a year.

pairs.tendency: The absent player speaks only through a message, and the table passes it on. The words can change before they arrive.
pros: The absent player stays in the game.
Players guess what they meant.
cons: A message can be misunderstood.
Nobody can ask the absent player.

pairs.tendency: The game master sends a message from the world, and the players pass it on to each other. The world is known only through what the players heard.
pros: The world reaches players by word of mouth.
Players tell each other what they know.
cons: A message can change the story.
The game master cannot be asked.

pairs.tendency: A message is passed along a street, and passers-by can add to it. The message that arrives has been in many mouths.
pros: Anyone can join the chain.
The message changes a lot.
cons: A crowd can lose the thread.
No one can trace the changes.

pairs.tendency: The group whispers a plan to each other, and the lone player tries to overhear. The group is spread out, so the message has to pass through many hands.
pros: The group has to speak low.
The lone player listens hard.
cons: A message can fall apart in a long chain.
The lone player may hear too much.

pairs.tendency: You play against the pack and pass a message to yourself, such as a note for the next game. The player who reads it later may not recall what it meant.
pros: A note joins separate games.
Players leave themselves clues.
cons: A note can be forgotten.
The note may read oddly later.

pairs.tendency: A whisper tells how the dice fell, and it travels round the table. Players cannot check a throw they did not see.
pros: News of the throws travels.
Players hear what luck brought.
cons: A throw can be reported wrongly.
Arguments about a throw have no answer.

pairs.tendency: Advice on softening a low roll is passed along. A player may use a tip that changed on the way.
pros: Tips about luck travel.
Players share ways to cope.
cons: A tip can fail.
The tip cannot be traced to its source.

pairs.tendency: A whisper shares a plan that depends on a small lucky draw. The plan may change on the way, but the lucky draw still falls as it does.
pros: Plans are shared.
Skill and luck both play a part.
cons: A plan can be spoiled by an unlucky draw.
A changed plan can be hard to correct.

pairs.tendency: A message shares a clever plan, and each player passes it on. Skill decides how well a player can use what they heard.
pros: Plans spread by word of mouth.
Players learn from each other.
cons: A plan can lose a step in the telling.
A wrong word can lose a long game.

pairs.tendency: The throw is read as a message, and the reading is passed along. Each player hears a different version of what the sign said.
pros: Readings travel.
Players talk about what a sign means.
cons: Each retelling moves the reading a little.
Players may disagree about the sign.

pairs.tendency: Players try to sense when the message will come, without any signal. The message arrives as a shared moment.
pros: Players learn each other's rhythm.
A message can feel natural.
cons: A late message breaks the feeling.
The rhythm is hard to keep with strangers.

pairs.tendency: The roll is looked up on a table, and the result is whispered along. The story told at the end is the story that was heard.
pros: Dice results travel as story.
Players hear the story in turn.
cons: A result can be changed in the telling.
The story at the end may not match the table.

pairs.tendency: Every piece can be seen, but the message still passes by whisper. A player can check the board against what they heard.
pros: Players can compare words to the board.
A wrong message is easy to find.
cons: A message adds little new.
Players may stop passing it.

pairs.tendency: A hint about your cards is whispered round the table. It may give away a hand, or be a bluff.
pros: Hints about hands move round.
Players read each other's words.
cons: A hint can give your hand away.
A hint can be a lie.

pairs.tendency: Hints about who is who go round the table. Players try to learn the secret roles from the changes.
pros: Roles are hinted at.
Players watch the chain.
cons: A hint can name the wrong person.
A secret can slip out.

pairs.tendency: A clue is whispered along the line and ends with the detective. The detective works out the answer from what came out at the end.
pros: A clue arrives from many mouths.
Players compare what they heard.
cons: A clue can be changed.
The detective cannot check the first words.

pairs.tendency: You send a false message and hope it travels. Each player decides whether to pass it on as it is.
pros: A bluff can spread.
Players learn to doubt a message.
cons: A bluff can come back at you.
A true message can be doubted.

pairs.tendency: A hint about the secret rule is whispered round. Players who hear it may follow a rule that has already changed.
pros: Hints about rules move round.
Players learn rules from each other.
cons: A hint can lead to the wrong rule.
Newcomers cannot check what they heard.

pairs.tendency: The one who knows the answer sends hints, and the players pass on what they think each hint means. The guesser gets a message that has been through many readings.
pros: Hints are passed round.
Players compare readings.
cons: A hint can lose its meaning.
The guesser may not hear the first hint.

pairs.tendency: Someone describes a place you have not seen, and the description is passed along. The place you reach may differ from what you heard.
pros: News of the map travels.
Players decide where to explore.
cons: A message can describe the wrong area.
A report can send you to an empty place.

pairs.tendency: A whisper describes the open hand and the cards on show. Players who cannot see it hear a version of it.
pros: Players describe what they see.
Open cards are shared.
cons: A description can leave out a card.
Players have to trust the one describing.

pairs.tendency: How others are scoring reaches you by whisper. Nobody can check a score, so the story decides who seems ahead.
pros: Players hear about scores.
A message sets who seems to lead.
cons: A score can be misreported.
Nobody can add up the truth.

pairs.tendency: The message moves one player at a time, with each turn adding a step. Players wait while their neighbour hears and passes it on.
pros: The message has a clear path.
Everyone knows whose turn it is to listen.
cons: Waiting for the message can be long.
The message may arrive after the play moves on.

pairs.tendency: Everyone whispers at once, so messages cross and mix. Each player hears a few and passes on what they caught.
pros: Many messages travel together.
Players listen hard.
cons: Messages can get mixed up.
A player cannot follow all of them.

pairs.tendency: Anyone may whisper at any time, so messages fly in every direction. The first to hear a message is the first to use it.
pros: Messages move fast.
Quick listeners gain.
cons: Messages can cross and change.
Slow players miss them.

pairs.tendency: The message has a few seconds at each stop. A player who runs out of time passes on whatever they have.
pros: Messages move quickly.
Players learn to say little.
cons: A rushed message can get muddled.
A word can be dropped.

pairs.tendency: A message travels over days, with a few players adding a word each morning. It may be changed a lot by the end of the week.
pros: A message grows over days.
Players think about each word.
cons: A message can be forgotten.
A long wait can wear down the words.

pairs.tendency: The message is passed slowly, with a breath between each word. The slow pace gives each player time to hear and think.
pros: Each word is heard clearly.
Players pay close attention.
cons: The message takes a long time.
Fast talkers get restless.

pairs.tendency: The message has to be passed faster and faster as the game goes on. Near the end the words are rushed.
pros: Passing speeds up.
Players learn to be brief.
cons: Late messages get muddled.
The end comes in a blur.

pairs.tendency: A lucky throw gives you another go, and you pass on a message during it. Many messages can move before other players act.
pros: A lucky player can send many words.
The chain moves quickly.
cons: One player can control what travels.
Others hear little until later.

pairs.tendency: In the first stage a message is passed round, and in the second stage players act on what they heard. What you heard in stage one shapes your play.
pros: Listening comes before playing.
Players act on what they were told.
cons: A changed message affects later play.
The whisper round can drag.

pairs.tendency: A message about a system, such as a village's wells, passes from person to person. The model runs on what each person heard.
pros: Information moves like it does in life.
Players see how news changes.
cons: A model can be built on a wrong report.
The first report is lost.

pairs.tendency: Each group sends word to the next, and the farmers hear it differently from the council. The message shows who hears what.
pros: Each group hears a different version.
Players learn how other groups hear things.
cons: A group can be left out.
A message can be changed to suit a group.

pairs.tendency: A whisper warns how low the shared well is, and it travels. Players act on a report that may be out of date.
pros: News of the resource spreads.
Players decide how much to take.
cons: A message can hide how little is left.
A rumour of shortage can cause a rush.

pairs.tendency: A message is sent now, and its effect shows up a few rounds later. By then the message may have changed and so may the result.
pros: Words and results are linked over time.
Players see where a message led.
cons: A result is hard to trace to a word.
A garbled message can be noticed late.

pairs.tendency: A new rule is whispered round and then tried. Players who heard it differently end up following different rules.
pros: The rule spreads by talk.
Players see how a rule drifts.
cons: The rule may be followed in several ways.
A trial can be hard to compare.

pairs.tendency: After play, players tell what each heard and compare it with what was sent. The changes in the message are laid out for all to see.
pros: Players see where the message changed.
The talk shows how each person heard it.
cons: People may remember it differently.
The comparison can run longer than the game.

pairs.tendency: A message sent cannot be taken back, and the board keeps the marks it caused. A wrong word leaves a lasting mark.
pros: Each message counts.
Players take care with words.
cons: A wrong word cannot be undone.
The board can fill with mistakes.

pairs.tendency: The rules make the message hard to pass without changing it. The game says something about how news travels.
pros: The rules say something about rumour.
Players see how a story shifts.
cons: Players may play it as an ordinary game.
Not everyone will accept what it says about news.

pairs.tendency: A message in the game carries a real promise or secret. A changed word can hurt a friend outside the game.
pros: What is said in the game matters outside it.
Players take care with what they say.
cons: A mistake can hurt a friendship.
Players may be afraid to speak.
