pairs.tendency: Landing on a certain square earns one more question, and a skip square loses your turn to ask. The others narrow down the secret while the squares decide who gets to ask.
pros: A landing can win a question.
Each question shrinks the list.
cons: A player who misses turns falls behind on clues.
A question tied to a square can be wasted.

pairs.tendency: Safe squares hold a lead and send-back squares can wipe one out, so the first player to the end is decided partly by the track.
pros: Everyone can see who is ahead.
The squares keep the race open.
cons: A leader near the end can be sent to the start.
A race drags on when players keep being sent back.

pairs.tendency: Some squares score points, some take them and some skip a turn, so players pick routes by what they can collect.
pros: Points sit on certain squares.
Routes are chosen by score.
cons: A skipped turn means points not collected.
A score can swing on a single landing.

pairs.tendency: Squares can knock a piece out or keep it safe. As players drop away, the safe squares matter more and the survivors crowd onto them.
pros: The end of the game crowds the safe squares.
Players race for shelter.
cons: A piece can be knocked out by a square alone.
Knocked-out players wait and watch.

pairs.tendency: The team shares a safe square to rest on and helps a stuck player past a skip square. The squares are part of what works against the whole group.
pros: Squares give the team places to rest.
Players help each other cross.
cons: A trap square can hurt everyone at once.
One stuck piece slows the group.

pairs.tendency: Every piece has to visit one particular square, so the group picks a route through the squares together.
pros: The group has stops to make together.
Players agree a route.
cons: One stuck piece holds up the goal.
A send-back square can undo shared progress.

pairs.tendency: A secret goal might be to land on one certain square. Others watch where a piece keeps stopping and try to guess the aim.
pros: A goal can hide among ordinary moves.
A route gives hints.
cons: A step onto the wrong square gives the goal away.
One landing can mislead a guess.

pairs.tendency: A square can bring a twist, a delay or a rescue, so the track reads like a plot.
pros: The story turns at the squares.
Players have scenes to describe.
cons: The story can stall on a skip square.
Players may disagree how a square fits the story.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, so the squares are there to wander through: a safe square for a rest, a send-back square for a surprise. At the end the group looks back at where each piece went.
pros: Squares leave a trail to talk about.
Players can try squares freely.
cons: With no prize, a trap square may stop mattering.
Players have little reason to pick one square over another.

pairs.tendency: One player aims to reach a single safe square and another wants to visit every skip square. The squares make both goals easy to check.
pros: Squares offer clear goals.
Each player picks a route.
cons: Two goals can clash on one square.
Players may disagree on whether a goal was met.

pairs.tendency: A skip square or a send-back square is where the player who is losing often ends up. Safe squares matter to everyone, since nobody wants to be last.
pros: Safe squares protect everyone.
Players watch whoever is last.
cons: The last player can be stuck on trap squares for long.
A player left behind has little to do.

pairs.tendency: A send-back square gives a second chance and a skip square gives a rest, so squares keep people in play.
pros: Squares bring players back in.
Nobody is out for long.
cons: Play has no clear end.
Players can wander round the same squares.

pairs.tendency: A safe square leads to a send-back square and the track loops, so every route returns the player. The squares carry the point of the game.
pros: Play shows the point.
The pattern shows after a few rounds.
cons: Players may stop once they see there is no end.
Square rules may look like mistakes.

pairs.tendency: Some squares on the layout hold cards in place and others let them move. Clearing the table means getting past the squares that hold cards back.
pros: Squares make some cards harder to reach.
A solo player can plan a route.
cons: A skip square can lock the layout.
A stuck layout ends the game early.

pairs.tendency: A different square rule can open each short game, so the player who won the last one has to learn which squares helped. Two wins out of three decides it.
pros: Players learn the squares between games.
A loser can adjust.
cons: One unlucky landing can lose a whole game.
Square rules need explaining again each time.

pairs.tendency: A square that hands out points is a hazard, so players steer round scoring squares and welcome skip squares that cost nothing.
pros: Squares that score are avoided.
Players read the board in reverse.
cons: A forced landing on a points square costs a lot.
New players find it odd to avoid squares.

pairs.tendency: A send-back square one step from the finish can undo a careful approach. Players hover near the end, waiting for the right roll.
pros: Squares near the end hold players back.
The finish takes luck and planning.
cons: Waiting for the exact number slows the end.
A player on a send-back square starts again.

pairs.tendency: A send-back square is a gift and a safe square is a nuisance. Players aim for the traps.
pros: Squares change meaning.
Safe squares get avoided.
cons: Players forget which way the game runs.
A safe square can hold a player who wants to leave.

pairs.tendency: Everyone plays at once on their own board with the same special squares. Players compare how the same squares hit different people.
pros: Players see the squares land on others.
Nobody waits for a turn.
cons: Players cannot change each other's squares.
Comparing can leave a player feeling behind.

pairs.tendency: A safe square gives a place to hide from an attack, and a send-back square helps whoever can push a rival onto it.
pros: A threatened piece has somewhere to go.
Attackers aim at squares.
cons: A piece on a trap square draws attacks.
Fights gather near the safe squares.

pairs.tendency: Nobody hits anyone directly. Players shape the squares, and the effect arrives when a rival lands.
pros: Squares carry the effect of earlier moves.
Players leave things for others to find.
cons: A blocked safe square can annoy a player who never saw it happen.
Rivals cannot tell who set a trap.

pairs.tendency: The team plans together how to cross the skip squares and who gets the safe ones first. The squares act as the game's moves against them.
pros: Players plan routes together.
A safe square can be shared.
cons: One piece on a trap square holds the team back.
Plans take longer with more players.

pairs.tendency: A safe square can be offered to a friend or kept for yourself, so the squares show who shares.
pros: Sharing becomes visible.
Players choose when to help.
cons: Help can be held back for a private gain.
Players may grow suspicious.

pairs.tendency: Teammates can keep a safe square open for each other, and a teammate stuck on a skip square holds the whole team up.
pros: Teammates cover each other.
The team plans around the squares.
cons: A stuck teammate slows the team.
The losing team may blame one landing.

pairs.tendency: A trap square gives the traitor cover, since sending a piece onto it looks like an accident. The group watches where each piece goes.
pros: The traitor can hide behind a square.
The group watches routes.
cons: A real accident can look like treachery.
Suspicion grows after each trap landing.

pairs.tendency: Moves arrive by post, so a piece on a skip square waits weeks for its next move. Every letter says which square was reached.
pros: Players feel every skipped move.
Each move can be thought over.
cons: One skip square adds days or weeks.
Letters can get lost.

pairs.tendency: The absent player's piece still stands on the board, and the squares can still catch it. The others move it for them.
pros: An absent piece keeps squares in play.
Squares work on a piece nobody speaks for.
cons: Others may move it unevenly.
The absent piece may be left on a trap square.

pairs.tendency: The game master decides what each special square means, so a square can be described in a new way each time it is reached.
pros: Squares can change with the story.
Players meet surprises.
cons: Players may disagree with the master's reading.
The master has a lot to remember.

pairs.tendency: Squares chalked on the ground are known to everyone passing by. A newcomer learns a safe square by watching.
pros: Anyone can see the squares.
Newcomers join by following.
cons: Chalk rubs out in rain.
Passers-by may step on a square and ask what it does.

pairs.tendency: The lone player may own the special squares, such as a safe square only that player may use, to even out the sides.
pros: The lone player gets a home advantage.
The group plans together to cross the squares.
cons: The group can trap the lone player.
A trap square can end a lone player's run.

pairs.tendency: The squares are the only opponent, and you meet each one as it comes.
pros: Squares set the pace.
The player can try again.
cons: Nobody is there to talk to about a landing.
A run of trap squares ends the game.

pairs.tendency: Dice decide where you stop and squares decide what that means, so chance is added to chance.
pros: Anyone can come from behind.
Little needs studying.
cons: Nothing is learnt from past games.
Players have little control.

pairs.tendency: A spare re-roll saves a piece from a send-back square, so players keep re-rolls for the landings that matter.
pros: Re-rolls have a clear use.
Players hold back re-rolls for send-back squares.
cons: Re-rolls run out.
A re-roll can be spent on a safe landing.

pairs.tendency: Choices matter most, and the squares give a few places where luck decides. A skilled player avoids them but cannot always.
pros: Planning pays off.
Luck gives surprise.
cons: A rare landing can undo a plan.
New players may find the squares confusing.

pairs.tendency: With no dice, squares are fixed hazards and rewards that players plan around from the first move.
pros: Squares are known obstacles.
Players can plan far ahead.
cons: Long thinking comes before moves.
A mistake on a trap square cannot be blamed on luck.

pairs.tendency: A throw is turned into advice about which square to seek. The message points to a special square.
pros: Throws mean more than numbers.
Squares become destinations that mean something.
cons: Players may read the same throw differently.
Reading takes time.

pairs.tendency: A square with room for one piece makes everyone wonder who will step first. Players try to sense when the others will move.
pros: Players read each other.
A small square adds pressure to the timing.
cons: Two players may step at once and clash.
There is nothing to calculate.

pairs.tendency: A special square can add its own entries to the table the dice are looked up on, such as a six on the market square bringing a stranger.
pros: Squares extend the story table.
A roll means different things at each square.
cons: Tables get long.
Players keep looking things up.

pairs.tendency: Everything is visible, including what every square does, so players can plan a route from the start.
pros: There are no hidden traps.
Routes can be planned far ahead.
cons: Players think for a long time at squares.
The first player to see the path has the edge.

pairs.tendency: A square may reward a card in hand, and others watch which squares you head for to guess your hand.
pros: Moves leak clues.
Bluffing is possible.
cons: Heading for a square can give the hand away.
Players may guess wrong.

pairs.tendency: Squares are where roles show: a player who dodges every send-back square might be on the safe side.
pros: Routes come under suspicion.
A role can be guessed from where a piece walks.
cons: A wrong guess starts a quarrel.
A safe square can hide a traitor.

pairs.tendency: A square can hand out one clue or take a turn, and where a piece goes tells others what it knows.
pros: Squares hand out clues.
Players follow each other's routes.
cons: A skip square delays a clue.
Players may chase the same square.

pairs.tendency: A piece standing near a safe square suggests a hand worth keeping, so players read the board for lies.
pros: Standing near a square can be a bluff.
Players study where pieces stand.
cons: A bluff to reach a safe square can be called.
A caught bluffer loses a turn.

pairs.tendency: The secret rule can be a square nobody was told about. Newcomers step on it and are told no.
pros: The hidden rule sits on a square.
Learning comes by stepping.
cons: Newcomers keep being sent back.
Squares may seem random.

pairs.tendency: Squares give the clue-giver landmarks to point at, such as a picture of the safe square.
pros: Squares are things to hint at.
Hints can point to a place.
cons: A hint can point to the wrong square.
Guessing can go on for long.

pairs.tendency: Squares are turned over only when someone steps there, so a trap square is a surprise.
pros: Every step reveals something.
Players take risks.
cons: A hidden send-back square can end a run.
Once turned over, the square is known to all.

pairs.tendency: One hand lies face up and is linked to the squares, so everyone sees what could happen. A player may play the open hand to reach a square.
pros: Open cards show which squares are within reach.
Shared knowledge helps plans.
cons: Players lean on the open hand.
Using it for the wrong square wastes the cards.

pairs.tendency: Scoring squares add points without telling anyone, so a player who lands on one can keep quiet.
pros: Nobody knows who profits from a square.
Players guess who is ahead.
cons: Others may avoid scoring squares out of doubt.
Guessing may end in disputes.

pairs.tendency: One player acts at a time, so every landing on a special square is watched by all. A skip square means a visible wait.
pros: Nothing happens unseen.
Players learn from each other's landings.
cons: Turns pass with nothing to do.
A skip square makes a long wait.

pairs.tendency: Two pieces may reach the same safe square at the same moment, and the square's rule decides who gets it.
pros: Squares settle ties.
Players guess the others' targets.
cons: Pieces collide on one safe square.
Fast rounds make square rules easy to forget.

pairs.tendency: The quickest piece takes the safe square, and a skip square holds a piece while the others pass.
pros: Speed counts.
Squares are raced to.
cons: Slow players miss every safe square.
Quarrels start over who arrived first.

pairs.tendency: A player stuck at a choice may lose the move when the clock runs out. A square that offers a gain and a risk gets a quick decision.
pros: The clock pushes quick choices.
Squares are read at a glance.
cons: Time can run out near a trap square.
Rushed moves land on the wrong square.

pairs.tendency: A skip square means missing a whole day, and a piece waits on its square while the clock goes.
pros: Each landing shapes a whole day.
Waiting is part of play.
cons: A skip square can last a whole day.
Players forget where their piece is.

pairs.tendency: Each landing on a special square comes with a pause. A safe square invites a breath.
pros: Squares can invite a rest.
Landings are noticed.
cons: The game takes long.
The slow pace may lose some players.

pairs.tendency: A safe square that once let you rest soon has a timer on it, as squares get closer or more dangerous with the pace.
pros: Squares change with the pace.
Early rounds teach the board.
cons: Late rounds arrive before anyone has planned.
Trap squares catch players in a rush.

pairs.tendency: A player who lands on the right square moves again at once, and a chain of such squares lets one piece cover a lot of track.
pros: Moves chain together.
One player can cover a lot of track.
cons: Others watch long runs.
A leader can run out of reach.

pairs.tendency: A safe square in stage one may be a trap in stage two, so players learn two sets of squares.
pros: A square's meaning changes between stages.
Early choices shape later routes.
cons: There are two sets of squares to learn.
An early choice may lose later.

pairs.tendency: Squares stand for real places such as a well or a field, which give water or take it.
pros: The board maps onto something real.
Players link moves to causes.
cons: A square's rule may not match the real place.
Players stop to argue about accuracy.

pairs.tendency: A market square helps the shopkeeper and does nothing for the farmer, so squares favour some roles.
pros: Roles meet the board differently.
Players see the problem from their side.
cons: A role with few useful squares falls behind.
Players may feel the board takes a side.

pairs.tendency: Landing on a well square takes water from the supply that all players share.
pros: Squares link to the supply.
Takers affect everyone.
cons: A greedy route empties the supply.
Others cannot stop a landing.

pairs.tendency: A piece steps on a square and pays three turns later, after it has moved on.
pros: A landing has a later cost.
Players learn to look ahead.
cons: Cause and effect are hard to trace.
Players blame the wrong square.

pairs.tendency: A square's rule is an easy rule to try. The group agrees a change to one square and plays on to see what it does.
pros: Squares are easy to test.
Rule changes show effects fast.
cons: A rule tried on one square may not fit others.
The group may argue about which rule to try.

pairs.tendency: The squares are what the group points at afterwards: the one that sent a piece back, the one that kept another safe.
pros: There are landings to point at.
Players recall moves.
cons: Talk may centre on luck.
The talk afterwards can take longer than the game.

pairs.tendency: A sticker on a square turns a safe square into a trap for every game after.
pros: Squares keep a record.
Later games start differently.
cons: A changed square cannot be restored.
Early moves have long effects.

pairs.tendency: Send-back squares that sit only in one part of the map say something about that part. The rules make their argument through the squares.
pros: The board states the claim.
Players see it by playing.
cons: Players may disagree with the claim.
The point can be missed if the squares are overlooked.

pairs.tendency: Real money or a promise rides on the game, so each landing on a special square carries weight outside it.
pros: Every landing matters.
Players watch each other closely.
cons: Skip squares sting.
Friends may quarrel over a send-back landing.

pairs.tendency: A kindness square gives points, and players chase the squares and forget the kindness.
pros: Squares show what the points stand for.
The gap between number and value appears.
cons: Players may seek only point squares.
The meaning of the squares can be lost.

pairs.tendency: A shared meal square and a shortage square act as events in a village's life. Players land on them and see how it might go.
pros: Squares let people try events.
Players see how it might go.
cons: Squares cannot cover all of life.
Players may take the squares for predictions.

pairs.tendency: The dice move the piece, and a small purse buys extra steps, a shield or a re-roll. The roll sets the spaces and the purse decides what can be done about them.
pros: Players can act against the dice.
A throw can be mended for a price.
cons: Coins run low before the end.
Players may hold coins and forget to spend them.

pairs.tendency: Each card in the shared row has a price. A pick means weighing what the card does against what is left in the purse.
pros: Prices show what cards are worth.
Players read each other's purses.
cons: The last pick may cost more than anyone can pay.
A dear card can sit in the row for rounds.

pairs.tendency: A bid is a price offered over a price listed on the item. Players pay what they bid, and every unit also has a listed price.
pros: Prices are public.
Players learn costs quickly.
cons: A bid can leave a player with nothing.
There are two kinds of price to remember.

pairs.tendency: One more try costs a coin, and so does keeping what you have. Each decision to continue is also a decision to pay.
pros: The risk has a price tag.
Players ask if a try is worth a coin.
cons: Paying can empty the purse.
A loss after paying hurts twice.

pairs.tendency: Each piece costs something to place, so holding many regions needs a steady supply of coins. A player picks between one region held by many pieces and several held by a few.
pros: Costs shape the map.
Expensive pieces carry weight.
cons: Running short leaves regions open.
A rival can wait until a player has spent.

pairs.tendency: A worker on a job pays the job's price, and the spot is then closed to everyone else. A job a player cannot pay for stays empty.
pros: Jobs have a price.
The purse limits choices.
cons: Players run out of coins early.
A paid spot blocks others as well.

pairs.tendency: Tiles cost coins to place, so a pattern is built from what a player can afford. A plan for a bright mosaic has to fit the price list.
pros: Planning follows the costs.
Tiles feel chosen.
cons: Patterns stay half-finished when coins run out.
A price can rule out a favourite shape.

pairs.tendency: Each card in hand has a price to play, so holding one back is saving it. A player can only play what they can pay for.
pros: Costs set the pace of play.
Players weigh now against later.
cons: Hands clog with cards too dear to play.
Coins and cards both need tracking.

pairs.tendency: A high card wins the trick and also costs more to play, so a won trick can leave the winner short for the next.
pros: Winning has a cost.
Players watch each other's purses.
cons: A won trick can leave a player unable to pay next time.
Hands slow down as players count.

pairs.tendency: "I'll pay two coins for your wheat" means more when everything has a cost. Prices give the haggling a starting point.
pros: Prices start the talk.
Deals are easy to compare.
cons: Haggling can run long.
A player can feel cheated by a price they agreed.

pairs.tendency: Each missing piece has a price, so the last item of a set can cost more than the set scores. Players compare the cost of finishing with the points.
pros: Sets get a price.
Players compare costs with scores.
cons: A set can cost more than it scores.
Players hold coins waiting for the right item.

pairs.tendency: A cheap tile joins the map and a dear one adds a city. Roads and fields cost coins to build.
pros: Tiles have a price.
The map shows each player's budget.
cons: A player with few coins can only place small tiles.
Map building slows down.

pairs.tendency: A longer or more daring answer costs a coin, so the chain of calls grows as long as players can pay.
pros: Costs shape the chain.
Short answers are cheap.
cons: A player with no coins is cut out of the chain.
Paying breaks the flow.

pairs.tendency: Nobody speaks, so a coin put down early tells the others something. Spending becomes the way to send a message.
pros: Spending carries a message.
Players watch where coins go down.
cons: A coin spent by mistake sends the wrong signal.
Silence makes the costs harder to count.

pairs.tendency: One rule change is to alter a price, making a card cheaper or dearer. The market moves on a player's turn.
pros: Prices can move.
Players shape the market.
cons: One price change can break a plan.
Everyone re-checks costs.

pairs.tendency: A knight pays in coins and a thief pays in risk, so each character's price is part of who they are.
pros: Costs belong to the character.
The story grows from the choices.
cons: A character with nothing to spend sits out.
Players may argue over what price fits.

pairs.tendency: A coin buys a second flick, so a steady hand and a full purse together decide the result.
pros: A try has a price.
Skill and money mix.
cons: Coins go on shaky hands.
Players waste retries.

pairs.tendency: Every road, wall or town drawn costs something, so a big map costs more.
pros: Space has a price.
The map reflects each budget.
cons: Drawing stops when funds run out.
Players quarrel over what is worth drawing.

pairs.tendency: Each place charges a price, so sharing a fixed amount means deciding what each one is worth. Players guess how rivals will share theirs.
pros: Costs shape the spread.
Players see where others invest.
cons: A thin spread leaves nothing in one place.
Choices are locked once the share is made.

pairs.tendency: Everyone moves until the signal, and a coin can buy a few extra steps. A player decides whether to pay and run.
pros: Coins buy speed.
Players choose when to spend.
cons: A spent coin cannot be used later.
Slow players with no coins are caught.

pairs.tendency: A hand is improved at a price: each swap costs a coin.
pros: Swaps have a price.
Players decide how many to buy.
cons: Too many swaps empty the purse.
A paid swap can still bring a card that is no use.

pairs.tendency: A big pile is a price paid for a lot of cards, since picking up the discard pile has a fee.
pros: The pile has a cost.
Players decide when a pile is worth it.
cons: A big pile bought too soon may hold unwanted cards.
Coins spent on a pile are gone.

pairs.tendency: To beat a high card of another suit a player pays, because trump cards cost more to play.
pros: Trumps cost.
Players keep trumps for tricks that matter.
cons: A player low on coins cannot play a trump.
A low trump costs as much as a high one.

pairs.tendency: There are two boards but one purse, so what is spent on one board is gone from the other.
pros: Every coin has two calls on it.
Players decide where to put coins.
cons: Coins on one board leave the other short.
Attention is split.

pairs.tendency: A wild card can stand for any card, but only if the player pays a coin.
pros: A wild is a purchase.
Players choose when to pay.
cons: A wild bought early may be wasted.
Players without coins cannot use wilds.

pairs.tendency: Shortcuts round the edge are bought: each crossing costs a coin.
pros: Edges become shortcuts with a price.
Players weigh distance against cost.
cons: Coins vanish at the edges.
Players forget the crossing fee.

pairs.tendency: Each question costs something, so the others pick their questions with care. The first question comes before the purse is empty.
pros: Questions have a price.
Players pick their asks.
cons: Running out stops questions.
An early question may waste coins.

pairs.tendency: A player behind can spend coins to buy steps, a shortcut or a shield. A lead can be bought.
pros: Players can catch up.
Spending shows who is chasing.
cons: Coins spent early leave none for the finish.
A runner with a full purse is hard to catch.

pairs.tendency: Coins spent on cards are coins not kept for points, so players weigh spending against scoring.
pros: Points compare with prices.
Players count carefully.
cons: Overspending leaves a low score.
Counting slows the last round.

pairs.tendency: Players with more coins last longer, since staying alive costs a coin each round.
pros: Survival has a price.
Each purse is watched.
cons: A player who runs out is out.
Early knocked-out players watch.

pairs.tendency: Every spend comes out of everyone's pocket, because the team shares one purse.
pros: Players talk about each spend.
A shared purse keeps the group together.
cons: One spend can drain the team.
Players may disagree on spending.

pairs.tendency: Players pool coins to buy steps towards the goal, as villagers might pool money for a well.
pros: Pooling helps.
Players agree priorities.
cons: Not everyone pays equally.
The goal may cost more than the pool holds.

pairs.tendency: What a player buys hints at a secret aim, so someone who keeps buying the same item is probably after it.
pros: Purchases hint at goals.
Players watch each other's buying.
cons: Buying the wrong thing gives the goal away.
Decoy buys waste coins.

pairs.tendency: A coin buys a rescue and another buys a delay, so the plot has a price.
pros: Story turns cost coins.
Players decide what the story is worth.
cons: The purse can stop the story.
Players argue over plot costs.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, and prices still apply. Players choose what to buy for its own sake, then look at what they bought.
pros: Choices show what players value.
Players try things freely.
cons: Without a goal, prices may seem pointless.
Players might stop spending.

pairs.tendency: One player saves for a single dear item and another spends on many cheap ones, so prices turn each goal into a plan.
pros: Players plan to their own goals.
Costs mean different things to each player.
cons: Two goals may clash over one item.
A goal may be priced out of reach.

pairs.tendency: The player who runs out of coins first is often the one who loses.
pros: Purses matter to all.
Players guard their coins.
cons: The first to run dry falls behind fast.
Safe players may stop watching the last one.

pairs.tendency: Costs ease when a purse is empty, so nobody is priced out of play.
pros: Empty purses still play.
Play continues.
cons: Prices lose weight.
The game may have no ending.

pairs.tendency: However much a player spends, the price rises again. The cost is what the game is about.
pros: The game shows what spending cannot buy.
Players see the pattern.
cons: Players may feel cheated.
Coins pile up with no use.

pairs.tendency: You play alone against the cards, and each move costs coins from a small supply. Clearing the layout takes careful spending.
pros: Solo play asks for planning.
Each spend is visible.
cons: One wrong spend ends the game early.
Few coins mean few choices.

pairs.tendency: Every game starts with a fresh purse, so savings do not carry over.
pros: Each game starts fresh.
Players try new spending.
cons: A loss from overspending can come back in the next game.
The same prices are met again each game.

pairs.tendency: Items carry points and the lowest score wins, so every purchase counts against the buyer.
pros: Buying is held back.
Players study the price list closely.
cons: Players who buy nothing may stall.
A forced purchase can cost the win.

pairs.tendency: A player one short pays a coin to move one step.
pros: Coins fill gaps.
Players plan the last step.
cons: Paying uses up coins.
The exact number still needs luck.

pairs.tendency: Spending is the way to give everything away, so the player who spends all their coins first wins.
pros: Spending is the aim.
Prices turn upside down.
cons: Players who forget the aim hoard.
Coins given away cannot be taken back.

pairs.tendency: Everyone plays alone at the same time with a purse and a price list, then compares what each bought.
pros: The same prices lead to different choices.
Nobody waits.
cons: Players cannot affect each other.
Comparing shows up each player's spending.

pairs.tendency: An attack costs the attacker something, and a defence costs the defender. Players think before they strike.
pros: Attacks have a price.
Each strike is weighed.
cons: A costly attack that misses is wasted.
Players with more coins attack more.

pairs.tendency: Players shape the board to affect each other, and each change has a price.
pros: Board changes show spending.
Rivals feel the effect later.
cons: A change cannot be bought back.
Rivals cannot tell who paid.

pairs.tendency: The whole team is against the game and each unit costs, so players decide together what to buy first.
pros: Players plan together.
Prices make the order matter.
cons: One player's overspend hurts all.
Arguments start about what to buy.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a private purse, so giving a coin to a friend costs your own plan.
pros: Help has a price.
Players test each other.
cons: Private purses breed suspicion.
A gift may never be returned.

pairs.tendency: Two teams buy units and teammates share what they hold.
pros: Teams plan their buying.
Roles split by cost.
cons: One teammate's spend can leave another short.
A team may be outspent.

pairs.tendency: A purchase that helps nobody looks odd, so the traitor's spending is a clue.
pros: Purchases give clues.
Players watch purses.
cons: The traitor can spend in a way that looks fine.
Honest players may be accused for odd buys.

pairs.tendency: The purse is kept on paper, and every letter says what was bought.
pros: Records are written.
Players can check each purchase.
cons: Mistakes in sums travel in letters.
Arguments start over arithmetic.

pairs.tendency: The absent player's purse still sits on the table, and the others spend it for them or leave it.
pros: An absent purse is a puzzle.
Others decide for the absent player.
cons: Spent coins may not match their wishes.
Left alone, coins pile up.

pairs.tendency: The game master sets the prices and the players haggle with them.
pros: Prices come from the master.
Prices can change with the story.
cons: Players may feel the prices are arbitrary.
The master has a lot to track.

pairs.tendency: Prices are simple enough for anyone who walks up: a pebble buys a step.
pros: Anyone can learn the prices.
Everyday objects can be coins.
cons: Passers-by leave with their purse.
Prices need explaining again.

pairs.tendency: The lone player gets a bigger purse to even out the sides.
pros: The purse balances sides.
The group pools coins.
cons: The lone player's single purse can run dry at once.
Group members compete over spending.

pairs.tendency: Moves cost coins, so careful budgeting is the game.
pros: Budgeting matters.
The same game plays differently with different spending.
cons: A short supply ends a run.
There is nobody to ask.

pairs.tendency: Dice decide most things, so spending is the one choice players have, and it is a choice about how to meet luck.
pros: Coins give some say.
Luck gets a little softening.
cons: Coins cannot change a roll.
Players may feel nothing matters.

pairs.tendency: A coin buys a re-roll after an unlucky throw.
pros: Re-rolls have a price.
Players decide when to buy.
cons: Coins spent on rolls are gone for other things.
Players may overuse re-rolls.

pairs.tendency: Choices matter most and a little luck adds surprise, and prices turn the choices into plain sums.
pros: Planning comes with a budget.
Luck rarely ruins a plan.
cons: A chance event can wreck a purchase.
New players need time to learn the prices.

pairs.tendency: With no luck, prices are fixed facts that players plan around from the first move.
pros: Everything can be calculated.
Plans can reach far ahead.
cons: Long pauses come while players calculate.
The first to see the cheap path leads.

pairs.tendency: A player may pay for another reading, as each throw answers a question.
pros: Asking has a price.
Players choose their questions.
cons: A second reading may bring the same answer.
Players may argue what a throw means.

pairs.tendency: A coin put down early shows intent, so players try to spend at the same moment as their friends.
pros: Coins are quiet signals.
Players watch when the others spend.
cons: Spending too soon gives you away.
Prices pull attention from the timing.

pairs.tendency: A coin buys a second look at the table, so the story is shaped by a rolled event and a paid one.
pros: Players can alter the story.
Prices limit retellings.
cons: Coins run out mid-story.
Players spend on twists.

pairs.tendency: Everything is visible, prices and purses too, so players can work out each other's options.
pros: There are no hidden costs.
Players can calculate.
cons: Players think for a long time.
The player with more coins is clear to all.

pairs.tendency: What a player pays for hints at the cards held.
pros: Buying leaks clues.
Players can buy to mislead.
cons: Spending gives away a plan.
Players may buy decoys.

pairs.tendency: A player who buys a weapon is probably a villain, so a purchase can reveal a role.
pros: Spending tells a story.
Players watch purchases.
cons: A false buy brings accusations.
Honest players may get blamed.

pairs.tendency: Players pick which clue is worth buying. Each one costs a coin.
pros: Clues have a price.
Players choose what to buy.
cons: Early clues may be wasted.
Coins run out before the answer.

pairs.tendency: A player who pays a high price for a card makes others believe they need it, so prices can mislead.
pros: A high price can be a lie.
Players read costs.
cons: A paid bluff costs coins when caught.
Bluffs get dear.

pairs.tendency: The secret rule can be a price nobody was told. Newcomers pay it and are told it was wrong.
pros: Prices are learnt by trying.
Each ask costs.
cons: Newcomers overpay.
Players may feel tricked.

pairs.tendency: Because each hint costs a coin, the clue-giver picks hints carefully.
pros: Hints have a price.
The clue-giver chooses carefully.
cons: The purse can empty before anyone guesses.
Fewer hints lead to guessing.

pairs.tendency: Players pay to look: exploring costs coins.
pros: Looking has a price.
Players choose where to explore.
cons: A costly look can show nothing useful.
Players with no coins stay in the dark.

pairs.tendency: The open hand has prices anyone can read.
pros: Prices are visible.
Players can plan spending.
cons: The open hand gives away a plan.
Players buy from it often.

pairs.tendency: Spending is hidden along with some points, so players guess from the buying they have seen.
pros: Nobody sees totals.
Guesses carry the game.
cons: Buying clues may mislead.
Disputes come at the end.

pairs.tendency: Every spend is seen by all, as one player acts at a time.
pros: Spending is visible.
Players learn from others.
cons: Players wait with nothing to buy.
A late player sees the prices go.

pairs.tendency: Prices are paid at the same moment, so two players may reach for one item.
pros: Spending is a guess.
Each round is over fast.
cons: Two players can tie on one item.
Coins spent on a lost tie may be gone.

pairs.tendency: The quickest hand takes the item, and players with coins ready buy first.
pros: A fast hand gets the item.
Coins at hand win items.
cons: Slow players find the shelves empty.
Quarrels start over who paid first.

pairs.tendency: Choosing what to buy has to be quick when the clock runs.
pros: Buying is quick.
Prices are memorised.
cons: Rushed buys happen.
The clock runs out before the purse is counted.

pairs.tendency: Coins can be saved for the next morning, and each day is one decision about spending.
pros: Saving can run across days.
Waiting becomes a move.
cons: A purse can be forgotten.
Long saving may not pay.

pairs.tendency: Each purchase comes with a pause, so players weigh each price.
pros: A pause gives time to weigh prices.
Buying is careful.
cons: The game runs slow.
Some players lose interest.

pairs.tendency: Prices rise with the pace, so early buying is cheap and late buying drains the purse.
pros: Costs climb.
Early buyers save.
cons: Late rounds drain purses.
Players are rushed.

pairs.tendency: A lucky throw gives another go, and a coin can buy one too.
pros: Turns have a price.
Luck and money mix.
cons: A player with coins moves twice.
Coins spent on turns run out.

pairs.tendency: What a player buys in the first stage is what they play with in the second.
pros: Early buying has later effect.
Planning reaches ahead.
cons: An empty purse leaves stage two short.
Each stage has its own prices.

pairs.tendency: Each action costs what it would in real life, such as water or labour.
pros: Costs mirror life.
Players see trade-offs.
cons: Costs may look too simple.
Players dispute the numbers.

pairs.tendency: A council has funds and a farmer has little, so roles have different purses.
pros: Some roles can do more than others.
Players see unequal means.
cons: A small purse leaves a role stuck.
Players argue over who gets what.

pairs.tendency: Each pail of water costs a coin, so taking from the shared supply is priced.
pros: Taking is priced.
A price may slow overuse.
cons: A price cannot stop a rush.
Coins vanish while the supply shrinks.

pairs.tendency: A player pays today and gets the result in three rounds.
pros: Buying is a bet on the future.
Players learn to wait.
cons: Purses stay empty while waiting.
Costs are hard to link to results.

pairs.tendency: What if every card cost one more? The group agrees and plays on to see.
pros: Prices are easy to test.
Effects show quickly.
cons: A test price may not hold in real use.
Choosing the test price can start an argument.

pairs.tendency: After the game, players talk through what they paid and for what.
pros: Spending leaves a record.
Looking back is easy.
cons: Luck can take over the talk.
Memory of costs fades.

pairs.tendency: A card torn up has been paid for once and is gone.
pros: Purchases leave marks.
A torn card stays out of later games.
cons: Nothing can be refunded.
A first purchase shapes every game after.

pairs.tendency: A game where health costs a lot says something about health, and the prices carry the point.
pros: Prices say something.
Players see it by buying.
cons: Some players will not accept it.
Someone who ignores the prices misses the point.

pairs.tendency: Real money rides on the game, so each in-game price is also a real one.
pros: Every spend counts.
Players are careful.
cons: Quarrels start over spends.
Some players avoid buying.

pairs.tendency: Kindness costs two coins and returns three points, so the price turns a value into a number.
pros: The price reveals a value.
Players see the trade.
cons: Players chase the number.
The kindness behind the points is forgotten.

pairs.tendency: Prices stand for time and effort, so players feel what a shared village costs.
pros: Players feel the cost.
Trade-offs are visible.
cons: Prices are guesses at real ones.
Players may take them as facts.

pairs.tendency: Before each roll you share a handful of points between the pieces on the track, and the dice then move the piece you backed the most. A piece with many points and a low roll sits still while the others wait.
pros: The roll still matters after you commit.
Each piece gets a different chance.
cons: Points on a low roller are lost.
Working out the split slows each turn.

pairs.tendency: A small stock of tokens goes onto the cards you hope to take from the shared row. When someone picks a card you backed, those tokens go to waste.
pros: Each pick shows where you put your effort.
Players can guess what others want.
cons: Tokens on a taken card are lost.
Waiting for the row to come round feels slow.

pairs.tendency: A fixed purse is shared across several lots, so a big bid on one lot leaves little for the next. Rivals watch where you spend and bid where you are thin.
pros: Players read each other's purses.
A cheap lot can be won while others fight over a dear one.
cons: Winning early leaves you empty later.
Players spend long minutes adding up.

pairs.tendency: Points are spread over several risky pushes, and each one can go bust on its own. A bust on one front does not end the others.
pros: A single loss does not wipe you out.
Each push is its own small risk.
cons: Pushing everywhere at once is hard to keep track of.
A big win on one front can be cancelled by two busts.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a fixed number of pieces to share over the regions of the map. Put many in one region and the others lie open to anyone who walks in.
pros: Every region is a separate small fight.
The map shows who is stretched thin.
cons: Spread pieces are easy to beat one by one.
A single heavy region can still be outflanked.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a few workers for many jobs, and each job taken is closed to everyone else that round. A worker on one job is a worker not on the next.
pros: Every placement shows what you chose to skip.
Players can block each other's plans.
cons: Late players find the choice jobs gone.
A wasted worker is felt for the whole round.

pairs.tendency: Tiles are shared between two or three patterns at once, so none of them grows as fast as it would alone. Finishing one means giving up a start on another.
pros: Several patterns can score together.
A late switch is possible.
cons: Unfinished patterns count for nothing.
The board gets crowded with half-built shapes.

pairs.tendency: On each front, a player picks how many cards to play and how many to keep back. Cards kept in hand cannot help the front that needs them now.
pros: Players decide how much to hold in reserve.
Each front can be backed in a different amount.
cons: Cards held back may never be used.
An empty hand leaves a front undefended.

pairs.tendency: Some tricks get your top cards and others are given up cheaply. Giving up one trick on purpose saves strength for the next.
pros: A lost trick can be a plan.
Players count cards to judge what is left.
cons: A trick given up cannot be won back.
Opponents can tell when you are saving.

pairs.tendency: Each player has only so much to give, so every deal you make leaves less for the next table you talk to. Others offer you things in return for the part you are holding back.
pros: Deals show what each player values.
A small gift can win a large favour.
cons: Promises run out of things to back them.
Talk can drag when everyone is counting.

pairs.tendency: Effort goes into two or three sets at the same time instead of one. Each set grows slowly, and a rival who takes the one card you need can stall one set but not all.
pros: A blocked set is not a lost game.
Players can change their aim late.
cons: No set may finish in time.
Partial sets score little.

pairs.tendency: Tiles go down on several parts of the map, so each part grows a little instead of one part growing a lot. A neighbour can close off a part before you return to it.
pros: Many small builds appear at once.
Rivals can only close one part at a time.
cons: A thin area is easy to cut off.
The map can look scattered.

pairs.tendency: One side of the chain is answered by several players at once, so a player splits their words or moves between them. Each answer you give shapes only one of the replies.
pros: Several threads of the chain run together.
Players follow each other closely.
cons: It is hard to keep every thread going.
A thread you neglect goes quiet.

pairs.tendency: With no talking, you share your effort between places and others have to guess your plan from where it lands. A thin spot may be a trap or an accident.
pros: Players read each other through actions alone.
Mixed signals add some guessing.
cons: Allies cannot say what they are covering.
Two players may cover the same spot by mistake.

pairs.tendency: A rule change can set how many points you get to share or where they may go. A player who is thin in many places votes for a rule that favours spreading.
pros: Rules can reward a wide spread.
One change can undo a plan.
cons: Players argue about rules for a long time.
A plan built on a rule can fall when it changes.

pairs.tendency: A character has limited time or strength to put into several tasks in the story. The group sees which tasks they chose to leave alone.
pros: Choices show what a character cares about.
The story moves where effort goes.
cons: A skipped task can come back as trouble.
Players can feel stretched.

pairs.tendency: A few moves or throws are shared between several targets, such as blocks to flick or towers to build. A throw spent on one tower is not available for the others.
pros: A steady hand is needed on every front.
Each target is a separate small test.
cons: A shaky throw wastes a limited try.
Players may rush the last tries.

pairs.tendency: Pens or counters go to several parts of the map, so only some are drawn in detail. The areas you skip stay blank until someone else fills them in.
pros: Players see where each person put their effort.
Blank corners leave room for others.
cons: An undrawn region can surprise everyone.
Detail is uneven across the sheet.

pairs.tendency: Everyone moves until a signal sounds, and you have a fixed supply of effort to put into where you freeze or which seat you grab. If you spent it all on running, you have nothing left for the grab.
pros: Players choose between speed and the final move.
The signal makes every share count.
cons: Over-committing early can leave you caught.
The slowest player is easy to spot.

pairs.tendency: Only a few swaps are allowed, so some go on one hand or pile, others on another. A swap kept back may be needed for a hand you cannot yet see.
pros: Swaps go where they are most needed.
A hand can improve in small steps.
cons: Used swaps do not return.
Players can swap too many on the wrong hand.

pairs.tendency: Cards are spread across more than one pile, and players wait to see which one grows the most before you pick it up. A big pile may tempt a rival to take it first.
pros: A fat pile is a prize.
Piles show where players are hiding cards.
cons: A pile left alone can be taken at once.
Players watch the piles instead of their own hand.

pairs.tendency: Only a few trump cards can be spent over the tricks of a hand. Using a trump early wins one trick and leaves fewer for the rest.
pros: Trumps decide when a low card can win.
Players count what is left.
cons: An early trump can be wasted on a small trick.
Players with no trump are easy to beat.

pairs.tendency: Attention is shared between two boards, and a move on one board is a move not made on the other. Your opponent can see which board you left alone.
pros: Two boards give two chances.
A loss on one does not end the game.
cons: Mistakes pile up on the neglected board.
Turns take longer to think through.

pairs.tendency: With a few wild cards, a player can finish a set in one place or save them for another. A wild used on a small set cannot finish a big one.
pros: A wild card turns a near miss into a finish.
Players choose where it matters most.
cons: A wild used early may be missed later.
Rivals can guess which set is short.

pairs.tendency: Pieces are spread around a board with joined edges, so a piece at the far right sits next to one at the far left. A thin line on one edge can be reached from the other.
pros: There is no safe corner.
Players watch both ends of the board.
cons: A spread force has gaps on every side.
It is harder to see who is close to whom.

pairs.tendency: A fixed number of questions has to cover several secrets, such as a few hidden cards. Every question about one secret leaves another unasked.
pros: Each answer narrows one list.
Players choose which secret to chase.
cons: A question spent on the wrong secret is gone.
Some secrets are never solved.

pairs.tendency: Steps are shared between several runners, and only the first to cross the line counts. Steps given to a runner who falls behind are gone.
pros: Players choose how to back each runner.
The leader can change late.
cons: Every step on a slow runner is wasted.
One lucky runner can end the race early.

pairs.tendency: Several places score points, and the total at the end is what counts. Small scores from many places add up against a large score from one.
pros: Several routes to points stay open.
Players can adjust late.
cons: No single place gets enough to score a lot.
Players can lose track of the running total.

pairs.tendency: Pieces are held across several fronts, and a player is knocked out when all of theirs fall. A front left thin invites an early strike.
pros: Pieces in reserve extend your life.
Players can pick the front to attack.
cons: A thin spot can end a player quickly.
Knocked-out players wait a long time.

pairs.tendency: The team has a limited supply to share over several dangers that all grow. Every danger you answer leaves another to grow.
pros: The group has to agree where to spend.
Everyone sees the same hard choices.
cons: A danger left alone can end the game for all.
One loud player can steer the choices.

pairs.tendency: The team shares its effort between several parts of the goal, and each part needs a minimum before the whole is done. Players argue over which part to fill first.
pros: Everyone sees what is still missing.
Different jobs can be given to different players.
cons: One part left short blocks the whole goal.
Talk takes up much of the time.

pairs.tendency: A player puts effort into several places, each hiding a bit of what they want. Others watch where you spread yourself to guess your goal.
pros: A spread plan is hard to read.
You can switch aim late.
cons: A thin spread may fall short of the goal.
A rival who guesses can block you.

pairs.tendency: A character spreads time across the threads of a story, and the story ends when its threads are tied. Threads left unfed stay open at the end.
pros: Several storylines can grow together.
Players pick which thread to resolve.
cons: A loose thread can leave the ending unfinished.
The tale may feel scattered.

pairs.tendency: With no goal to win, the way you share effort between places shows what you cared about. At the end the group looks at where everyone put their share.
pros: The pattern of choices is easy to see afterwards.
Players are free to spread any way they like.
cons: Nothing marks one spread as finished.
Players may not know when to stop.

pairs.tendency: A personal goal decides how each player shares what they have. One player puts it all on one place, while another spreads thinly to keep many things safe.
pros: Two players can share the same pieces and aim for different ends.
A player can change the goal as they go.
cons: It is hard to compare results.
A goal can turn out to need more than you shared.

pairs.tendency: Strength is shared over several places, and whoever ends up with the least safe one is the loser. Everyone else is safe once they cover their weakest spot.
pros: Players watch one another's thin points.
A well-covered player can relax.
cons: Players race to avoid the last place.
One mistake can leave you alone as the loser.

pairs.tendency: The group shares its effort between many parts of a game that has no end, so something is always left to do. A part nobody feeds can fade away.
pros: Play can move around the table for a long time.
Different players can look after different parts.
cons: Some parts may be forgotten.
The game can wear out without a clear stop.

pairs.tendency: No spread can lead to a win, however the effort is placed. Players are left looking at what each choice shows.
pros: Every choice shows how a player thinks.
Players may talk about what went wrong.
cons: The effort has no result to reach.
Some players give up sharing at all.

pairs.tendency: Alone at the table, you share a small number of moves over several piles in the layout. A move spent on one pile leaves another stuck.
pros: The solo player gets a clear plan to weigh.
The layout is the only rival.
cons: A pile ignored can block the whole table.
One wrong share can end the game early.

pairs.tendency: The same amount of effort is given for every game, and a player spends more in some games and less in others. Winning two games with all your effort can leave you empty for a third.
pros: A game can be thrown to save effort for the next.
Players can tell which games to give up.
cons: Saving effort for a later game may lose the first.
Games that feel one-sided can still count.

pairs.tendency: Every place you put effort into can add points to your score, so keeping each one small keeps your total low.
pros: Spreading thin keeps single risks small.
Players can drop points in many places.
cons: Small points from many places still add up.
A rival can push points on to you.

pairs.tendency: Steps are shared between several runners that all need to land on an exact number. One runner too far along cannot take more steps, so the rest soak them up.
pros: Players tune each runner separately.
Extra steps find a home.
cons: A runner that overshoots loses its place.
Every step needs a careful count.

pairs.tendency: You spread your effort to give things away in several places, and whoever has the least left wins. Spreading wide drops your total quickly.
pros: Players give away on many fronts.
A rival is often helped by your gifts.
cons: Giving too fast ends the game early.
It is hard to tell who is really ahead.

pairs.tendency: Each player shares their own pool between their own projects and nobody takes from anyone else. The only news is a glance at how the others have spread theirs.
pros: Everyone has a plan to keep.
Players can compare spreads quietly.
cons: Nothing you do changes the other players.
The game may feel like separate puzzles.

pairs.tendency: How much strength to send against each rival is a choice, and a rival who gets less can hit back. A hard strike on one leaves you open to another.
pros: Players pick targets with care.
Revenge is easy to plan.
cons: A thin guard invites an attack.
One player may be hit by everyone.

pairs.tendency: You put your pieces on several spots of the board to block, claim or build, and rivals feel it through the map. A spot you leave open can be taken by someone else.
pros: The board shows each plan.
Players are never aimed at directly.
cons: Thin spots are easy to take over.
It is hard to see who a move was meant for.

pairs.tendency: One pool of effort serves the whole team across many jobs, and every job needs some. Players take turns saying what they will cover and what they leave.
pros: Jobs get spread among players.
Everyone has a say in the split.
cons: One job left short can end the game.
Talk can fall to one confident person.

pairs.tendency: A common pool goes to the team's shared jobs, but each player holds some back for a private aim. Others watch how much each person keeps in their own hand.
pros: Players can show how much they trust the team.
A small private share can win the game.
cons: Hoarding is easy to suspect.
Common jobs can be left short.

pairs.tendency: Each team shares its effort between fronts, and the other team does the same. A front your side leaves thin is a front the other side may push.
pros: Teammates agree who covers what.
Both teams can read each other's spread.
cons: A team can be caught thin.
Arguments inside a team slow the game.

pairs.tendency: The loyal players share their effort among the jobs, while the traitor puts theirs where it does the most harm. A job that comes up short looks like an accident or a lie.
pros: Players check each other's shares.
The traitor hides in a small gap.
cons: Every shortfall casts doubt on someone.
An honest mistake can get a player accused.

pairs.tendency: Each letter tells your partner how you have shared your effort this week, and the reply comes days later. Plans have changed by the time you read it.
pros: Players think carefully before each letter.
A spread can be planned over weeks.
cons: Waiting leaves you guessing at others' moves.
A lost letter hides a whole plan.

pairs.tendency: The absent player's share sits on the board, spread by a rule or by a hint they left behind. The others can see where it lies but cannot ask why.
pros: The missing player still shapes the board.
Their spread can be studied.
cons: Nobody can fix the spread when it goes wrong.
The group can argue about what the absent player meant.

pairs.tendency: The game master shares out the pressure of the world between places, and the players share their effort in reply. Players work out where trouble is likely to land.
pros: The world presses on several fronts.
The game master can adjust the spread to the group.
cons: Players may feel the game master has chosen against them.
One front can swallow the group's time.

pairs.tendency: Players in a park or street spread their pieces across a chalk board, and passers-by can join or move a piece. Someone you did not know can change your spread.
pros: Anyone can enter a front.
Onlookers can give advice.
cons: A spread changes without warning.
Strangers may join and leave in the middle.

pairs.tendency: The lone player shares their strength across all the others, and the group shares theirs over how to answer. The lone player is hit hard if a gap in their spread shows.
pros: The group can cover for each other.
The lone player has to choose a target.
cons: One mistake by the lone player can end the game.
The group can disagree over how to spread.

pairs.tendency: You share your effort over several parts of a problem set by the cards, and no one else can change the split. Any piece you leave alone stays as it was.
pros: The player decides everything.
A game can be replayed with a different spread.
cons: Nothing pushes back when a share goes wrong.
The same spread tends to be tried again.

pairs.tendency: The dice decide which of your places gain or lose, so the spread you chose only softens the blow. A wide spread keeps some places safe from a low throw.
pros: A wide spread smooths out the dice.
Players still make a choice before the throw.
cons: A throw can undo a careful spread.
Sharing matters less than luck.

pairs.tendency: Your spread of effort is your way of softening low throws, since a loss in one place leaves the others. A re-roll can then go where it is needed.
pros: Spreading acts as a cushion.
Re-rolls have more places to help.
cons: A cushion costs points that could win one place.
Players may spread out of habit.

pairs.tendency: The spread is a skill, and a small amount of luck changes which place pays off most. A player who reads the odds spreads well and still gets caught by a lucky throw.
pros: Careful spreads tend to win more often.
A small surprise keeps rivals guessing.
cons: A plan can lose to one lucky throw.
Skilled players can slow the game with sums.

pairs.tendency: Nothing is left to chance, so the way you spread your effort is all that separates you from the other player. A spread that leaves one gap is found and used.
pros: Every spread is a plan to study.
Players can learn from each game.
cons: Mistakes cannot be put down to luck.
A beginner meets a long list of things to weigh.

pairs.tendency: The throw is read as a sign, and you decide how to share your effort in answer to it. The sign says something, and each player is free to read it their own way.
pros: A sign gives players a reason to talk.
The same throw can lead to different spreads.
cons: The reading of a sign may differ between players.
A spread based on a reading can seem odd to others.

pairs.tendency: Players share their attention across the group and try to act at the same moment as the others. A player who looks at only one friend misses the rest.
pros: Players grow aware of the whole group.
A shared moment can be felt.
cons: Attention spread too thin misses cues.
One person who drifts can break the moment.

pairs.tendency: The dice pick the event from a table, and you decide where to put your effort to meet it. A spread across many places lets you meet more events.
pros: The story shifts around the spread.
Players can prepare for several outcomes.
cons: An event can land where you have little.
The table can bring too many events at once.

pairs.tendency: Everyone sees how every player has shared their effort, so a thin place cannot be hidden. A player who leaves a gap sees it noticed at once.
pros: Players plan against what they see.
Nothing is hidden about who is thin.
cons: A mistake in the spread is public.
The game can slow while people count.

pairs.tendency: You hide how your effort is spread and keep your cards close. Others test where you are thin by pushing on one place at a time.
pros: A hidden spread invites guessing.
Players can bluff about where they are thin.
cons: A sharp guess finds the gap.
Turns slow while players study each other.

pairs.tendency: You spread your effort to look like the role you claim, while others watch where your share goes. A wrong spread can give your role away.
pros: Actions show who a player might be.
A careful spread keeps a secret.
cons: One odd spread causes doubt.
Honest players may be blamed for odd choices.

pairs.tendency: Each place you put effort into answers one question, and you have too little to ask about every place. Players pick which clue to chase and which to leave.
pros: Each probe narrows the guess.
Players choose which question to ask.
cons: A clue not chased stays hidden.
A wrong choice of probe wastes the whole turn.

pairs.tendency: You put a large share in one place and a small share elsewhere, and others cannot tell whether the big one is real. A thin spread can be a trap as well as a gap.
pros: Players read each other's claims.
A bluff can hide a gap.
cons: A call on a bluff costs the whole share.
A bluffer can be caught out by a calm rival.

pairs.tendency: You share your tries between actions while you are still working out the secret rule. A try spent on a wrong guess is gone before you know it was wrong.
pros: Each try teaches something.
Players learn from what others try.
cons: Many tries are used while guessing.
New players spend a lot of effort on mistakes.

pairs.tendency: The clue-giver has a limited number of hints to share over several guessers, and each hint can only go to one of them. The others work from what they see around them.
pros: Hints go where they help most.
Guessers learn from each other.
cons: A guesser with no hint is left to guess.
A hint spent on the wrong guesser is lost.

pairs.tendency: You send your pieces to several unexplored areas at once, and each one turns over a piece of the map. Pieces sent far find more but are hard to bring home.
pros: The map opens in many places.
Players find out what the world holds.
cons: Scattered pieces are alone when trouble appears.
Some areas are found too late.

pairs.tendency: One hand lies open on the table, so everyone sees how it is spread. The player who plays it has to share their effort between it and their own hand.
pros: Open cards help the others plan.
The open hand gets used with care.
cons: The player is busy with two hands.
Mistakes with the open hand are plain to all.

pairs.tendency: Your effort goes to several places, and the points you gain from each are kept secret. Others can see where you spent but not what it earned.
pros: Players guess who is ahead.
A spread hides its returns.
cons: No one is sure of the standing.
A lead may be lost without anyone seeing.

pairs.tendency: You use your whole turn to decide how to share your effort between places, while the others wait. Each turn is one decision about where to put the next share.
pros: Each turn shows a plan.
Players can see how a spread develops.
cons: Waiting players have little to do.
A long think holds up the table.

pairs.tendency: Everyone chooses their spread in secret and reveals together. You cannot see where others put their effort before you place yours.
pros: No one waits to act.
Players have to guess what others will do.
cons: A spread that matches a rival's is wasted.
The reveal can bring many surprises at once.

pairs.tendency: Anyone can move a share at any time, so you spread your effort while the others are doing the same. A quick player puts more shares in play before a slow one has finished thinking.
pros: Players act when they see a gap.
The pace is quick.
cons: A slow player falls behind.
It is hard to follow what everyone has done.

pairs.tendency: The clock gives you only a short time to decide how to share your effort. A spread made in a hurry may leave an obvious gap.
pros: Players act on first sense.
The game keeps a steady pace.
cons: A rushed spread can go wrong.
A timer can cut off a careful sum.

pairs.tendency: You make one move a day and share your effort across a week of days. A move spent today is not there tomorrow.
pros: Plans are made over many days.
Players can think between moves.
cons: A gap in a spread lasts a long time.
A missed day cannot be made up.

pairs.tendency: The slow pace gives you time to weigh how to share your effort. A pause before each move lets you notice a place you had forgotten.
pros: Players see the whole spread before they act.
Rash shares are less likely.
cons: The game takes a long time.
Players may lose track of what they planned.

pairs.tendency: The game speeds up while you try to keep your effort spread. As the clock shrinks you have less time to rethink where you put things.
pros: Early spreads matter most.
The end arrives in a rush.
cons: A gap found late cannot be mended.
Careful sums become hard near the end.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn gives you a second chance to place a share, so you can fill a gap straight away. A player with many extra turns spreads out faster than the others.
pros: A lucky player recovers quickly.
A gap can be fixed at once.
cons: Others may feel left behind.
An extra turn makes a careful plan less useful.

pairs.tendency: In the first stage you decide how much to put aside for the second, and the second stage uses whatever you saved. A spread chosen early shapes everything that follows.
pros: An early choice has effects later.
Players have time to see what they gave up.
cons: A share spent too soon is gone for later.
A rough start follows you to the end.

pairs.tendency: The shares of a limited supply, such as water, go to fields, homes and wells in the model. When too much goes to one part, the others dry up as they would in the village.
pros: The model shows how a limit works.
Players see the cost of each share.
cons: A simple model leaves out many real causes.
A choice can look right in the game and wrong outside.

pairs.tendency: Each group has its own supply to share across its needs, such as farmers sharing between crops and seed. The groups see how thin each other's spreads are.
pros: Roles show what each group has to give up.
Players can talk about whose need comes first.
cons: Some groups have much less to spread.
A role can be played with little thought.

pairs.tendency: Everyone shares their own effort over places that draw from one common supply. When all of them take at once, the common supply is gone for everyone.
pros: The common stock shows its limit.
Players see how choices add up.
cons: One player taking a lot can empty the stock.
Careful players pay for the careless.

pairs.tendency: The share you put in one place shows its result a few rounds later. A spread that looks thin now may have been the one that paid.
pros: Players learn to wait for results.
An early share can pay off late.
cons: A mistake shows itself only once it is hard to put right.
It is easy to forget what you put where.

pairs.tendency: The group agrees a new rule about how effort may be shared, then plays on to see what it does to the spread. A rule that caps one place pushes shares to the others.
pros: A rule can be tested without real cost.
Players see its effect on the spread.
cons: A rule may suit some players and hurt others.
The group may change the rule too often.

pairs.tendency: After the game the players look at where each of them put their effort and talk about why. The whole spread is laid out on the table for everyone to see.
pros: A spread is easy to talk about afterwards.
Players can compare plans.
cons: Memory of the reason can fade.
Some players do not want to explain.

pairs.tendency: A share you put in a place changes it for ever, and you cannot take it back. Each spread leaves a mark on the board that the next game starts from.
pros: Every share has weight.
Players think before they commit.
cons: A wrong share stays on the board.
New players see old mistakes.

pairs.tendency: The rules for how effort can be spread make a point, such as what a city rewards. A spread that covers many places says one thing, and a spread that backs one place says another.
pros: The rules give players something to argue about.
A spread shows what a player takes the game to mean.
cons: Players may read the point differently.
A rule that pushes one spread can feel one-sided.

pairs.tendency: Your share of effort is tied to something outside the game, such as a favour or a promise. A spread that looks safe on the board can still cost you at home.
pros: Choices carry weight beyond the table.
Players take the sharing seriously.
cons: Friends can fall out over a split.
Players may avoid sharing at all.

pairs.tendency: Your effort is shared between things that stand for health, kindness and the like, each turned into points. You see which value you let slip when you chase the others.
pros: A spread shows what a player values.
The cost of a skipped value is clear.
cons: Players may chase points and forget what they stand for.
Values squeezed into points lose some meaning.

pairs.tendency: Players share their effort between old habits and new ways of living, and the game shows how thin each can become. The spread tells the group how much of the old way they are keeping.
pros: A group can try a new way at no real cost.
Gaps in the plan show up early.
cons: Real life has more pressures than the game.
A spread that works on the board may fail in a village.

pairs.tendency: Everyone rolls and moves their piece along the track until the signal sounds, then all pieces freeze where they are. A player who rolled the least when the signal came is caught.
pros: The pace is quick.
The signal can cut a lead short.
cons: A player who is slow to roll is easy to catch.
The result depends on the timing of the signal.

pairs.tendency: Cards go round the table fast while the music plays, and you keep the one in your hand when it stops. Players take cards they like in a hurry.
pros: Picks are made on first sense.
The signal ends the passing at a surprise moment.
cons: A hasty pick may be a mismatch.
Cards held at the stop may not go together.

pairs.tendency: Bids rise round the table while the signal is silent, and when it sounds the latest bid stands. A bidder may jump high to be last.
pros: Players watch the signal as well as the price.
A late bid can win cheaply.
cons: A jumpy bid can be too high.
Nobody can plan a bid with certainty.

pairs.tendency: You keep pushing for more until the music cuts out, and anyone still pushing at that moment loses whatever they had not banked.
pros: Players watch for the signal as they push.
A cautious player banks early.
cons: A late push can lose everything.
The signal feels random when it comes at the wrong time.

pairs.tendency: Everyone races to put pieces on the map, and the regions are counted the moment the music stops. A player with the most pieces in a region holds it.
pros: The map fills quickly.
The end comes with little warning.
cons: Pieces placed too fast leave thin spots.
A region can be lost by one piece at the stop.

pairs.tendency: Workers go onto jobs as fast as players can place them until the signal sounds. Jobs taken by then are closed, and a worker not yet placed does nothing.
pros: Fast hands reach the first jobs.
Everyone knows the placing ends at the signal.
cons: Slow players are left with the leftovers.
A rush can lead to workers placed in the wrong job.

pairs.tendency: You lay tiles into a pattern, and at the stop it is judged as it stands. A half-made pattern scores nothing.
pros: A pattern is judged on its state at a moment.
Players aim to finish just before the stop.
cons: A pattern left half-done is lost.
A player has to guess when the signal will come.

pairs.tendency: You choose which cards to play while the signal is silent, and any cards still in hand when it sounds are counted against you. A held card can be a plan or a loss.
pros: Players decide when to play.
The signal keeps hands from being held for ever.
cons: Held cards can be wasted.
A late burst of play is hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: Tricks are played fast round the table until the signal sounds, and the trick in play at that moment is cut short. A card played just before the stop may win or be lost.
pros: Players choose when to play high.
No hand drags on past the stop.
cons: A cut-off trick may be left unfinished.
Fast play makes it easy to miss a card.

pairs.tendency: Players trade and make deals until the music stops, and any deal not yet shaken on is void. Deals get made by people with no time to think.
pros: Deals are made quickly.
The signal gives a cut-off for promises.
cons: A half-made deal falls through.
Players can feel pushed into hasty terms.

pairs.tendency: You gather cards into sets, and when the music stops only the complete ones count. A set one card short scores nothing.
pros: Sets are gathered at speed.
The signal forces a decision about which set to finish.
cons: A near-finished set is worth nothing.
Players grab cards without looking.

pairs.tendency: Tiles go onto the shared map until the stop, and the map is scored as it stands. A tile held in the hand at the signal counts for nothing.
pros: The map grows in a rush.
Players choose when to hold back.
cons: Tiles may be placed without much thought.
An unfinished road earns no points.

pairs.tendency: One player calls and another answers, and whoever owes the next answer when the music stops is caught. The chain speeds up as the signal draws near.
pros: Players listen closely to each call.
The signal ends the chain at a surprise point.
cons: A slow answer is caught.
The caller can trap the next player with a hard call.

pairs.tendency: Everyone moves without a word until the signal sounds. Apart from the signal and the noise of moving there is nothing to hear, so players watch each other closely.
pros: Players read each other's body and timing.
The signal is the only noise.
cons: Nobody can warn a friend.
Players can bump into each other.

pairs.tendency: A player can change a rule while the music plays, and the new rule holds the moment the signal sounds. A rule about who is caught can be changed in the middle of play.
pros: The rules are open until the end.
Players have to listen for new rules.
cons: A new rule may be missed in the rush.
Players can argue about when a rule began.

pairs.tendency: Characters act in a scene until the signal sounds, then every character freezes in place. The group can look at what each character was doing when the scene stopped.
pros: The frozen scene can be talked about.
Players act on instinct.
cons: A character caught mid-action can look odd.
Players can lose their place in the story.

pairs.tendency: Players stack, flick or balance pieces up to the signal, and whatever they built has to hold still when it sounds. A tower that falls after the stop does not count.
pros: Fast hands matter.
The stop leaves a clear result.
cons: A shaky hand at the stop spoils the work.
A quick move often topples the stack.

pairs.tendency: Players draw the map as fast as they can and put their pens down when the music stops. The map shows how far each player got.
pros: The map is full of rough lines.
Each map is different.
cons: Parts of the map can be left blank.
A rushed drawing may be hard to read.

pairs.tendency: Players swap cards in a hurry and keep whatever they hold at the stop. A swap made a second too late is not allowed.
pros: Swaps happen at speed.
The signal fixes each hand.
cons: A hasty swap may break up a set.
Some players do not get to swap at all.

pairs.tendency: Anyone may take the discard pile while play runs, and whoever is holding it at the stop is caught. A tall pile is a risk at the stop.
pros: The pile is a prize and a danger.
Players watch the pile as they watch the signal.
cons: A big pile taken late is hard to use.
Players hold back from taking it.

pairs.tendency: Cards are played quickly, and the moment the music stops the hand is scored by who holds the most trumps. A trump held back is a risk if the signal comes early.
pros: Trumps are worth keeping an eye on.
Nobody can stretch the hand out.
cons: Players may play trumps too soon.
A hand cut short may leave tricks unplayed.

pairs.tendency: Both boards run until the music stops, and then each is judged where it stands. Time spent on one board was time the other went without.
pros: Two boards give two chances.
The stop shows which board was ignored.
cons: One board may be lost for lack of moves.
Players have to keep two things in mind in a rush.
