A piece can end up in front by accident.

pairs.tendency: Each player has their own board with joined edges, so their moves loop on their own. Nobody's pieces meet anyone else's.
pros: Each board is a small world.
Nothing is blocked by rivals.
cons: Players only compare results.
The loops do not touch.

pairs.tendency: Attackers come at a piece from behind through the join, so a player has no wall to back against. Every fight is open on all sides.
pros: Attacks can come from any side.
Pieces cannot be cornered.
cons: Players watch every edge.
A target can be hit from where it did not look.

pairs.tendency: A wall built at one edge shows up on the other, so the effect crosses the seam. A player who blocks a road at the east finds it blocked in the west as well.
pros: Board changes reach far.
Walls act twice.
cons: A block can hurt its builder.
A change at the seam is easy to miss.

pairs.tendency: The team covers the board, and with no corners everyone has a neighbour on each side. They guard the whole ring together.
pros: Everyone has neighbours.
The team shares the ring.
cons: Gaps open at the seam.
A gap can sit next to a teammate.

pairs.tendency: A player with a private reason to win may push a threat across the join onto a neighbour. The team sees the threat move, and nobody is sure why.
pros: A hidden aim is easy to act on.
Threats can pass between players.
cons: Players doubt each other.
Team talk gets cautious.

pairs.tendency: Two teams on a loop meet from both sides, so a team cannot stay behind its own line. Each side is also the other's back.
pros: Teams meet on both flanks.
Both sides are open.
cons: Teams cannot keep a safe line.
A team can be surrounded on a ring.

pairs.tendency: The traitor's path across the join is hard to follow, so suspicion grows each time a piece disappears from one side. Players watch both edges for a returning piece.
pros: The traitor can slip away.
A path across the seam is hidden.
cons: Players suspect each other.
A watcher may miss the crossing.

pairs.tendency: Moves are sent by letter. A letter says leave east, and the reply says where the piece arrives in the west. A long gap lies between each pair.
pros: The join is explained in writing.
The reply holds a surprise.
cons: Letters can cross.
A mistaken square takes weeks to fix.

pairs.tendency: The absent player's pieces travel round the loop on their own, and other players can meet them at any point. The ghost moves with no one at the seat.
pros: A ghost piece roams.
Players meet it from behind.
cons: Nobody can ask it anything.
Its route may block a live player.

pairs.tendency: The game master describes a world where the edges meet and tells travellers they have come back to a place they know. Players learn the ring from the game master's voice.
pros: The world has a shape.
A trip can bring travellers back.
cons: The game master has to keep the joins straight.
Players may not trust the description.

pairs.tendency: A game chalked on the ground as a loop lets players run round, and passers-by can join at any point. A stranger steps in at the chalk line.
pros: Anyone can join mid-way.
The loop has no front.
cons: Players cross each other's paths.
The loop can be crowded.

pairs.tendency: The lone player faces many from both sides, since there is no wall to back against. The many close in from the left and the right at once.
pros: The many can surround one.
The lone player runs in a circle.
cons: The lone player cannot hide.
The many get in each other's way.

pairs.tendency: A solo player's piece circles, and the board never traps it in a corner. The player makes laps and watches what comes round.
pros: There is no dead end.
The player can keep going.
cons: The board gives no stop.
The player may circle without gain.

pairs.tendency: Dice move pieces round the loop forever, so luck decides who laps whom. A long run of high throws puts one piece a lap ahead.
pros: The loop never runs out.
Anyone can catch up.
cons: A lap can come from a few throws.
Players have nothing to steer by.

pairs.tendency: A low roll can be softened since the loop comes round again. A player who lands short gets another chance on the next lap.
pros: A miss is not final.
The next lap offers a retry.
cons: Each retry costs a full lap.
A soft landing slows the lead.

pairs.tendency: Players plan routes through the join, and a small amount of luck from the dice changes where a piece ends. A route that looked clear can be crossed by a throw.
pros: Routes use the join.
A little luck adds change.
cons: Plans can be broken by a throw.
Players need to keep both edges in mind.

pairs.tendency: With no dice, the join gives routes to work out, and opening strategies differ from those on a flat board. A player thinks in rings.
pros: Routes go through the seam.
Openings change.
cons: Players need time to learn the ring.
Mistakes at the seam are costly.

pairs.tendency: A throw names a direction, and with joined edges every direction lands on a square, so the sign always points to a place. The reader finds meaning there.
pros: The sign always has a place to land.
A direction has no dead end.
cons: Readers keep walking round.
The same square may come up often.

pairs.tendency: Players moving round a ring try to arrive at the same square together. They sense each other's pace and speed up or slow down.
pros: Pace is shared.
Players read each other.
cons: A missed beat shows at once.
Players can circle for a long time without meeting.

pairs.tendency: A roll on the table says you travel west, and the story brings the traveller home from the east. The roll brings the traveller back.
pros: The story curves back.
The dice send a traveller round.
cons: The same places come up again.
A story can repeat itself.

pairs.tendency: Everyone sees all the pieces and how the edges connect, so planning runs across the join. Nothing is hidden, so the only puzzle is where the ring leads.
pros: Every route can be worked out.
Rivals see the same ring.
cons: Nobody can spring a surprise.
Players take time to plan.

pairs.tendency: Hidden cards hide which way a player will jump, so watchers cannot tell if the join will be used. A player with a jump card looks like any other.
pros: A jump is a surprise.
The join stays secret.
cons: Watchers guard both ways.
A false alarm costs a turn.

pairs.tendency: A hidden role might be across the join, so players check both edges for a returning piece. A player seen on the left may be the same as one seen on the right.
pros: An identity can be mistaken.
Players watch more of the board.
cons: Suspicion falls on the wrong player.
Careful checking takes time.

pairs.tendency: Clues are placed on the board, and a clue at the right edge points to the left. Investigators follow it across the seam.
pros: Clues reach across the seam.
A trail has no end.
cons: Searchers can go round twice.
A clue at the edge is easy to miss.

pairs.tendency: A player pretending to head one way can slip across the join. The others think the piece is going away when it is coming back.
pros: A feint can use the join.
The piece seems to vanish.
cons: Others doubt every move.
A bluff can be called when the piece comes round.

pairs.tendency: Newcomers find that the edges join when a piece goes off one side and is told it came back on the other. The ring is learned by walking off the board.
pros: The join is found by trying.
A newcomer learns by doing.
cons: A first try wastes a move.
The rule is easy to miss until it is tested.

pairs.tendency: The one who knows can only point to a square, and the others puzzle over whether a hint across the edge counts. A pointing finger at the left edge may mean the right.
pros: A pointer can mean two places.
Guessers think in rings.
cons: A hint may be read wrongly.
The pointer cannot explain.

pairs.tendency: Exploring west past the last known area reveals an area already seen in the east. The map folds back onto itself as it is turned over.
pros: The map closes on itself.
Explorers find old ground.
cons: New ground runs out.
The hidden part is smaller than it looked.

pairs.tendency: The open hand shows all the jump cards, and the player who plays it can use the join. Others see the jump coming but cannot stop it.
pros: Jumps are in plain view.
The player has more routes.
cons: There is no surprise in the open hand.
The player carries two hands at once.

pairs.tendency: Scores come from squares held, and nobody can tell from the layout alone because the board has no edge to mark off areas. Players guess who holds more.
pros: Scores are hard to read.
The board looks even.
cons: Guessing takes the place of counting.
Players doubt the final tally.

pairs.tendency: One piece moves each turn, and the next player sees where it came out. A move across the join is seen once it is done.
pros: Each move is clear.
The next player sees a crossing.
cons: Players wait their turn.
A crossing can undo a plan.

pairs.tendency: All pieces move at the same moment, so two may head for the same square across the join. They arrive together from opposite sides.
pros: Moves meet on the seam.
No player sits out a turn.
cons: Pieces may collide.
A clash is only seen when the reveal comes.

pairs.tendency: The quickest player grabs a move, and pieces slide round at any moment. A piece can cross the seam before anyone else can react.
pros: Fast hands get ahead.
The join gives a quick escape.
cons: Slow players are left behind.
The board changes without notice.

pairs.tendency: With a clock running, there is little time to work out where the join leads. Players hurry and sometimes land on squares they did not mean to.
pros: Moves are quick.
The join is used by instinct.
cons: Mistakes come from rush.
A player can lose time counting.

pairs.tendency: One move a day on a loop brings a piece back to its starting square after some weeks. Players watch their own pieces return.
pros: A piece comes home.
A full lap takes weeks.
cons: The wait is built in.
A lap is slow to see.

pairs.tendency: Pieces move slowly round the loop, and players watch them circle. A pause before each move shows how far the piece has come.
pros: Movement is calm.
Players watch closely.
cons: Few things happen in a turn.
A lap takes a long time.

pairs.tendency: Pieces speed up round the loop, so laps get shorter and meetings from behind come sooner. The last laps pass in a blur.
pros: Laps get quicker.
Pieces meet more often.
cons: Thinking time shrinks.
Later laps are hard to follow.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn lets a piece make a whole lap in one go. A lucky player goes round and lands behind a rival.
pros: A lap can be done in one turn.
Pieces jump ahead.
cons: A piece may overshoot.
The next player is left behind.

pairs.tendency: The first stage is a flat board, and in the second the edges join. What was a wall in stage one becomes a door.
pros: The board changes shape.
The first stage sets up the second.
cons: Stage one plans can fail.
Players have to learn a new board.

pairs.tendency: A loop board models a closed system such as a canal where water circles round. Anything poured in at one point comes back round.
pros: The model has no outside.
Changes come back round.
cons: Players see a closed system.
Nothing leaves the loop.

pairs.tendency: Each group lives along a ring and has neighbours on both sides. A farming group sits next to a town on one side and a river group on the other.
pros: Each group has two neighbours.
Players see both sides of a border.
cons: A group cannot turn its back.
Neighbours on both sides can make demands.

pairs.tendency: A resource travels round the loop, so what upstream takes the downstream misses, and the downstream is also upstream. A player who takes too much finds the shortage coming back round.
pros: Overuse returns to the user.
Players see a cycle.
cons: A shortage arrives late.
The cause is hard to trace.

pairs.tendency: A polluted square's effect travels round the board and returns to the sender after some rounds. A player who dirtied the river finds it dirty at their own door.
pros: A harm comes back to its maker.
Players learn to look ahead.
cons: The harm shows up rounds later.
The sender may be blamed too late.

pairs.tendency: The group tries joining the edges as a rule and plays on. They see how a loop changes where people go.
pros: A rule can change the board.
Players compare two boards.
cons: Players need time to adjust.
A rule can take a round to show its effect.

pairs.tendency: The group talks afterwards about whether the loop felt like home, and which edge they stopped guarding. The talk starts from where each piece went.
pros: The talk starts from the board.
Players recall their routes.
cons: The shape of the board gets noticed.
A strange feeling may be hard to explain.

pairs.tendency: A piece that crossed the join leaves a mark where it came out. The marks pile up until the seam shows on the board.
pros: The seam is visible.
Crossings leave a trace.
cons: A mark cannot be undone.
The board fills with old crossings.

pairs.tendency: A board without edges says that nowhere is far from anywhere. A game about a country built this way argues that no region is remote.
pros: The board makes a point.
Players think about distance.
cons: The point may not suit every topic.
The ring may hide real differences between places.

pairs.tendency: Players who sit on opposite sides of the table become neighbours on the board, so a real promise made to the person across the table matters.
pros: Promises cross the table.
Friends can become rivals.
cons: Real feelings enter the game.
A broken promise lasts beyond the game.

pairs.tendency: Values are counted on a loop, so a score ends where it began. A player who gathers kindness points circles back to the first kind act.
pros: A score can come full circle.
Players see their values return.
cons: The count has no top.
Players lose track of what the number means.

pairs.tendency: Players rehearse a world where no one lives at the edge, such as a village in which every house has neighbours on both sides. They find out how it feels to have no outskirts.
pros: Players try a place with no outskirts.
Every house has someone on both sides.
cons: There is no far corner to retreat to.
The real world may have edges after all.

pairs.tendency: Each space a player lands on earns one yes-or-no question for the keeper of the secret, so the dice decide how many questions each player gets.
pros: Questions arrive at a steady pace.
The path shows who has asked the most.
cons: A low roll leaves a player with little to go on.
A player near the end may guess before knowing enough.

pairs.tendency: The secret is one card from the first hand. Players ask a question, take a card and pass the rest on, so the answers describe a pile that keeps shrinking.
pros: Every answer rules out some cards.
Picks tell the table what each player is chasing.
cons: The secret card can be taken before anyone names it.
Slow when many players wait to pick.

pairs.tendency: Asking costs coins. Players offer coins for the right to ask, and the highest offer gets its question answered with a yes or a no.
pros: Each question has a price.
Offers show how much a player thinks they already know.
cons: A player with few coins is shut out of asking.
Coins can run out before anyone makes a guess.

pairs.tendency: Every extra question makes a right guess worth more, but a wrong guess throws away the points built up so far.
pros: Each question raises the prize.
Players watch for the moment someone stops asking.
cons: One wrong guess wipes out the points.
A player can wait and copy a guess made late.

pairs.tendency: The secret is a place on a map. Questions like "is it in the north?" cut the map down, and players put pieces on the areas they think are still open.
pros: Answers cut the map into smaller parts.
Pieces show where each player is looking.
cons: A piece on a ruled-out area is stuck there.
Everyone can see which area a player backs.

pairs.tendency: A job spot gives its owner a question to ask that turn, and a spot taken by one player is closed to the rest.
pros: Only some players ask each turn.
Choosing a spot is a choice about timing.
cons: A blocked player waits with no question.
The first to place can gather several answers before others get one.

pairs.tendency: The secret is a pattern of colours or shapes. Players ask about one row at a time, then place tiles that match what the answers said.
pros: Each answer fixes one part of the pattern.
Players can check their tiles against the answers.
cons: One misread answer throws off a whole row.
Two players can read the same answer in different ways.

pairs.tendency: Every question costs a card from the hand, so a player chooses between asking now and keeping the card for the final guess.
pros: Each question is a choice about what to give up.
Players count how many questions they have left.
cons: A player with few cards cannot ask more.
Saving cards can leave a player short of answers.

pairs.tendency: The player who wins a trick gets to ask the keeper one question, so a high card turns into a clue.
pros: Winning a trick brings an answer.
The cards played tell the table about hands.
cons: A player who keeps losing tricks never asks.
The player who leads collects most of the clues.

pairs.tendency: Players talk over what the keeper has said, trade answers they heard and promise to share later ones.
pros: Answers travel between players.
Players learn who keeps their word.
cons: A player can pass on an answer that is false.
Long talks slow down the questions.

pairs.tendency: A yes earns the asker a card from the pile and a no earns nothing, so players gather matching cards while they narrow down the secret.
pros: Answers give cards along with clues.
Each player works on two goals at once.
cons: A run of no answers gives the asker nothing.
A player may ask to win cards and ignore the clue.

pairs.tendency: The secret is one spot on a map the players build. A player asks where it sits, then lays a tile that agrees with the answer.
pros: The shared map records every answer.
Tiles make each answer visible to all.
cons: A misplaced tile blocks the way for others.
Late tiles have few places left to go.

pairs.tendency: Each question is a call and the keeper's yes or no is the reply. The next player builds a new question on that answer.
pros: Each question grows from the last answer.
The game moves along as a chain.
cons: A player who missed the last answer loses the chain.
An early wrong turn leads the whole chain off course.

pairs.tendency: Nobody talks. The keeper nods or shakes their head, and players ask by pointing at things on the table.
pros: Questions and answers are all gestures.
Players watch each other closely.
cons: A gesture can be read in two ways.
A long question cannot be put into one point.

pairs.tendency: A player may change a rule, such as allowing three questions in one turn or letting the keeper answer "maybe".
pros: Players can change how many questions they get.
A new rule can open a path to the secret.
cons: A changed rule can make an earlier answer unclear.
Arguments about a new rule use up the time.

pairs.tendency: Players ask as their characters, and the keeper answers as the world would. A detective asks things a child would not think of.
pros: Each character asks from what they know.
Players look at the secret from a new angle.
cons: A character may ask something that does not help.
Staying in character slows the guessing.

pairs.tendency: A question is earned by stacking or flicking something first. A steady hand wins more answers.
pros: Skill with the hands buys extra answers.
Everyone watches each flick.
cons: A shaky hand leaves a player with no questions.
A quick thinker can fall behind through clumsy fingers.

pairs.tendency: The secret sits somewhere on a map that the players draw as they go. Each yes or no adds a line or a mark to the shared sheet.
pros: Answers turn into marks on the sheet.
The sheet shows what is known.
cons: A wrong line misleads the players who come later.
The map gets crowded as questions pile up.

pairs.tendency: The first player to name the secret wins, so every question is a step in a race and a quick guess can end the game early.
pros: The goal is clear to everyone.
A fast guess ends the game.
cons: A wrong guess leaves a player behind.
A slow thinker is left out.

pairs.tendency: Right guesses add points and wrong guesses take some away. When the questions run out, the highest total wins.
pros: Careful questions earn points.
Small guesses can score along the way.
cons: A player may hold back a guess to wait for more answers.
Keeping the count adds work for the keeper.

pairs.tendency: A wrong guess knocks a player out, so each question is a way to avoid being the one who guesses wrong.
pros: Players ask more before they guess.
Every guess carries a risk of leaving.
cons: Knocked-out players wait and watch.
The last players left may hear most of the answers.

pairs.tendency: The whole table asks the keeper questions together against a clock that counts down. If nobody names the secret in time, everyone loses.
pros: Players share every answer.
Questions get split between people.
cons: One careless guess hurts all.
A quiet player can be left out of the asking.

pairs.tendency: Players work as one team to name the secret, taking turns to ask while the keeper answers for all.
pros: Every answer helps the whole team.
Players can plan questions together.
cons: A loud player may take over the asking.
Too many ideas can crowd out the next question.

pairs.tendency: Each player holds a secret aim, and a question may help that aim more than the shared search. Players ask what suits themselves while looking as if they ask about the secret.
pros: Questions can serve two purposes.
Players read each other's questions for clues.
cons: A question may confuse the others by accident.
Players may suspect a plain question.

pairs.tendency: The secret is the missing piece of a story. Each answer adds a line to the tale, and the game ends when the story is told.
pros: Answers become parts of the story.
The tale shapes the next question.
cons: A story can wander away from the secret.
The ending depends on how the answers were read.

pairs.tendency: Players ask questions about a secret, but no guess scores anything. The game stops when the group stops wanting to ask.
pros: Players ask for the sake of asking.
Players have time to talk afterwards.
cons: Nobody knows when to stop.
Players can drift away without an end.

pairs.tendency: Before the questions start, each player says what they want from the secret, such as finding it fastest or asking the fewest questions.
pros: Players choose their own measure.
Two players can finish happy with different results.
cons: The group cannot compare results easily.
A player can change their goal after seeing the answers.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins by guessing. The player who asks the question that gives the secret away, or guesses wrong, is the loser.
pros: Questions are asked with care.
The game ends at one clear moment.
cons: Everyone else is safe at once.
Players may avoid asking.

pairs.tendency: A secret is never quite named. Each answer opens a new question, and players aim to keep the questions coming and never finish.
pros: Questions never run dry.
The game can go on for hours.
cons: There is no end to point at.
Players who want an answer may grow restless.

pairs.tendency: The keeper's answers may be changed, refused or a joke, so no chain of questions leads to the secret.
pros: Players see that the questions go nowhere.
The game shows what a fair answer looks like.
cons: Players can feel cheated.
Some players give up asking.

pairs.tendency: The secret is how a laid-out set of cards can be cleared. A lone player asks yes-or-no questions of a helper who knows the answer, then moves cards to match.
pros: A helper can point out a path.
The lone player still makes each move.
cons: Answers can narrow the choices too far.
A player gets stuck if the answers are unclear.

pairs.tendency: Each short game has its own secret, and the player who names the most of them wins the set.
pros: Each game starts with a new secret.
Early games teach the players how to ask.
cons: One slow game can decide the set.
A keeper has to invent many secrets.

pairs.tendency: Each question costs a point, and each wrong guess costs several more. The player with the fewest points when the secret is named wins.
pros: Players ask only what they need.
Careful players score low.
cons: Short games end with few points to compare.
A bold guess can lose a lot at once.

pairs.tendency: Questions are counted, and a player has to name the secret on exactly the tenth question, not before and not after.
pros: Players count their questions.
A guess is timed and chosen.
cons: Asking too many ends a hope of winning.
A player who knows the answer early has to wait.

pairs.tendency: The player who names the secret first is the one who loses, so everyone asks questions that help others and hide their own idea.
pros: Players ask questions that point away from the answer.
Everyone hides what they know.
cons: The questions can become confusing.
The keeper may have to say yes to a question that gives the secret away.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a separate keeper and a separate secret, and they all ask at once without watching each other's board.
pros: Everyone asks at the same pace.
Players do not wait on one another.
cons: Nobody learns from another player's questions.
The game feels like several quiet games side by side.

pairs.tendency: Players can use their turn to attack a rival, such as taking away a clue card, instead of asking the keeper.
pros: A rival can lose a clue.
Players choose between asking and attacking.
cons: A player can be hit just before a guess.
Attacks slow down the questions.

pairs.tendency: A question's answer changes the board, such as closing off a path, and rivals feel the change without being targeted.
pros: Answers reshape the board.
Players react to what has changed.
cons: A rival's question can close a player's path.
It is hard to tell who caused a change.

pairs.tendency: The whole table works against the game, with one keeper answering for the game itself. Together they ask and then agree on a final guess.
pros: Players share their answers.
Everyone has a say in the guess.
cons: A single wrong guess can end the game for all.
One player can end up speaking for the group.

pairs.tendency: Players share answers to reach the secret, but each also has a private reason to be the one who names it.
pros: Players trade answers freely.
A player can hold back a last question.
cons: The one who names the secret takes the credit.
A player may stop sharing near the end.

pairs.tendency: Two teams race to name the secret. Team-mates talk about which question to ask next, and the rival team hears the answers.
pros: Team-mates plan each question.
Each team can learn from the other's answers.
cons: A team that talks loudly gives away its plan.
A small team has fewer ideas to draw on.

pairs.tendency: One player secretly knows the secret and answers truthfully only when it suits them, while the rest ask questions and suspect each other.
pros: Questions double as tests of the traitor.
The traitor can steer the guessers.
cons: Players may stop trusting every answer.
An honest answer may be taken as a lie.

pairs.tendency: Each question and each answer travels in a letter, so one round can take days. Players have time to think before they write back.
pros: There is time to plan each question.
Answers are written down and can be kept.
cons: The game takes weeks to finish.
A lost letter stops the game.

pairs.tendency: The keeper is not at the table. They left their answers on cards or in a book, and players check it for each yes or no.
pros: The keeper's answers stay fixed.
Players cannot talk the keeper into a hint.
cons: A gap in the answers leaves a question unanswered.
The keeper cannot explain an unclear answer.

pairs.tendency: The game master holds the secret and answers every question while also running the world around it.
pros: One person controls the answers.
The questions can be tied to the story.
cons: The game master has a lot to track.
Answers depend on one person's memory.

pairs.tendency: The game is played in a street or market, and passers-by can ask a question or hear the answers.
pros: New players join at any time.
A crowd can work on the secret together.
cons: Late joiners miss earlier answers.
Players may talk over the answers.

pairs.tendency: One player knows the secret and the others work together to find it. The lone player answers every question alone.
pros: The group can share out the questions.
The lone player sees every move.
cons: The lone player answers a flood of questions.
The group may agree too quickly on a wrong guess.

pairs.tendency: A lone player draws a secret card and asks a deck or a book of answers. Each question is checked against the key.
pros: A player can work at their own speed.
The key gives the same answer each time.
cons: There is nobody to argue with.
Once the key is read the game is over.

pairs.tendency: The secret and the answers come from dice or random draws, so a question may be answered by a roll that knows nothing of the secret.
pros: Every game plays out differently.
A lucky roll can end the game quickly.
cons: A careful question can still get a random answer.
Players cannot learn a method from earlier games.

pairs.tendency: Dice can change an answer, but players hold a few tokens to re-ask a question or ask for the answer again.
pros: Tokens soften an unlucky answer.
Players choose when to spend a token.
cons: Spent tokens leave a player short later.
Re-asking slows the turn.

pairs.tendency: Most of the game is careful questioning, with a small random element such as a coin that sometimes flips the answer.
pros: Careful players are usually rewarded.
A coin keeps the result from being sure.
cons: A flipped answer can mislead a careful player.
A lucky guess can beat a long search.

pairs.tendency: The secret is hidden by a set of clear rules, and a careful player can always find it by choosing the right questions.
pros: A careful order of questions is rewarded.
The result follows the player's reasoning.
cons: Newcomers rarely win.
Players can solve the secret on paper.

pairs.tendency: Players throw dice or coins and read the result as a hint, then ask yes-or-no questions about what the sign might mean.
pros: The throw gives players something to ask about.
Two players can read the same throw in different ways.
cons: The sign does not point to one answer.
Players may argue over its meaning.

pairs.tendency: Players try to ask the same question at the same moment, and the keeper answers when two or more match.
pros: Players learn to read each other.
Matching questions build a shared picture.
cons: Players who are out of step ask nothing.
The keeper may wait a long time for a match.

pairs.tendency: A dice roll looks up a story event on a table, and players ask yes-or-no questions about who or what appeared.
pros: The story gives players new things to ask about.
A roll adds a clue.
cons: A roll can send the questions in a new direction.
The table may hide a clue the keeper did not plan.

pairs.tendency: Everything on the board is open, and only the secret stays hidden. Players ask about the one thing they cannot see.
pros: Players know what is hidden and what is not.
Questions can be aimed with care.
cons: A guess shows nothing to the others that they could not see.
There are no hidden cards to bluff with.

pairs.tendency: Each player holds cards nobody else can see, and a question can be about the keeper's secret or about another player's hand.
pros: Questions can reach the cards in a hand.
Players learn what others hold.
cons: A question about a hand shows what the asker holds.
Hands can distract from the secret.

pairs.tendency: Some players have secret roles, and a question to the keeper may also work as a way to find out who has which role.
pros: Questions can test roles.
Players read each other's questions.
cons: A role may be given away by what is asked.
Players may become cautious about asking anything.

pairs.tendency: The keeper's answers are clues, and players work out the secret by putting yes and no answers together.
pros: Each answer adds to a chain of reasoning.
Players compare their notes.
cons: One missed note throws off a whole line of thought.
Players with the same notes reach the same guess.

pairs.tendency: Players can ask a question they already know the answer to, or look pleased at a no, so others think they are close.
pros: A question can send others the wrong way.
Players watch each other's faces.
cons: A bluff costs a question.
Others may stop believing any player.

pairs.tendency: The secret is a rule of the game itself. Players find it by testing moves and asking whether each was allowed.
pros: Each answer shows a bit of the rule.
New players learn by doing.
cons: A player who breaks the rule gets no points for that move.
Some players may never find the rule.

pairs.tendency: The keeper may only answer yes or no, and cannot add a word of hint. Players have to build everything from those two words.
pros: Answers are short and clear.
The keeper has little to give away by mistake.
cons: A question that is clumsily worded draws a useless answer.
The keeper cannot help a stuck player.

pairs.tendency: The map starts face down. A yes lets a player turn one area over, and a no leaves it hidden.
pros: Answers uncover the map.
Players plan which area to ask about.
cons: A run of no answers shows nothing of the map.
The first to uncover a section shares it with everyone.

pairs.tendency: One hand is laid face up and the keeper's secret is one of those cards. Players ask about the open cards.
pros: Players can see all the options.
Questions can target the open hand.
cons: There is little left to hide.
The game can end on the first few questions.

pairs.tendency: Each player's points are hidden, and a right answer adds to a secret tally. Nobody is sure who is ahead.
pros: Players guess at each other's scores.
A late guess can still change the result.
cons: Players cannot tell who leads.
The final tally can surprise the whole table.

pairs.tendency: Players ask in order round the table, one question per turn, with everyone else listening to every answer.
pros: Everyone hears the same answers.
Each player has a clear turn.
cons: Waiting is long with many players.
Questions asked earlier may be forgotten.

pairs.tendency: Every player writes one question and the keeper answers all of them together, so the table gets many answers at the same time.
pros: Answers come in a burst.
Nobody waits for a turn.
cons: The keeper has a lot to answer.
Two players may ask the same question.

pairs.tendency: Anyone can shout a question at any moment, and the keeper answers the first one they hear.
pros: Questions fly fast.
A quick player gets more answers.
cons: Quieter players get fewer questions.
The keeper can lose track of who asked what.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a short time to think of a question, and when the sand runs out the turn is lost.
pros: Questions are quick.
The clock keeps the game moving.
cons: A player who is thinking may lose the turn.
Rushed questions can repeat an earlier one.

pairs.tendency: One question a day goes to the keeper, and the answer arrives the next morning. A secret may take weeks to find.
pros: Players have time to think between questions.
The game fits into daily life.
cons: A long wait can make players forget.
Players may leave before the end.

pairs.tendency: A pause is built in before every question, so players breathe and think, and ask only once the pause has passed.
pros: Questions are slower and more thought out.
The table stays calm.
cons: The game takes longer.
Restless players find the pause hard.

pairs.tendency: Each round the time for a question shrinks, so early questions are slow and later ones have to be fired off quickly.
pros: The pace picks up as the secret gets closer.
Late rounds feel rushed.
cons: Late questions are less careful.
Players who think slowly fall behind.

pairs.tendency: A player who gets a yes can ask another question straight away, so a long run of yes answers can last many questions.
pros: A yes opens another question.
A lucky player can learn much in one turn.
cons: A run of yes answers helps one player more than others.
Others wait while that player asks.

pairs.tendency: In the first stage players ask only about colour, in the second only about shape, and in the third they may guess.
pros: Each stage narrows the questions.
The secret is cut into parts.
cons: A wrong answer early makes the later stages harder.
A later stage can feel cramped.

pairs.tendency: The secret is how a system behaves, such as where water goes in a village. Yes-or-no questions test the system, and the model answers by what would happen.
pros: Players learn by testing the model.
Answers follow the rules of the system.
cons: A question the model cannot answer stops the game.
Players need to know the system first.

pairs.tendency: Each player asks as a group in the problem, such as a farmer or a shopkeeper, and the keeper answers from the same world.
pros: Each group asks what matters to it.
Players see the problem from several places.
cons: A question from one group may mean little to another.
The keeper answers differently for each role.

pairs.tendency: Every question draws on a shared pool of questions, so what one player asks is gone for the rest.
pros: The pool is shared by everyone.
Players watch how many questions remain.
cons: Greedy asking leaves others none.
When the pool is empty, the guessing stops.

pairs.tendency: The keeper's answer arrives only a few rounds later, so a player asks now and learns what it meant after other questions have been asked.
pros: Answers come together in batches.
Players keep track of what was asked.
cons: An old answer can contradict a newer idea.
Players forget what the answer was for.

pairs.tendency: The group agrees a new rule, such as "a no costs the asker a point", then plays on to see what questions people ask.
pros: The rule changes how players ask.
The group learns from one test.
cons: The new rule may remove a useful question.
Players may argue over the rule.

pairs.tendency: After the secret is named, players go back through each question and talk about what the answers did and did not tell them.
pros: Players see how they reasoned.
The keeper can explain a hard answer.
cons: The talk can take longer than the game.
Players may disagree over what an answer meant.

pairs.tendency: Every answer changes the game for ever: a card is torn or a mark inked, and that question cannot be asked again.
pros: Each question counts.
Players ask with care.
cons: A hasty question can spoil later games.
The next game starts with fewer cards.

pairs.tendency: The rules of asking make a point, for instance that a question only gets a yes if it names a person. Players learn the point by seeing what gets a yes.
pros: The answers show what the game values.
Players see the point by playing.
cons: Some players may not notice the point.
A player may find the rule at odds with what they asked.

pairs.tendency: Players put real things at stake, such as a promise to wash the dishes, so each question and guess carries a cost outside the game.
pros: Players ask carefully.
The result carries into the day.
cons: A friend can feel hurt by a wrong guess.
Players may refuse to guess.

pairs.tendency: Points for kindness or health are scored by asking, so players find that the questions they ask change to chase the points.
pros: Questions follow what scores.
The game shows how numbers can steer players.
cons: A caring act can turn into a number to chase.
Players may ask for the points and forget the secret.

pairs.tendency: Players ask yes-or-no questions about a way of living that does not exist yet, and the keeper answers as that future would.
pros: Questions test an imagined world.
Players can try out a future safely.
cons: The keeper may not know the answers.
Answers may differ between games.

pairs.tendency: A lone player rolls a dice and moves a piece along a path of laid-out cards, flipping each card landed on. The aim is to clear every card before the path runs out.
pros: The dice choose which card turns up next.
The path gives a clear picture of the game.
cons: A low roll can leave cards stuck at the far end.
The player has no choice over where to land.

pairs.tendency: The player takes cards one at a time from a spread and passes the rest to an imaginary neighbour who takes the next one. The spread is cleared in order.
pros: Each pick leaves a smaller spread.
The player chooses the order.
cons: The pick that clears the table is hard to see early.
With one real player the passing has nobody to learn from.

pairs.tendency: The player bids cards or counters to unlock the next card in the layout, and the layout answers with a price.
pros: Every card has a price.
The player decides how much to spend.
cons: Overspending leaves nothing for the last cards.
No rival to outbid, so prices feel fixed.

pairs.tendency: The player flips cards from the layout one by one for points, and may stop before the next flip, or carry on and risk getting stuck.
pros: Each flip can add a card to the cleared pile.
The player chooses when to stop.
cons: A stuck layout ends the game on the spot.
One flip too many can undo a long run.

pairs.tendency: The layout is a map of regions, and the player puts counters on each region until all are held.
pros: A map shows what is left to hold.
The player can see how many counters remain.
cons: Counters spent on one region are gone from another.
The map does not push back.

pairs.tendency: The player has a few workers and puts them on spots in the layout to clear cards. A worker on a spot is used up for that turn.
pros: Each spot has a clear job.
The player plans turn by turn.
cons: A mistake in placing leaves a card stuck.
Only a few workers can do many jobs.

pairs.tendency: The layout is a set of cards to arrange into a pattern, such as runs of one colour. The game is won when every card sits in its place.
pros: The pattern is the goal.
The player can see progress.
cons: One wrong card can block the row.
Moving a card back costs a turn.

pairs.tendency: The player holds a hand of cards used to clear the layout, and decides which to play now and which to keep for a later card.
pros: Hand cards are limited.
Choosing the order is the game.
cons: A wasted card can leave a layout card unreachable.
The player may run out of cards before the layout is cleared.

pairs.tendency: The player plays a card against a card from the layout, and the higher card wins the trick. The layout is cleared by winning the tricks.
pros: A high card wins one trick.
A clear order of cards helps the player plan.
cons: The layout can hold all the high cards.
The player has no rival to read.

pairs.tendency: With no one to bargain with, the player trades with the layout itself by swapping a card for a card, and the game sets the rate.
pros: The rate is fixed and known.
Swaps help clear the stuck cards.
cons: A swap made in haste cannot be taken back.
There is nobody to persuade.

pairs.tendency: The player gathers matching cards from the layout into groups. The table is cleared when every group is complete.
pros: Matching cards give a clear target.
The player counts what is left.
cons: One missing card blocks a group.
Sets may take cards another set needs.

pairs.tendency: The player lays tiles one at a time to complete the layout, and each tile has to fit the edges of those beside it.
pros: The finished layout is visible.
Each tile limits the next.
cons: A tile in the wrong place can wall off a corner.
A run of the wrong tiles ends the game.

pairs.tendency: The player calls a card and the layout responds with the next card, and the exchange goes back and forth.
pros: The layout answers each move.
The game has a rhythm.
cons: The player is both caller and answerer.
A call with no answer ends the game.

pairs.tendency: Nobody talks, which a lone player does anyway, so silence has little to change here. The player plays out the layout without a word.
pros: The table stays quiet.
The player can focus on the cards.
cons: The rule removes nothing from the game.
The silence is easy to forget.

pairs.tendency: The player may change a rule of the layout, such as letting a card move one more space, so the game being cleared is not the one that began.
pros: The player can loosen a stuck position.
The rules become a tool.
cons: An easy rule change can make the win feel empty.
Nobody checks the changes.

pairs.tendency: The player acts as a character working through the layout, saying what that character does with each card.
pros: The cards turn into a short story.
The player thinks as a character.
cons: A character's choice may differ from the move that clears the layout.
Telling the story slows play.

pairs.tendency: The layout is set up as a tower or a spread of tokens, and the player clears it by pulling and flicking without knocking the rest over.
pros: Hands decide the result.
The layout is easy to read.
cons: A shaky moment can ruin a run.
Planning counts for less than steadiness.

pairs.tendency: The player draws the layout as the game goes and clears each area once it has been drawn.
pros: The map grows with play.
The drawing records progress.
cons: A smudged area can hide a card.
The player may spend more time drawing than playing.

pairs.tendency: Several people play their own layouts at the same time and compare how each one ended.
pros: Everyone plays at their own pace.
Results can be compared at the end.
cons: Nobody affects another player.
Players may lose interest in each other's layouts.

pairs.tendency: A rival is added who can take cards out of the layout, so the lone player now plays against a person as well as the cards.
pros: The rival can block a move.
The player has someone to beat and the layout.
cons: The layout may be cleared by the rival, not the player.
The game stops being a game played alone.

pairs.tendency: Several people work on the same layout, and a card moved by one changes what the others can reach.
pros: Players share a layout.
A move shows up on the board.
cons: One player's move can close another's way.
Players can block each other without meaning to.

pairs.tendency: The whole table works together to clear one layout, so a win means every card is cleared and a loss means the group is stuck.
pros: Players share one goal.
Everyone helps plan.
cons: A single error is shared by all.
A bossy player can take over the layout.

pairs.tendency: Players work together to clear a layout, but each wants the last card for themselves.
pros: The layout is cleared together.
Each player has a personal reason to help.
cons: A player may keep a card back.
Players may argue about who takes the last card.

pairs.tendency: Two teams each work on their own layout, and the first to clear theirs wins.
pros: Team-mates plan together.
Each team can see how far the other has got.
cons: A stuck team can see the rival pulling ahead.
A team with a stuck layout has no way to catch up.

pairs.tendency: A group tries to clear the layout together while one member secretly moves cards to leave it stuck.
pros: Players watch the moves closely.
A stuck layout makes people suspicious.
cons: A mistake can look like sabotage.
The honest players may stop helping each other.

pairs.tendency: The player makes one move a day and posts the layout state to a friend who writes back with a reply.
pros: The layout can be planned slowly.
A friend sees the state of play.
cons: One move a day makes the game last long.
A letter can go missing in between.

pairs.tendency: Someone who is not at the table has left instructions for how the layout is to be laid out, and the player clears it without being able to ask them.
pros: The instructions are fixed.
The player can think about the absent person.
cons: If an instruction is unclear, nobody can explain.
A gap in the rules stops the game.

pairs.tendency: A game master lays out the layout and decides what each card does, while the player tries to clear it.
pros: The layout can be made for one player.
The master can adapt the cards.
cons: A master can make the layout very easy or very hard.
The game is no longer a pure test against the cards.

pairs.tendency: The layout is chalked on the pavement or spread on a market table, and passers-by can lend a hand.
pros: Strangers can join in.
The layout is seen by everyone nearby.
cons: Too many helpers can crowd the layout.
The solo goal gets lost in the crowd.

pairs.tendency: One player controls the layout while the others, as a group, try to clear it.
pros: The group has a shared target.
The lone player designs the problem.
cons: The lone player answers everyone.
The group can agree too fast.

pairs.tendency: A single player sets out the layout and works through it with nobody else at the table, and compares the result with a friend later.
pros: The game fits a quiet moment.
The player sets the pace.
cons: There is no one to play with.
A stuck layout cannot be shared with anyone.

pairs.tendency: Cards are shuffled into the layout and dealt out at random, so most layouts clear by luck of the draw.
pros: No two layouts are dealt the same.
A lucky layout clears fast.
cons: Some layouts cannot be cleared by anyone.
The player's choices matter little.

pairs.tendency: The layout is dealt at random, but the player holds a few moves that undo a run of low throws, such as a free swap.
pros: A free swap can rescue a stuck position.
The player keeps some control.
cons: Free moves run out.
An awkward deal can still end the game.

pairs.tendency: The player studies the layout and plans a route through it, with a small element of luck in what card comes up next.
pros: A careful plan usually works.
A small surprise keeps each game different.
cons: A late surprise can break a plan.
Planning ahead only goes so far.

pairs.tendency: The whole layout is laid face up, so a careful player can plan every move and a clear solution exists.
pros: The player can work out a route.
Every loss can be traced to a move.
cons: The same layout gives the same answer every time.
Once solved, the layout holds no surprise.

pairs.tendency: The player throws a coin or dice, and the result is read as a hint about which card to turn next.
pros: The throw gives a nudge.
The player reads the hint.
cons: A hint can point two ways.
The layout may not follow the sign.

pairs.tendency: The player tries to sense which card the layout is about to need.
pros: The player learns the layout's pattern.
Success comes from paying close attention.
cons: Nobody can check the sense.
The player may mistake a hunch for a pattern.

pairs.tendency: A roll of the dice looks up an event on a table, and the layout changes to match what happened.
pros: The dice add events to the layout.
The layout turns into a story.
cons: A roll can add a card the player cannot clear.
The table has to be written before play.

pairs.tendency: Every card of the layout is face up from the start, so the player sees the whole puzzle and no card is hidden.
pros: The player can plan to the end.
Nothing is hidden.
cons: A solved layout is quickly done with.
Mistakes come from missed moves, not hidden cards.

pairs.tendency: Some of the layout is face down, so the player works with a hidden hand of cards along with the open ones.
pros: Hidden cards add surprises.
The player makes the most of what is shown.
cons: An unlucky reveal can stop the clearing.
Planning is harder with parts missing.

pairs.tendency: The layout has cards whose real nature is hidden until flipped, such as a friend that is really a trap.
pros: Flips reveal what a card truly is.
The player learns the layout by testing.
cons: A trap can end the game at once.
A hidden card cannot be planned for.

pairs.tendency: The player reasons about which face-down cards are where, using the cards already shown, and clears them in the order the reasoning allows.
pros: Reasoning narrows the choices.
Open cards give clues.
cons: One wrong reading can leave the layout stuck.
The player may need to start again.

pairs.tendency: With no one to fool, the player cannot bluff the cards, so a bluff would have to be aimed at the layout's rules.
pros: Nobody can be deceived.
The player only needs to play honestly.
cons: A bluff has no one to land on.
The skill of lying is lost here.

pairs.tendency: The player does not know all the rules of the layout and finds them by trying a move and seeing whether it is refused.
pros: Each refusal teaches a rule.
The player learns by testing.
cons: A refused move may cost a turn.
The layout may be lost before the rules are known.

pairs.tendency: A helper who can see the answer to the layout can give hints but cannot say what to do.
pros: Hints can unlock a stuck layout.
The helper watches the player's moves.
cons: A hint can be misunderstood.
The helper cannot step in when the player is lost.

pairs.tendency: The layout starts face down, and each card is turned over only when the player reaches that part of the map.
pros: Each flip is a new reveal.
The player learns the layout as they go.
cons: A reveal late in the game can undo earlier choices.
The player cannot plan the whole route.

pairs.tendency: One extra hand is laid face up beside the layout, and the player may use it to clear cards along with their own.
pros: A second hand gives more options.
The open hand is easy to read.
cons: The open hand's cards may be the ones needed.
The player has less to guess about.

pairs.tendency: The player records points in secret, and the layout hides how close the player is to clearing it.
pros: The score stays private.
The player cannot be pushed by a count.
cons: A close finish cannot be seen.
Nobody else can check the points.

pairs.tendency: The player moves, then the layout moves in its own turn, such as a card being added or removed.
pros: The layout acts on its own turn.
The player can plan one move at a time.
cons: The layout can add cards faster than the player clears them.
The player waits through the layout's turn.

pairs.tendency: Several players clear their own layouts at the same time, and all flip their cards together on a signal.
pros: Everyone plays together.
The pace stays equal.
cons: No player can use another's layout.
Slow players are left behind.

pairs.tendency: The player clears the layout without any turns, picking up and placing cards in any order and as fast as their hands allow.
pros: Play flows without a pause.
The player decides the pace.
cons: A hasty move can lock the layout.
There is no break to think.

pairs.tendency: The player has a timer on each move, such as a count of ten, and a card left unplayed goes back into the layout.
pros: The timer sets a pace.
The player has to decide.
cons: A rushed move can block the layout.
A time-out removes cards that would help.

pairs.tendency: The layout stays on a table for a week, and the player makes one move each morning.
pros: The layout can be left and returned to.
One move fits into a morning.
cons: A week-long game is easy to abandon.
Nothing can be changed once the day is over.

pairs.tendency: The player pauses before each card, takes a breath and looks over the whole layout before moving.
pros: The player looks over the layout calmly.
The game feels unhurried.
cons: A game runs long.
A restless player may skip the pause.

pairs.tendency: The layout adds more cards each round, so the player has to clear faster and faster as it grows.
pros: The game picks up pace.
The player sees the layout filling.
cons: Late rounds are crowded.
A slow start is hard to recover from.

pairs.tendency: When the player clears a card of a set colour, they get another go, so one clever move can clear many cards.
pros: A chain of moves can clear a row.
A single move can change the whole layout.
cons: A lucky chain can finish the layout at once.
Missing the trigger leaves no extra move.

pairs.tendency: The layout is cleared in two stages: first sort the cards by colour, then lay them in order.
pros: The first stage sets up the second.
The player can plan stage by stage.
cons: A careless sort makes the second stage hard.
A stuck layout in stage two cannot go back to stage one.

pairs.tendency: The layout is a model of a real place, and clearing it means the system is in balance, such as a village with enough water.
pros: The layout matches the real thing.
The player learns how the parts depend on each other.
cons: A move can have an effect elsewhere.
The model may leave out something real.

pairs.tendency: The player takes each group in turn, such as a farmer or a council, and plays the layout from that group's side.
pros: The player sees the layout from many sides.
Each role has its own aim.
cons: The roles may want opposite things.
One player has to keep every role in mind.

pairs.tendency: The layout draws on one pool of tokens, and every card cleared takes some from the pool.
pros: The pool shows what is left.
Each choice affects the next.
cons: An empty pool ends the game.
Clearing the easy cards first can leave too little for the last ones.

pairs.tendency: A card cleared now changes the layout only a few turns later, so the player has to guess what will happen.
pros: Choices have later results.
The player learns to plan ahead.
cons: A move can be wrong without anyone knowing yet.
The player cannot tell which move caused the problem.

pairs.tendency: The player tests a new rule on the layout, such as clearing two cards at once, and sees how the game changes.
pros: The rule can be tried safely.
The player sees the effect at once.
cons: A new rule may make the layout too easy.
Nobody else checks the result.

pairs.tendency: Once the layout is cleared or stuck, the player and a friend talk through what happened and why.
pros: The talk shows the player's reasoning.
A friend notices what the player missed.
cons: The talk can be longer than the game.
A lone player may have no one to ask.

pairs.tendency: Each card cleared is torn or marked, so the layout is changed for ever and the next game starts from this one.
pros: Each clearing leaves a mark.
The player sees the layout shrink.
cons: A mistake stays on the table.
The next game starts from a worn layout.

pairs.tendency: The way the layout can be cleared makes a point, for instance that cards for the needy are always the last to be reached.
pros: The rules say something about the world.
The player discovers the point by playing.
cons: The point might be missed.
The player may feel the game is lecturing.

pairs.tendency: The player promises something real, such as a day of chores, if the layout cannot be cleared.
pros: The layout carries a real cost.
The player takes each move seriously.
cons: A loss reaches beyond the game.
A friend may not agree to hold the stake.

pairs.tendency: Each card cleared earns a point for something that matters, such as kindness, and the player starts to clear for the points.
pros: The layout turns a value into a number.
The player sees how a score can steer a choice.
cons: The point may replace the thing it stood for.
A player can chase points and miss the meaning.

pairs.tendency: The layout is a picture of a future, such as a village sharing everything, and the player works through it to feel how it would go.
pros: The player tries out an imagined world.
Clearing the layout shows what it would take.
cons: The layout cannot cover everything.
A cleared layout may hide a hard part.

pairs.tendency: The players run several short races along a path, and whoever wins the most races takes the set.
pros: Each short race starts with fresh dice.
A lost first race can be made up for.
cons: One lucky roll decides a single race.
Players can tire of racing the same path.

pairs.tendency: After each short game, the cards are passed round again and drafted afresh, and the games won are added up at the end.
pros: Each draft starts from a new row.
Players learn what others pick.
cons: Cards in each draft are quickly forgotten.
Many drafts add up to a long evening.

pairs.tendency: A series of short auctions is run, and each auction is one game. The player who wins the most auctions wins the set.
pros: Money can be saved for the right game.
An early loss can be a plan.
cons: A player may waste coins on a low-value game.
Coins run out before the last game.

pairs.tendency: Each short game is a round of risking and stopping, and the player who wins the most rounds wins the set.
pros: A single bust costs only one game.
A cautious player can win by staying out of trouble.
cons: A bold player may bust too often.
Players take risks in the last game when behind.

pairs.tendency: Players fight over a small map in each short game. Whoever wins the most maps takes the set.
pros: Every game starts with an empty map.
A player can try a new plan in each game.
cons: A map can be lost in one move.
Setting up each map takes time.

pairs.tendency: Each short game gives a few workers and a few jobs. Games won are counted across the set.
pros: The job spots reset each game.
Players try a different spot each time.
cons: A wrong first choice only costs one game.
The set takes longer to set up each round.

pairs.tendency: In each game players race to build a pattern, and whoever builds more patterns across the games wins.
pros: Tiles are reset each game.
A new pattern is tried each time.
cons: A short game limits how large a pattern can grow.
Players tire of building again.

pairs.tendency: A new hand is dealt each game, and wins are tallied across the set.
pros: A hand can be played all out in a single game.
Players can try a new way each time.
cons: A thin hand costs one game only.
A player cannot carry cards over.

pairs.tendency: Each game is a round of tricks, and the set goes to the player who wins the most rounds.
pros: Each round starts with a new deal.
A lost round can be forgotten.
cons: A string of low hands can lose the set.
Shuffling and dealing takes time between rounds.

pairs.tendency: Between games players make deals, such as swapping a promise to let someone win the next game, and wins still decide the set.
pros: Deals can span several games.
Players learn who they can trust.
cons: A broken deal can sour a later game.
Talk between games slows the set.

pairs.tendency: Each game is a short race to collect a set of cards, and whoever completes the most sets across the games wins.
pros: Every game starts with an empty hand.
Players can chase a different set each time.
cons: A late set may come too late.
Sets cannot be kept from one game to the next.

pairs.tendency: Each game builds a small shared map from tiles, and the player who wins the most maps takes the set.
pros: Every game has a new map.
Players learn which tiles fit.
cons: A tile bag may run out too soon.
Packing away the map between games takes time.

pairs.tendency: Players trade calls and replies in short rounds, and the set goes to whoever outlasts the other the most times.
pros: Every round starts a new chain.
A player who loses one chain can start another.
cons: Calls begin to repeat.
Players run out of fresh words.

pairs.tendency: Several short silent games are played, and the set goes to the team that wins the most without a word.
pros: Players grow used to reading each other.
Each game is over quickly.
cons: A silent mistake is hard to explain.
Players may lose patience with the silence.

pairs.tendency: Between games the winner may change a rule, so the next game is a different game. The count of wins decides the set.
pros: Each game plays differently.
A loser may get a rule that helps.
cons: Players argue over whether the new rule is fair.
Early wins give early control.

pairs.tendency: Each short game is a scene in which players act as characters, and the set is decided by who wins the most scenes.
pros: Each scene is a new episode.
A character can grow over several games.
cons: A character who loses early may be forgotten.
Staying in character takes effort.

pairs.tendency: Players flick or stack in a few short rounds, and the player who wins the most rounds takes the set.
pros: A shaky round is only one game.
Hands warm up over several tries.
cons: Tired hands lose later rounds.
A short round gives little time to recover.

pairs.tendency: A fresh map is drawn in each game, and the maps won are counted at the end.
pros: A new sheet starts each game.
Players try a new drawing each time.
cons: A drawn map takes time to finish.
Pencils and paper pile up.

pairs.tendency: Everyone plays their own short game at the same time, and the set goes to the one who wins most of them.
pros: Everybody plays at once.
Wins are easy to count.
cons: Players cannot affect each other.
Each game feels like a separate exercise.

pairs.tendency: Each short game is a direct fight, and the winner of two out of three wins the match.
pros: A loser can return to attack.
Players can try a new attack each time.
cons: Grudges can carry from game to game.
A knocked-out player waits for the next game.

pairs.tendency: Each short game is played on a shared board where players block each other without direct attacks, and wins over the series decide the set.
pros: The board is reset each game.
A new position is tried each time.
cons: Players may repeat earlier blocks.
The board needs tidying between games.

pairs.tendency: The whole table plays several short games together, and the set is won if the group beats the game in most of them.
pros: Teams share each win.
A lost game does not end the set.
cons: A group that loses early may lose heart.
A fast player may take over each game.

pairs.tendency: Players work together in each short game but have a private aim, and the set goes to the player with the most private wins.
pros: The group wins together.
Each player keeps a personal count.
cons: Private aims can lead to quarrels.
A player may hold back in a late game.

pairs.tendency: Two teams play several short games, and the team that wins the most games wins the match.
pros: Team-mates learn each other's moves.
A team can change its plan between games.
cons: A lost first game puts one team on edge.
The match can end early when one team leads.

pairs.tendency: A traitor is chosen afresh for each short game, so a player may be a traitor in one game and an ally in the next. Wins are counted across them all.
pros: Roles change each game.
Players learn to spot signs.
cons: A player who was a traitor is watched later.
Trust starts fresh each game.

pairs.tendency: Players send a move by post in each short game, and the set takes weeks to finish.
pros: Each game fits in a few letters.
A set can run through a year.
cons: Letters can be lost.
Waiting gets long.

pairs.tendency: An absent player's moves are left on cards for each short game, and the set goes to whoever beats them most often.
pros: The absent player is the same each game.
Players learn the absent player's habits.
cons: The absent player cannot change their plan.
Cards for each game need to be written in advance.

pairs.tendency: A game master runs each short game as an episode, and the player who wins the most episodes takes the set.
pros: Each episode has its own story.
The master can change the world between games.
cons: The master has to prepare many games.
A tired master runs later games thinly.

pairs.tendency: The game is played in the street in short rounds, and passers-by can join a round and count toward the set.
pros: New players can join between rounds.
A round is quick to learn.
cons: The set is hard to keep track of.
Players come and go.

pairs.tendency: One player faces the rest in each short game and the roles pass round, so everyone gets a turn alone.
pros: Everyone takes the lone role.
The lone role changes each game.
cons: A tired lone player gets one game to recover.
The set takes a game per player.

pairs.tendency: A lone player plays several short games against the pack, and the set is won with more wins than losses.
pros: The player can count wins easily.
A player can stop when the count is settled.
cons: There is no rival to learn from.
A run of losses is felt alone.

pairs.tendency: Each short game is decided by dice or cards, so over many games the luck evens out and the set favours whoever was luckier most often.
pros: A lucky streak can win the set.
An unlucky game costs little.
cons: More games do not remove luck.
Skill barely shows.

pairs.tendency: Dice rule each short game, but the player keeps re-rolls that carry over, so a sharp player spends them across the set.
pros: Re-rolls last across games.
Players choose when to use them.
cons: A re-roll spent early is not there later.
A set can turn on the last few re-rolls.

pairs.tendency: Each short game is mostly about choices with a little luck, so over several games the more careful player usually wins the set.
pros: Repeated games show who plays more carefully.
A single lucky game is not enough to win.
cons: A careful player may still lose to an unlucky streak.
A new player is beaten again and again.

pairs.tendency: Every short game is pure thinking. Most wins takes the set.
pros: Wins track careful play.
A single slip is forgiven by the next game.
cons: A beginner loses game after game.
The set can end early.

pairs.tendency: In each short game the throw is read as a sign, and the set goes to the player whose readings were followed most.
pros: Each game has its own sign.
Players compare readings over the set.
cons: A sign can be read in two ways.
Players argue over whose reading counts.

pairs.tendency: Players try again and again to act at the same moment, and the set is won by the pair who match most often.
pros: Players grow closer after a few tries.
A pair can learn each other's timing.
cons: A pair that is out of step stays out of step.
Match counts can be hard to agree on.

pairs.tendency: Dice write each short game as an episode, and the episodes won are counted up.
pros: Dice write a new episode each time.
The story builds across the set.
cons: An early event may be forgotten.
Tables of events need to be ready for every episode.

pairs.tendency: Each short game is played with everything face up, so the set goes to the player who spots the shortest line in the most games.
pros: Players can see everything in each game.
Mistakes can be traced to moves.
cons: Repeated play leads to repeated openings.
Players know all the options each time.

pairs.tendency: New hidden hands are dealt for each game, and the player who wins the most of them takes the set.
pros: A fresh deal gives a new puzzle.
Players keep their cards private each time.
cons: A low deal costs one game only.
Reshuffling takes time.

pairs.tendency: Secret roles are dealt again in each game, so a player is a spy in one game and an ally in the next. The set is counted in wins.
pros: Roles are new every game.
Players try several roles.
cons: Habits from a previous role can give a player away.
A set can be decided by a lucky role.

pairs.tendency: Each short game is a small mystery to solve, and the set goes to whoever solves the most.
pros: Each game is a new mystery.
Players learn how to reason from clues.
cons: Clues may repeat across the games.
A slow solver falls behind.

pairs.tendency: Players bluff their way through each short game, and the wins are added up.
pros: A bluff that failed in one game may work in the next.
Players learn each other's habits.
cons: A caught bluffer is watched in later games.
Players may remember each other's tells.

pairs.tendency: The secret rule is guessed in the first game, so it is known in every game after. Most wins takes the set.
pros: The first game teaches the rule.
Later games run faster.
cons: Only the first game has the discovery.
A player who found the rule early gets ahead.

pairs.tendency: In each game a different player knows the answer and can only hint, and the player ahead on wins at the end takes the set.
pros: Everyone takes the hinting role.
The role changes each game.
cons: A vague hinter can lose a game.
Players may repeat their hints.

pairs.tendency: Each game starts with a face-down map turned over bit by bit. Whoever wins on the most maps takes the set.
pros: A new map each game.
Players learn how to explore.
cons: An early reveal can decide a game.
Setting out a hidden map takes time.

pairs.tendency: One hand is laid open in every game, and the set is counted in games won.
pros: The open hand is a new puzzle each time.
Players learn from what is shown.
cons: The open hand shrinks the surprise.
Play can feel the same each game.

pairs.tendency: Points are kept secret over the games, so nobody knows who leads until the set ends.
pros: Each game could change the result.
The set stays open to the end.
cons: Nobody can plan to catch up.
The set cannot be stopped early.

pairs.tendency: Turns go round the table in each short game, and the wins are added up once the last game ends.
pros: Everyone gets an equal chance in each game.
Turn order can change between games.
cons: A player waits for others to move.
The first player in the order may have an edge.

pairs.tendency: Every short game is played by everyone at the same time, and the set goes to the player who wins the most.
pros: Games finish fast.
Nobody waits.
cons: A quick player may win all of them.
A slow player is behind at once.

pairs.tendency: Each short game has no turns, so anyone grabs and plays at any moment, and wins are counted game by game.
pros: Games are over in seconds.
Fast reflexes decide each game.
cons: A set may end in a few minutes.
Slow players seldom get a turn.

pairs.tendency: Each game has a clock on every turn, and the set goes to whoever wins most games under the clock.
pros: Games stay short.
Players practise thinking quickly.
cons: A rushed player can lose by a time-out.
Players may start to rely on guessing.

pairs.tendency: One short game is played each day over a week, and the set goes to whoever has won most by the end.
pros: Each day brings a new game.
The set fits into a week.
cons: A missed day is a lost game.
Players can lose track of the count.

pairs.tendency: Every move in each short game waits for a pause, and the winner of the set is whoever won most often.
pros: Each game feels unhurried.
Players think about each move.
cons: The set takes a long time.
A long set may wear on patience.

pairs.tendency: Each game speeds up as it goes, and the next game starts at a slower pace, so the set goes to whoever copes with the rush most often.
pros: Each game ends in a rush.
The next game calms down.
cons: Players tire of racing.
A rush can spoil the last game.

pairs.tendency: In each short game some moves give another go. Games won decide the set.
pros: A lucky chain can win a game in one turn.
Every game can swing quickly.
cons: A chain can end a game before others move.
A set can turn on a single chain.

pairs.tendency: Each short game has two stages, such as picking cards then playing them, and wins are tallied over the set.
pros: Each game has two parts.
Players try new choices in the first stage.
cons: Short games leave little time for stage two.
A rushed first stage costs the game.

pairs.tendency: Each short game runs a small version of a real system, and the set shows which choices kept it going most often.
pros: Players see the system run many times.
Small changes show their effect.
cons: The model cannot carry everything real.
A single run can mislead.

pairs.tendency: Roles pass round after each short game, so every player gets to be the farmer, the council and the shopkeeper.
pros: Each player sees every side.
The roles change each game.
cons: A role is only held for one game.
A player may find one role hard to play.

pairs.tendency: A shared pool is drawn on in each game and refilled before the next, and the player with the most wins takes the set.
pros: The pool starts full each game.
Players see how fast it empties.
cons: A greedy first game leaves ill feeling.
Players refill the pool between games.

pairs.tendency: A choice made in one game shows its effects in a later game, and the set still goes to whoever wins most.
pros: A choice in one game matters in the next.
Players learn to plan across games.
cons: An early choice may be forgotten.
It is hard to tell which game caused a result.

pairs.tendency: Players try a different rule in each short game, and the set shows which rule gave the closest games.
pros: Each game tests a rule.
Players compare results.
cons: A rule tried once can mislead.
Rules that need time to settle are cut short.

pairs.tendency: After every game the players talk about what happened, then play the next. Whoever wins most takes the set.
pros: Each game gets a short talk.
Players change their plans between games.
cons: The talk adds to the evening.
The talk may help the player who was already ahead.

pairs.tendency: Each game changes the board for ever, so the next starts where the last ended, and the set is counted in wins.
pros: The board carries the history of the games.
Old moves shape the new game.
cons: A mistake stays on the board.
Late games are played on a worn board.

pairs.tendency: Each short game makes the same point about the world through its rules, and the set shows players the point many times.
pros: The point comes up game after game.
Players notice it on the second try.
cons: The point may feel repeated.
A player who disagrees is not won over.

pairs.tendency: Each game carries a small real stake, such as a favour, and the set decides who owes whom.
pros: Small stakes add up over games.
Players take each game seriously.
cons: A loss reaches into daily life.
A friend may feel pressed.

pairs.tendency: Each game scores a value such as kindness, and across several games players find themselves chasing the points.
pros: Players see the score steering them.
A value is turned into a number.
cons: The number may replace what it stood for.
Players may argue about how kindness is scored.

pairs.tendency: Each short game rehearses a different part of a future the group is imagining, and the set shows which parts held.
pros: Players try several parts of a future.
Short games cover many scenes.
cons: A short game cannot show the full future.
Players may forget earlier scenes.

pairs.tendency: Each space on the track carries a penalty number, and the aim is to finish with the lowest total. A short roll can keep a piece off a costly square, so everyone watches every throw.
pros: Every throw is watched closely.
A small number feels like a win.
cons: The dice hand out the penalties.
There is little to plan once the dice have landed.

pairs.tendency: Cards carry penalty points. Each player takes one from the row and passes the rest, so the costly cards keep moving round the table until someone keeps one.
pros: Every pick hands a risk to the next player.
Players learn what their neighbours want to avoid.
cons: The last player to pick gets the costly leftovers.
A hand full of penalty cards is hard to shake off.

pairs.tendency: A penalty card goes up for auction and bidders pay chips to push it onto someone else. Whoever bids least takes the points.
pros: Chips turn into a way to dodge penalties.
Bids show how big each penalty looks to the table.
cons: Players with few chips cannot dodge anything.
Rounds drag when everyone bids low.

pairs.tendency: Every extra risk adds points against you, so choosing to press on also raises your total. A player who keeps going can end a round with a pile of penalties.
pros: Stopping early feels sensible.
