cons: One big grab by the lone player hurts everyone.
Team agreements can fall apart.

pairs.tendency: What the lone player does now shows up a few rounds later, and the team sees the build-up before the lone player does. The team can guess what is coming and prepare.
pros: The team can prepare in advance.
The lone player can plan a long way ahead.
cons: Waiting makes cause hard to see.
The team may blame the wrong move.

pairs.tendency: The team agrees a new rule to try, and the lone player has to play under it. Everyone sees what the rule does to one person against many.
pros: The effect on the lone player is easy to see.
A rule can be dropped after a try.
cons: The lone player has less say in the choice.
One try may not show enough.

pairs.tendency: When the game ends, the team and the lone player talk it through. The lone player gets to say what it was like to play on their own.
pros: Both sides are heard.
The lone player's view gets space.
cons: Team voices can drown out the lone player.
It needs time after the game.

pairs.tendency: A card torn up by the team or a sticker placed by the lone player stays for the rest of the game. The lone player's marks and the team's marks end up on the same board.
pros: The board shows the game's history.
The next game starts from here.
cons: A hasty move cannot be undone.
A loss for the lone player carries over.

pairs.tendency: A game of one against the rest makes a point about the many and the one. Paying the lone player more is part of that point, about how a crowd treats a single person.
pros: The rules carry a point.
Players can talk about it afterwards.
cons: The point can be missed during play.
The extra pay for the lone player can read as a hint.

pairs.tendency: Real money or a real promise rides on the result, and the team shares the risk while the lone player carries it alone. The lone player's bigger pay matches the bigger risk.
pros: The stakes are clear to all.
The lone player is paid more for the risk.
cons: The lone player can lose the lot.
Friends may fall out over a result.

pairs.tendency: A number stands for something that matters, such as health. The team shares the count between them and the lone player holds the whole count.
pros: The number is easy to track.
The team can see each member's share.
cons: Chasing the number can push out what it stands for.
The lone player carries the whole count alone.

pairs.tendency: Players practise a way of working that does not exist yet. The lone player tries it alone while the team tries it together, so the two ways can be compared.
pros: Both ways of working show up.
The lone player can try bold ideas.
cons: Team practice takes time.
Results may not carry over to real life.

pairs.tendency: You throw the dice and walk your pawn along the path with nobody else on it. Only the squares and your throws can stop you, and afterwards you can compare turns taken with a friend.
pros: Quick to set up.
The result is a number you can compare.
cons: There is nobody to race or catch.
The dice decide almost everything.

pairs.tendency: A row of cards stands in for the players you would pass to. You pick one, and a set rule removes others as if a neighbour had taken them.
pros: Each pick is still a choice.
The row can be reset and tried again.
cons: The row has no person behind it to read.
The removal rule can be learnt and then predicted.

pairs.tendency: Each prize comes up with a price from the pack, and you decide whether to pay it. No one outbids you, so the only pull is your own purse.
pros: It gives practice at judging a price.
Prices repeat so you can learn them.
cons: There is no haggling.
The price does not react to you.

pairs.tendency: You draw card after card from the pack and stop when you choose. If a danger repeats, you lose the lot, and a friend can try the same shuffle later.
pros: Each draw is a small decision.
The score is easy to share.
cons: Only your nerve is tested.
One draw can end a long run.

pairs.tendency: You place pieces on the map while the pack moves its own pieces by card. You hold areas against a force that follows a card order.
pros: The map fills in over time.
The pack's moves can be learnt.
cons: The pack cannot be bargained with.
The pack's pieces move without a plan.

pairs.tendency: You send workers to jobs, and a card from the pack closes a spot each round. You plan around which spots will be gone.
pros: Closing spots forces choices.
You can plan ahead.
cons: There is nobody to see you take a spot.
A spot can vanish before you can use it.

pairs.tendency: You lay tiles to build a pattern while the pile of tiles runs down. The pile is the only clock.
pros: It is quiet and steady.
You can set your own speed.
cons: No rival's pattern gets in your way.
The order of the pile is luck.

pairs.tendency: You hold cards and decide what to play and what to keep, with nobody reading your hand. The pack hands you the next problem each turn.
pros: The hand is yours alone.
You need hide nothing.
cons: You have no other hand to guess at.
The same hand rarely comes twice.

pairs.tendency: You play a card and the pack answers with one chosen by fixed rules. You win or lose each trick against a card that has no plan behind it.
pros: Tricks go quickly.
The pack's rules are easy to learn.
cons: There is no bluff to read.
The pack plays the same way each time.

pairs.tendency: With nobody to talk to, deals come as offers the pack turns up. You accept or refuse each one.
pros: The offers are laid out in front of you.
No talking skill is needed.
cons: Offers cannot be argued with.
The talking part of the game goes unused.

pairs.tendency: You gather sets from a market that the pack refills. The race is against the supply running out.
pros: Sets build up slowly.
The number of sets is your score.
cons: Nobody competes for your cards.
The refill decides what you can collect.

pairs.tendency: Tiles come off a pile one at a time and you decide where each goes on your own map. The map ends up as a record of your choices.
pros: You end with a map to look at.
There is time to think each tile through.
cons: No one else shapes the map.
A run of awkward tiles has no fix.

pairs.tendency: You call and answer yourself, or answer a recording or a card that calls. The chain only has one voice behind it.
pros: It can be done anywhere.
You set the rhythm.
cons: There is no surprise from a second person.
The chain can feel one-sided.

pairs.tendency: Nobody can talk, and nobody else is there, so the silence is there anyway. You play cards in order and test your own sense of the count.
pros: There is nothing to disturb you.
You learn your own timing.
cons: There is nobody to read or be read by.
The rule about silence changes nothing.

pairs.tendency: You change a rule on your own turn and live with the result on the next. Nobody votes against you.
pros: You can try rule changes freely.
A rule can be tested over many turns.
cons: No one pushes back.
You can change rules until the game is easy.

pairs.tendency: You speak as a character to an empty chair, or to a book that answers. You play the hero and the people the hero meets.
pros: You can try a voice in private.
There is no audience to worry about.
cons: The story has no surprises from other people.
You voice every part yourself.

pairs.tendency: You stack, flick or balance with nobody watching. Your own hands decide the result, and you can try the same task many times.
pros: You can practise in private.
The result is a clear number or a fall.
cons: There is nobody to cheer or jostle.
A tired hand shows in the score.

pairs.tendency: You draw the map as you go, from prompts the pack gives you. The map holds one person's choices.
pros: You end with a map to keep.
You can draw at any speed.
cons: No one else adds to it.
A prompt can leave you with nowhere to draw.

pairs.tendency: You race the pack, or the clock, to the end of the track. The only way to see if you were quick is to play again or ask a friend what they scored.
pros: The finish is easy to see.
A time or a count can be compared.
cons: There is no one to beat on the day.
The pack's pace is fixed.

pairs.tendency: You play for a high score and afterwards set it beside a friend's. Neither of you affects the other's cards.
pros: A score gives a clear target.
You can try again to beat your own.
cons: Scores from different shuffles are not equal.
While you play, no rival sits beside you.

pairs.tendency: You stay in the game as long as you can against the pack. The pack removes your pieces one by one by a fixed order.
pros: A longer run is easy to see.
Each round shows how close you came.
cons: Eventually the pack wins.
A run can end on a single draw.

pairs.tendency: You try to outlast the pack with nobody sharing the load. All the choices that a team would split fall to you.
pros: You make every choice yourself.
A run that lasts feels earned.
cons: You carry every job alone.
One slip has nobody to cover for it.

pairs.tendency: There is one goal and one person aiming at it. The pack throws up the problems and you answer them.
pros: The goal is plain.
You answer to no one.
cons: Nobody shares the effort.
The goal can feel quiet without others.

pairs.tendency: A secret goal is dealt to you and nobody else is there to hide it from. You play toward it, and the pack does not know.
pros: The goal gives you a direction.
You can choose when to look at it.
cons: There is no one to keep it from.
Keeping it secret changes nothing.

pairs.tendency: You play through a story with an ending that the pack's cards decide. You reach the last scene or fall short of it.
pros: A story builds as you play.
The ending is your own.
cons: The story has no other voice.
Some endings come from luck.

pairs.tendency: There is no winning and nobody else, so you play and look at what happened. You can stop when you like and think about it.
pros: There is no pressure.
You look at what you made.
cons: No one to talk it over with.
It can end without any mark.

pairs.tendency: You decide what success means before you start, and you are the only one to check. A friend might choose a different aim for the same game.
pros: The aim is yours.
You can raise it after a run.
cons: Nobody else checks the aim.
An easy aim can make the game short.

pairs.tendency: The game runs until you lose, since you are the only player who can. Your result is how long you lasted.
pros: The result is a number.
It ends with a clear mark.
cons: You always lose in the end.
There is no one else who loses.

pairs.tendency: You keep a game running for as long as you can, adding to it a little each day. Nothing ends it except you stopping.
pros: It can go on for weeks.
You can pick it up and put it down.
cons: It has no finish line.
It can fade without anyone noticing.

pairs.tendency: You play a game that cannot be won, with nobody else to share the surprise. The game keeps refusing what you expect.
pros: It leaves something to think about.
You can stop at any time.
cons: You cannot compare notes with anyone.
It may feel pointless to some.

pairs.tendency: The dice and cards decide almost everything, and you are the only one at the table. You throw, turn a card and see what comes.
pros: It is quick to learn.
Nothing needs careful thought.
cons: Your choices change very little.
Results come from luck alone.

pairs.tendency: You can soften a low throw with re-rolls or a spare card. The pack throws luck at you and you use what you have to answer.
pros: A low throw is not the end.
You decide when to spend a re-roll.
cons: A spent re-roll cannot come back.
Luck still sets the broad result.

pairs.tendency: Your choices decide most things and a little luck keeps each game from repeating. The pack supplies the luck.
pros: Each game turns out differently.
Careful play shows in the result.
cons: One unlucky shuffle can spoil a plan.
Without others there is no one to learn from.

pairs.tendency: With no dice and no one else, the puzzle is just you and the position. You can take as long as you like.
pros: The result is all your doing.
You can go back and try again.
cons: A stuck position has no one to ask.
There is no luck to blame or thank.

pairs.tendency: You throw and read the result as a message for yourself. Nobody else is there to argue over what it means.
pros: You can ask a question in private.
The reading is yours.
cons: There is no one to check your reading against.
You can read it to say what you wanted.

pairs.tendency: You try to sense a moment by yourself, such as the point to clap or to stop. With nobody else, the thing to tune to is a count in your own head.
pros: It trains your own sense of timing.
It needs no equipment.
cons: There is no one to move in step with.
Without a partner it is just counting.

pairs.tendency: Each throw is looked up on a table that says what happens next in your story. You write what comes out, with nobody to share it.
pros: The table gives you ideas.
The story is yours.
cons: Nobody else can add to it.
Odd results can stall the story.

pairs.tendency: Everything is in view, with no opponent to hide anything. You can see the whole position and plan as far as you like.
pros: There is nothing to guess.
You can plan long moves.
cons: There are no surprises.
The same position gives the same plan.

pairs.tendency: The cards you cannot see belong to the pack and not to a person. You guess what is coming from what has been played.
pros: Guessing is a real task.
Counting cards helps.
cons: There is no face to read.
Hidden cards cannot be bluffed.

pairs.tendency: A role is hidden from you, such as who is the traitor in the pack. You work it out from the cards that turn up.
pros: It gives a puzzle to solve.
You can go back over the clues.
cons: There is nobody to question.
The answer is set by the deal.

pairs.tendency: You follow clues to a fact the game has hidden. The pack lays out the clues and you narrow down what it could be.
pros: Clues build up in order.
You can take your time.
cons: There is nobody to suggest a guess.
The answer is the same on a second try.

pairs.tendency: A bluff needs someone to fool and nobody is there. You can play against the pack's fixed rules or against a friend's earlier game.
pros: The rules of the pack can be learnt.
Past games can be played back.
cons: There is nobody to deceive.
The pack never believes or doubts you.

pairs.tendency: The game keeps a rule secret and tells you no when you break it. You find the rule by trying, and the pack never tires of saying no.
pros: You can try things without being watched.
Each no gives a clue.
cons: No person gives you a hint.
Without a person it can feel cold.

pairs.tendency: The game holds the answer and gives you hints through pictures or cards. You guess and the game sends the next hint.
pros: Hints come at your pace.
The guess is yours alone.
cons: The hints cannot adapt to you.
No one reacts to a wrong guess.

pairs.tendency: The map is face down and you turn over areas as you walk into them. Nobody else knows more than you do.
pros: Each reveal is a surprise.
The map is different each game.
cons: No one to share a find with.
An unlucky turn-over can end a run early.

pairs.tendency: A hand lies face up and you play it along with your own. Both hands are yours to decide, and nobody else sees your private cards.
pros: You can see an open hand to learn from.
You play two hands in turn.
cons: There is nobody to hide the private hand from.
The open hand may make the game too easy to read.

pairs.tendency: Your points are kept hidden from you until the end, since nobody else could see them anyway. You tally them up only when it is over.
pros: The final count is a surprise.
You play without checking the total.
cons: The secret is kept from no rival.
A mistake in counting goes unseen.

pairs.tendency: You act, then the pack acts, and the two take turns. Your wait is short because the pack answers at once.
pros: Turns are quick.
The order is simple.
cons: Nobody is waiting on you.
A turn does not feel like a turn with no one watching.

pairs.tendency: You pick and the pack's pick is already set face down, then you reveal both together. Only you choose, so the reveal is more like a check.
pros: Nothing waits.
Reveals are quick.
cons: The pack cannot copy you.
The reveal has no surprise from a person.

pairs.tendency: You act whenever you like with nothing to wait for. The pack moves by its own clock.
pros: There is no waiting.
You set your own pace.
cons: There is no one to be quicker than.
Fast and slow play are hard to tell apart.

pairs.tendency: You race a clock that is the only other thing at the table. When the sand runs out your move is made for you.
pros: The clock gives a clear limit.
Every turn is short.
cons: Nobody shares the pressure.
A rushed move has nobody to blame.

pairs.tendency: You make one move a morning for days or weeks. The game waits for you and nobody else is waiting.
pros: It fits into a day.
It can last a long time.
cons: You can forget it.
The pack gives no reply while you wait.

pairs.tendency: You slow yourself down on purpose, with a breath before each move. Nobody is hurried by the wait.
pros: It leaves time to look at the board.
The pace is calm.
cons: The game can feel empty.
It takes a long time for a small game.

pairs.tendency: The pack speeds up round by round and you try to keep pace. Nobody else is sharing the load as it rises.
pros: The ending comes in a rush.
The rise in pace is easy to feel.
cons: Every job falls to you.
By the last rounds there is no time to think.

pairs.tendency: A lucky throw gives you another go at once, with no one else waiting for theirs. A run of lucky throws can carry you a long way.
pros: A lucky run is possible.
Turns can chain quickly.
cons: A run can end the game early.
Luck outweighs choices on those turns.

pairs.tendency: You choose your cards in the first stage and play them in the second. With no opponent, the second stage tests only your own first choices.
pros: Early choices show up later.
You can try different choices next time.
cons: The first stage cannot be undone.
Two sets of rules take longer to learn.

pairs.tendency: You run a small version of a real system, such as a village's wells, on your own. The system answers each move by its rules.
pros: It shows how a system reacts.
You can try again with a different choice.
cons: No one else acts in it.
A real system has many more actors.

pairs.tendency: You play every group at the table in turn, such as the farmer and the council. Each time you switch you read the problem from a new side.
pros: You see more than one view.
You move between roles at your own pace.
cons: You argue with yourself.
Each group's reply comes from you.

pairs.tendency: You draw from a resource, such as a pond, that the pack also draws from by its rules. The pile goes down by what you take and what the pack takes.
pros: You watch the pond go down.
You see how much you took.
cons: The pack takes without thought.
Nobody shares the choice of how much to take.

pairs.tendency: What you do now shows up a few rounds later, and the blame or the credit is yours alone. You can look back and trace it.
pros: Cause and result can be traced.
You can learn from a past round.
cons: Waiting hides which move did it.
A slow reply can be forgotten.

pairs.tendency: You try a new rule on your own and see what it does. Nobody has to agree and nobody can complain.
pros: It is a safe place to test a rule.
You can swap rules every game.
cons: Only one person's play is seen.
A rule that works alone may not work with others.

pairs.tendency: You look back over your game on your own, perhaps with a notebook. A friend can read it afterwards and compare their run.
pros: Nothing hurries you.
The notes can be kept.
cons: There is no one to ask a question back.
It is easy to skip.

pairs.tendency: Cards you tear and stickers you place stay put, and the next game starts where this one ended. Nobody else's choices are mixed in.
pros: The board keeps a record of your past games.
The next game is tied to this one.
cons: A rushed choice stays on the board.
You cannot hand it to someone fresh.

pairs.tendency: The game's rules make a point and you are the only one to hear it. You play through the point on your own.
pros: The point can be taken in quietly.
You can replay to check it.
cons: Nobody talks it over with you.
You can miss the point.

pairs.tendency: Something real rides on your result, such as a promise to yourself, and you are the only witness to whether you keep it.
pros: The stakes are your own.
You decide what it is worth.
cons: Nobody checks it.
A promise can be bent without anyone knowing.

pairs.tendency: A number stands for something that matters to you, like how much you slept. You chase the number and may drift from what it meant.
pros: You can follow the number day by day.
You see your own habits.
cons: The number can take over from the sleep it measures.
Nobody else can point out the drift.

pairs.tendency: You practise a way of living that does not exist yet, on your own. You see how it feels before telling anyone.
pros: You can try it in private.
You can change your mind in secret.
cons: You do not see how others would act in it.
One person trying it alone says little about a whole village.

pairs.tendency: One hand of cards lies face up and a player may play it along with their own. They throw the dice for their pawn and can spend open cards to change how the move goes.
pros: The open hand adds a choice to every throw.
Everyone can see which cards remain.
cons: A card in the open hand can undo a throw.
The player who uses it moves twice as fast.

pairs.tendency: A player picks from a face-up hand as well as their own. Everyone watches what gets taken from the open hand.
pros: The open hand shows what is on offer.
Picks from it tell the table what is wanted.
cons: The open hand is the first to go.
Players read each other's plans from the open cards.

pairs.tendency: The open hand is the prize on offer and everyone can see what they are bidding for. Players bid on a hand they can read, though they still cannot see each other's private cards.
pros: The prize is clear.
Bids are easier to price.
cons: Everyone bids on the same facts.
Private hands still hide the real value.

pairs.tendency: Everyone can see the open hand, so the cards still to come are partly known. A player keeps drawing and can count what is left from what lies face up.
pros: Counting becomes possible.
A cautious player can read the danger.
cons: Risk is less of a surprise.
Someone can stop just before a danger they can see.

pairs.tendency: The open hand shows which moves are coming for one side of the map. Everyone can see where that side is likely to push.
pros: One side's plans can be read.
The others have time to prepare.
cons: The hand's player has less surprise.
The player of the open hand has two hands to look after.

pairs.tendency: Others can read from the open hand which extra jobs one player can afford, and so which spots that player is likely to take.
pros: The open hand hints at the next spot.
Others can block it early.
cons: The player of the open hand is easy to predict.
Everyone plans around one spot.

pairs.tendency: The open hand lies face up with its colours and shapes in view. A player can build from it along with their own pile, and others can see what it leads to.
pros: Everyone sees which pattern is close.
The open hand gives spare pieces.
cons: Others can take the piece the open hand needs.
The pattern is hard to hide.

pairs.tendency: One hand is shown to all while every other hand is held close. A player decides which of two hands to play from.
pros: The player has twice the cards to choose from.
Others see half of what the player holds.
cons: Choosing between two hands is slow.
Keeping track of both hands takes effort.

pairs.tendency: The player who has the face-up hand plays its cards along with their own. Every other player can count which cards are left in that hand.
pros: The open hand lets everyone count cards.
The player with it plays two hands.
cons: The others read the hand's plan.
Two hands in one head make for a slow turn.

pairs.tendency: The open hand gives everyone a fact to talk about. Players trade offers knowing what one hand holds.
pros: Deals can use the open cards.
Talk starts from a shared fact.
cons: Others know what the open hand will do.
Players can use the open hand as an excuse.

pairs.tendency: A part-built set sits in the open hand for all to see. Others can see which cards would finish it and can hold those back.
pros: Everyone sees which set is near.
Players can plan to block it.
cons: Hiding the set is not possible.
The set's owner can pick up cards for it quickly.

pairs.tendency: The open hand shows which tiles one side will lay next. Others place their own tiles around what they can see coming.
pros: Upcoming tiles can be read.
The map can be planned around.
cons: The next tile is no surprise.
The player of the open hand is easier to block.

pairs.tendency: The open hand shows what one voice is about to say. The reply can be prepared before the call is made.
pros: A reply can be ready in advance.
The chain can speed up.
cons: The call is no surprise.
The response can feel scripted.

pairs.tendency: Without speech, the open hand is the one clear message on the table. Players read it for a cue and play around it.
pros: Everyone has the same cue.
Nobody has to say it.
cons: The open hand can be over-read.
A silent player cannot explain a choice.

pairs.tendency: A rule change shows at once in what the open hand can do. Others can see which changes would help or harm the open hand.
pros: The effect is easy to see.
Players see which rule helps them.
cons: A rule can be changed to hit the open hand.
The player of the open hand is a clear target.

pairs.tendency: A character's gear or notes lie face up for all to read. The player speaks as that character while the group reads the open notes.
pros: The group knows what the character carries.
Scenes can start from open facts.
cons: The character has few secrets.
The group can use the notes against the character.

pairs.tendency: A set of attempts lies face up, such as which stunt comes next. The player flicks or stacks while others read what is planned.
pros: Everyone sees what is coming.
Others can prepare to react.
cons: The attempt loses surprise.
The player feels watched on each try.

pairs.tendency: One hand of map cards is laid face up, and the player who has it draws from it and from their own. The group can see which places will be added.
pros: Places on the map are known in advance.
Others can plan routes.
cons: The map has fewer surprises.
The player of the open hand draws more than the others.

pairs.tendency: One racer's available moves are laid out in the open hand. Others can see how fast that racer can go.
pros: The speed of the open racer is known.
Rivals can aim to block.
cons: The open racer cannot hide a burst of speed.
The player of the open hand has twice the cards to use.

pairs.tendency: The open hand shows points that one side can score. Others can count how far ahead that side may get.
pros: Points on the table are open.
Others can work out the gap.
cons: The score of the open side is no secret.
Players can aim to take those cards first.

pairs.tendency: The open hand shows how many hits one player can still take and which cards will answer an attack. Others can work out how long that player is likely to last, and aim their attacks at the gap.
pros: Everyone can see how close a player is to falling.
The open cards make attacks easier to time.
cons: The player with the open hand cannot hide a low point.
Knock-outs come as less of a surprise.

pairs.tendency: The whole team can read the open hand, so it becomes a shared tool that anyone can point to. The player holding it plays it and their own, and the team talks over which to use.
pros: The team can plan around cards they all see.
The open hand gives talk a fixed starting point.
cons: The player with the open hand carries two hands of choices.
One loud voice can steer every play from it.

pairs.tendency: The team reads the open hand and counts how far its cards go towards the common goal. One player plays it along with their own hand.
pros: The goal can be measured against cards on the table.
Everyone has the same facts to work from.
cons: Private hands still hold what the team cannot see.
The player with two hands can slow the group down.

pairs.tendency: A secret goal sits beside a hand that everyone can see, so the open cards give clues to what a player wants. Others watch which open cards get played and which are left.
pros: Open plays leave traces of a goal.
The secret goal still hides in the private hand.
cons: Watching the open hand can mislead a guesser.
A player can play the open cards to throw people off.

pairs.tendency: A hand of story cards lies face up, so the group knows which turns the story can take. A player draws on it and on their own cards to move the story to an ending.
pros: The group can see where the story may go.
Endings can be planned towards.
cons: Open cards leave fewer twists.
The story can feel mapped out before it starts.

pairs.tendency: There is no winner, and one hand lies open for everyone to look at and talk about. Players try cards from it as they like.
pros: Players can handle cards without a score to chase.
The open hand gives everyone something to point at while talking.
cons: Nothing pushes anyone to use it.
The open hand may sit untouched.

pairs.tendency: Each player names their own goal, and the open hand lays out what one of them could reach. Others can see how far that goal is from the cards on the table.
pros: Players can judge a goal against open cards.
The open hand can start a talk about goals.
cons: One player's aim is easier to read than the rest.
A goal can be changed after looking at the open hand.

pairs.tendency: The game runs until one player loses, and one hand is open, so the loser's risks can be read from the table. Others can see which cards would save that player.
pros: Danger to the holder of the open hand is plain.
Others can choose whether to help or leave it.
cons: The player with the open hand is watched closely.
The open hand can make that player the easy target.

pairs.tendency: The game is meant to keep running, and the open hand lets everyone see which cards could end it. Players can steer clear of those cards, or feed in new ones.
pros: The group can see what would end the game.
Open cards help players keep it going.
cons: Some players may play the ending cards on purpose.
A hand that never changes goes stale.

pairs.tendency: The game cannot be won, and one hand lies open so players can see exactly how it keeps blocking them. They play the open cards and meet the same block each time.
pros: The block is easy to see.
The open cards show how the game pushes back.
cons: There is nothing to find in the hidden cards.
Players may lose interest once the open hand shows the pattern.

pairs.tendency: Everyone builds their own thing at the same time, and one open hand lies in the middle for any of them to look at. Players learn what the open cards do but do not take them.
pros: Everyone can learn from the open hand.
Players stay out of each other's way.
cons: The open hand affects only the player who plays it.
Others learn little from watching.

pairs.tendency: Players attack each other on purpose, and everyone can see the cards one of them might use. The open hand tells the target what could come their way.
pros: A target can see attacks coming.
The player with the open hand can plan around being watched.
cons: The attack is less of a surprise.
The open hand makes its holder the first one hit.

pairs.tendency: Players act on each other only through the board, and the open hand shows which changes one player may make next. Others can see a change coming before it is made.
pros: Moves can be read from the open cards.
Players can plan their own board changes in response.
cons: Blocking the open hand's changes is easy.
The board moves slowly because players wait and watch.

pairs.tendency: Everyone is on the same team and everyone can see the open hand, so there is no one to hide it from. The team treats it as shared stock.
pros: No cards are held back from the team.
The team can plan with the same facts.
cons: One player can end up deciding for everyone.
The private hands remain the only secrets.

pairs.tendency: Players work together but each has a small private aim, and the open hand is the one thing they can all rely on. Each player reads it to guess how the others will behave.
pros: The open hand gives common ground.
Private aims stay private.
cons: Others can see when a player skips the open cards.
A player can use the open hand as cover for a private aim.

pairs.tendency: Two teams play, and the open hand belongs to one of them. Both sides can see it, so the team that owns it plays with its cards in view of the other side.
pros: The other team can plan against open cards.
The owning team can use it as a joint hand.
cons: The owning team has fewer secrets.
The other team has an advantage in reading what is coming.

pairs.tendency: One player secretly works against the rest, and the open hand is the only hand the group can check. If the traitor plays it in a strange way, the group can see.
pros: Odd plays from the open hand stand out.
The group has something to check.
cons: A traitor can avoid the open hand to stay hidden.
Players may blame whoever plays the open hand.

pairs.tendency: Players are far apart and send moves by letter, and the open hand is written out for all to read. Each letter says which cards were played from it.
pros: Everyone has the same list to check.
A letter can be short.
cons: Mistakes in copying the list show up late.
Waiting for replies makes it hard to keep track.

pairs.tendency: The absent player's hand lies face up, and someone present plays it for them. The hand stands in for the person who is not there.
pros: The missing player still has cards in play.
Everyone can read their hand.
cons: The present player plays for someone else.
The absent player cannot answer for what was done.

pairs.tendency: The game master lays out one hand face up and runs it for the world while the others play their own cards. Players can see what the world holds in its open hand.
pros: Players can see what the world is able to do.
The game master has less to remember.
cons: The game master loses surprise.
Players can use open cards to plan around the world.

pairs.tendency: The game is played in a street or a park, and the open hand lies where passers-by can see it too. Anyone walking past can read the cards and join in.
pros: Newcomers can pick up what is happening.
The open cards act as an invitation.
cons: Private hands are easy to peek at.
The open hand can get knocked or mixed up.

pairs.tendency: The open hand lets everyone see some of the luck before it lands. The cards left in play come from random draws, but part of the pile is no longer hidden.
pros: Some of the luck can be read.
Counting is possible.
cons: Most of the result still comes from draws.
Counting does not help much if the shuffle is fresh.

pairs.tendency: A low draw can be fixed by playing a card from the open hand, and everyone can see which fixes remain. Players can plan around when each fix will be used.
pros: The fixes are visible.
A player can recover from a low draw.
cons: Others know what fix is left.
A fix used early cannot be used again.

pairs.tendency: The open hand takes some of the luck out of the cards while choices decide the game. A little luck remains in what is drawn next.
pros: More of the game rests on choices.
A small amount of luck keeps rounds open.
cons: The open cards make some choices easy to predict.
One lucky draw can still change a plan.

pairs.tendency: There is no luck, and one hand lies open, so players see more of the position than in most games. A player reads the open hand and works out what it will do.
pros: Reading the position is clearer.
Careful thought pays off.
cons: Little is left to guess.
A single mistake with the open hand costs a lot.

pairs.tendency: The throws are read as signs, and the open hand lies face up as the group's shared text. Players read a throw against the open cards.
pros: The group reads from the same cards.
Throws get a place to be compared.
cons: Readings may differ over the same cards.
There is no way to settle whose reading is right.

pairs.tendency: Players try to act at the same moment, and the open hand gives everyone the same cue to watch. They tune to the cards they can all see.
pros: A shared cue helps timing.
Players move in step more often.
cons: Players rely on the cue instead of each other.
Without the cue the group falls out of step.

pairs.tendency: A throw is looked up on a table, and the open hand shows which story cards the player may use after seeing the result. The dice write part of the story and the open cards shape the rest.
pros: The table and cards work together.
Players can choose how to answer a throw.
cons: Everyone sees the choices before the dice land.
The story depends on whichever card is open.

pairs.tendency: One player acts at a time, and the open hand is played by one of them, so the others watch the same cards come and go. Each turn leaves fewer open cards.
pros: Everyone sees what has been used.
Turns are easy to follow.
cons: Waiting players have time to count the open cards.
The player with two hands takes longer.

pairs.tendency: Everyone picks at the same time, and the open hand gives away what one player is likely to choose. The others can see the options before they reveal.
pros: A choice can be guessed from the open cards.
Players can pick against it.
cons: The open player has little surprise.
Players can spend the pick on a guess about the open hand.

pairs.tendency: Anyone can act at any moment, and the open hand is there for any player to grab from. The quickest hand takes the open cards.
pros: Everyone can see what is on offer.
Open cards go fast.
cons: Slower players miss the open hand.
A grab at the open hand can start an argument.

pairs.tendency: Each turn runs on a clock, and the open hand saves time because the player can read it before their turn starts. Others see which open card is picked when time runs short.
pros: Reading ahead saves seconds.
The open hand gives a quick choice.
cons: The player with two hands has more to decide in the same time.
Others can guess a rushed play.

pairs.tendency: The game runs over days, and the open hand stays on show between moves. Players can think about it each morning.
pros: There is time to study the open cards.
The open hand is the same all week.
cons: The open hand loses surprise.
Players can forget what the open cards were.

pairs.tendency: The game is slow on purpose, and a long pause before each move gives everyone time to read the open hand. The pause is spent looking at the cards on the table.
pros: There is time to look at the open cards.
The pace suits careful reading.
cons: Waiting players can run out of things to do.
The open hand holds few secrets for such a long wait.

pairs.tendency: The pace rises, and the open hand lets players decide faster because they have seen the cards. Later rounds come with less time to read it.
pros: Quick decisions are easier with open cards.
Players keep up as the pace rises.
cons: The last rounds come too fast to read it.
Mistakes with the open hand pile up.

pairs.tendency: A lucky throw gives a player another go, and the open hand lets the others see what that player will do with it. The extra move is easy to guess.
pros: An extra turn can be planned for.
Others can see the run coming.
cons: A long run can take every open card.
The rest of the table waits out the run.

pairs.tendency: The first stage is for choosing cards and the second for playing them, and the open hand shows what one player picked. The others can plan the second stage against what they saw.
pros: A first-stage pick shows up in the second.
Players can plan against the open cards.
cons: A slip in the first stage cannot be hidden.
Each stage has its own rules to learn.

pairs.tendency: The board stands for a real system, and the open hand shows what one group in it can do. Everyone sees how that group could act on the system.
pros: The effect of one group is easy to see.
The model can be studied from the open cards.
cons: The open group has little surprise.
The model gets harder to read with two hands in play.

pairs.tendency: Each player plays a real group, and one of them plays with its hand face up. The others see how that group sees the problem.
pros: One group's options are in view.
Other roles can answer it.
cons: The group with the open hand loses its secrets.
Players can use the open hand to speak for the group.

pairs.tendency: Everyone draws from one pile, and the open hand shows how much one player plans to take. The others see the draw before it happens.
pros: A big grab can be seen coming.
Others can act to protect the pile.
cons: The open player is easy to blame.
Others can race to take their share first.

pairs.tendency: What a player does now shows up some rounds later, and the open hand lets the others see what is already on its way. They can guess what will land.
pros: Coming effects can be read.
Players can prepare.
cons: The gap makes it hard to tell what caused what.
Others may take the blame for the wrong move.

pairs.tendency: Players agree a new rule and try it, with one hand open to show how it would change play. Everyone can see the effect on a hand they can all read.
pros: Everyone watches the rule change one readable hand.
The open hand gives a fixed test.
cons: One hand only shows part of what changes.
A rule may look different with hidden cards.

pairs.tendency: After the game, players look back at the open hand and ask what its cards did. The hand lies there as a record they can all point at.
pros: The group has one hand to talk about.
The open cards help memory.
cons: Private hands cannot be discussed in the same way.
Players may spend too long on the open hand.

pairs.tendency: Cards torn up or stickers placed stay for the rest of the game, and the open hand shows which cards are at risk. Everyone can see what might be lost.
pros: Risks to the open cards are plain.
The loss of a card is easy to see.
cons: A torn card cannot be put back.
The player with the open hand may play it safe.

pairs.tendency: The rules make a point, and the open hand lets everyone watch a player use them. Players read the point from what the open cards do.
pros: The point is shown by open play.
The group can talk about it afterwards.
cons: The point can be missed in play.
The open hand may suggest a point that was not meant.

pairs.tendency: Real money or a promise rides on the result, and the open hand tells everyone what the holder could do about it. Others can see how much is at risk.
pros: Stakes are in view.
Others can react to the open hand.
cons: The player with the open hand is under watch.
Friends can argue over how the open cards were used.

pairs.tendency: A number stands for something that matters, and one player's possible points sit in the open hand. Players watch how the number is chased.
pros: The chase for points is visible.
Others see what the number is doing.
cons: The count can crowd out the value behind it.
With the points laid open, counting them is easy and the reason for them slips.

pairs.tendency: Players practise a way of working that does not yet exist, and the open hand holds the tools they have. Everyone sees what the new way allows.
pros: The new way is laid out in view.
Players can try it with the same facts.
cons: The open hand shows only part of the future.
A practice with open cards leaves out surprises.

pairs.tendency: A piece can race along the path while its owner holds few points, because the positions are on view and the scores are hidden.
pros: The path no longer shows who is ahead.
Throws become clues about rival totals.
cons: Nobody can tell how near the end is.
Each player keeps a private tally.

pairs.tendency: Each pick from the shared row adds to a total that stays hidden, so what a player takes hints at a score nobody can check.
pros: Every pick gives a small clue away.
Players try to read totals from the cards taken.
cons: Hard to know whom to block.
A pick that looks small may carry many points.

pairs.tendency: Bids are paid from money that others cannot count, so a high offer may show a full purse or a bluff.
pros: An offer says little about what is left.
Bidders watch faces along with numbers.
cons: A bidder can run dry without warning.
A big win may hide a thin purse.

pairs.tendency: The points at risk are hidden, so the others watch you carry on without knowing what you stand to lose.
pros: A bold streak and a careful one look alike.
Others guess when you will stop.
cons: Nobody can size up a bust.
Guessing can slow down a quick turn.

pairs.tendency: The map shows who holds each area, but what the areas pay is hidden, so the board shows who holds what and nothing about the score.
pros: The map and the score tell different things.
Players guess whose areas pay the most.
cons: Picking which rival to attack is a guess.
Holding the most spots may not mean leading.

pairs.tendency: Workers go onto jobs in full view, while the rewards go into private piles. Others can see where you work and can only guess what you gained.
pros: Job choices hint at plans without proving them.
Players read each other's spots for clues.
cons: Blocking a rival is a guess.
A taken spot may have paid little.

pairs.tendency: Patterns grow in the open, but the points each one earns are written down and covered. A tidy pattern may be worth a lot or a little.
pros: Everyone can see every pattern.
The value of a pattern stays secret.
cons: Players count rival patterns in their heads.
A finished pattern gives no sign of its score.

pairs.tendency: Cards in hand are hidden and so are the points already won, so a rival has two things to guess at.
pros: Two sets of hidden facts.
Careful play stays private.
cons: Little is left to read at the table.
A wrong guess about a rival can last to the end.

pairs.tendency: Each trick won adds to a hidden total, so watching who takes tricks gives only a rough count of who leads.
pros: Players can count tricks but not points.
Close contests stay close to the end.
cons: Trick wins and scores can disagree.
A lead can change hands unseen.

pairs.tendency: Deals are struck across the table by people who cannot see what the other side holds. A trade may help the leader without anyone knowing.
pros: Each deal rests on a guess about the other side.
Talk can let hints about scores slip out.
cons: A player may help the leader by mistake.
Trust is hard to settle.

pairs.tendency: Sets are gathered in the open while their points are counted in secret. Seeing a finished set tells nobody what it paid.
pros: A set shows what a player went for.
Rivals can guess what you are after.
cons: Counting a rival's total takes guesswork.
A big set may be worth less than it looks.

pairs.tendency: The shared map grows tile by tile for all to see, while each score stays hidden. A road laid by one player may pay another.
pros: The map shows what was built.
Who gained from it stays private.
cons: A tile laid for a rival is easy to miss.
The map cannot say who leads.

pairs.tendency: A line is called and answered round the table, and the score for each answer is kept private. Players hear every answer without learning what any of them scored.
pros: The chain is heard by everyone.
Answers invite guesses about points.
cons: Hard to know if a clever answer paid off.
A quiet player can score without notice.

pairs.tendency: Nobody speaks and nobody shows a score, so the only signs are the cards put down and the moment they come down.
pros: Silence leaves little to read.
Players watch hands and faces closely.
cons: No sign of who is ahead.
The table can go very quiet.

pairs.tendency: With scores hidden, a rule changed on your turn might help someone without anyone knowing who.
pros: A rule change can hide its winner.
Each player can aim a rule at their own total.
cons: Rules that favour the leader are hard to spot.
Arguments start without facts to settle them.

pairs.tendency: Each person speaks as a character, and the points that character collects are private. Everyone follows the story while each tally stays with its player.
pros: The story runs on with no numbers in the way.
A character's choices are made without a scoreboard.
cons: Nobody can say how a character is doing.
A player may act on a wrong guess about the others.

pairs.tendency: A flick, a stack or a throw happens in plain sight, but the points it earns are out of sight. Onlookers can watch a steady hand without knowing whether it leads.
pros: Skill is on view for everyone.
A shaky hand may hide a big lead.
cons: A fine throw may add only a few points.
Onlookers cannot rank the throwers.

pairs.tendency: The map is drawn on paper in front of everyone, while the points gained from it are held in private.
pros: The drawing is shared by all.
Every line invites questions.
cons: A rival's score cannot be read from the map.
A drawing made for one player's gain can pass as a joint effort.

pairs.tendency: Runners head for the end while a hidden pile of points sits beside each of them, so arriving first may or may not settle the game.
pros: A runner can see who is ahead on the path.
The hidden pile adds a second contest.
cons: Two aims can blur what the game is for.
A late reveal can overturn the race.

pairs.tendency: Scores stay hidden to the end, and the reveal names the winner. Everyone plays on without knowing where they stand.
pros: The final reveal settles the game.
Everyone has a reason to keep going.
cons: Nobody knows when to change plans.
The loser finds out late.

pairs.tendency: Players are knocked out one at a time, and the points of those still in stay hidden. So the table knows who has gone and only guesses who has the most.
pros: Knock-outs are easy to see.
Survivors guess at each other's totals.
cons: A player can be knocked out while ahead on points.
An early exit leaves a long wait.

pairs.tendency: The whole group survives or falls together, yet each person keeps private points. Nobody knows a team-mate's score.
pros: A shared fate sits beside a private tally.
Players can still work as one.
cons: Hidden points can pull one person away from the group.
Doubts about a team-mate can creep in.

pairs.tendency: Everyone pushes for one goal while keeping a private score on the side. Only the group result is on view.
pros: One open goal for the group.
A side contest runs in secret.
cons: Private scores can pull against the shared goal.
The group may waste time guessing.

pairs.tendency: Each player has a secret aim and a secret score, so the table holds two kinds of hidden facts at once.
pros: A player can bluff about both aim and total.
Moves are hard to read.
cons: Nobody knows what the others are working towards.
Talk at the table has little to stand on.

pairs.tendency: The story runs to its end while points are tallied in secret, so the finish is a plot ending with a score nobody has seen.
pros: The story gives the game a clear end.
Scores add a private side to it.
cons: The tally may seem out of place at the close.
A player may chase points at the story's expense.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, yet each player keeps a hidden tally. The numbers may come out in the talk afterwards, or never.
pros: The tally gives a reason to look back.
Players choose whether to share it.
cons: A secret number can feel out of place without a winner.
Some players may chase it anyway.

pairs.tendency: Each player decides what a result means to them and keeps a private count. Two people can leave the table content with very different numbers.
pros: Each count follows its owner's aim.
Nobody is judged by another's measure.
cons: Counts cannot be compared.
A player may forget what they set out to do.

pairs.tendency: Nobody wins, the game runs until one player loses, and the points that mark the loser stay hidden.
pros: Players guess who is nearest to losing.
Hidden totals keep everyone wary.
cons: The loser may be a surprise at the end.
A player who knows they are last has little left to play for.

pairs.tendency: The game goes on with no end in view while each player holds a private count. Nobody can say who leads at any moment.
pros: A running count never has to be revealed.
The game is not cut off by a reveal.
cons: Counts can drift far apart unseen.
A player may stop caring about a number nobody reads.

pairs.tendency: Scores are kept in secret in a game that nobody can win, so the numbers lead nowhere.
pros: The hidden count is a puzzle with no answer.
Players may look for ways round it.
cons: Players may ask why they are counting at all.
A player may try harder than the game allows.

pairs.tendency: Everyone builds their own thing at the same time with scores hidden, so no one knows whose build earns most.
pros: Each player works undisturbed.
Peeking is the only way to compare.
cons: Nobody can tell who is ahead.
The game can feel like many separate games.

pairs.tendency: Players attack and steal from each other, but hidden scores keep the real leader out of view. A blow may land on the wrong person.
pros: Attacks are aimed by guess.
Rivals bluff about how far ahead they are.
cons: A leader can go unhit.
A trailing player can take hits meant for the leader.

pairs.tendency: Players change the board and feel each other's moves through it, while the score each move earns stays private.
pros: The board still shows what was done.
Hard to tell which move helped whom.
cons: A rival's wall may be a gift or a blow.
Nobody knows who to build against.

pairs.tendency: The group wins or loses together, so a hidden score has no obvious use. It can only be a private tally on the side.
pros: Players share the same aim.
A private count adds a small side contest.
cons: Hidden numbers can spread doubt in a group that needs trust.
Players may wonder why scores are kept.

pairs.tendency: Players work together, but each has a small private reason to come out ahead. Hidden scores let that reason stay quiet.
pros: Teamwork carries on in the open.
Private gains can grow unseen.
cons: Helping the group may feed a rival's score.
A quiet leader goes unnoticed.

pairs.tendency: Two teams play each other, and each member's points are private, even to team-mates.
pros: A team can pool its guesses.
Rivals have nothing to read.
cons: A team may not know how it is doing.
A team-mate's hidden score can mislead the side.

pairs.tendency: One person works against the rest, and with scores hidden a low total could be honest or put on.
pros: The traitor can fake a low total.
The traitor can hide among the scores.
cons: The rest cannot rely on numbers to find them.
Accusations rest on little.

pairs.tendency: Moves arrive by post or message over weeks, and the scores stay secret, so each reply may or may not hide a lead.
pros: Waiting leaves time to guess at scores.
A reply carries only what the sender chooses.
cons: A score can sit unchecked for weeks.
A letter that goes missing can leave the tally in doubt.

pairs.tendency: One player is not at the table, and their score is hidden too. A ghost or a far-off player might be ahead for all anyone knows.
pros: The absent player stays a mystery.
Their gains cannot be checked.
cons: Nobody can tell if the missing player leads.
A score nobody can check gets doubted.

pairs.tendency: One person runs the world and so can keep each player's points in secret. Only the game master sees the whole tally.
pros: The game master holds all the scores.
Players are spared the bookkeeping.
cons: Everyone relies on one person to keep the count straight.
The keeper holds facts nobody can check.

pairs.tendency: Passers-by join a street game where scores are secret, so a new player cannot tell how far ahead the regulars are.
pros: Anyone can step in.
A new player faces no visible gap.
cons: Scores are hard to carry when people come and go.
The regulars may keep a lead without anyone knowing.

pairs.tendency: Dice and draws decide most things and the score is secret, so a lucky run goes unseen until the reveal.
pros: Luck stays private.
A trailing player can still hope.
cons: Nobody can judge whether a result was earned.
The reveal can seem arbitrary.

pairs.tendency: A player softens a low roll with a re-roll or a card, and the saved points go into a hidden total. Others never see what was saved.
pros: Rescues stay private.
Rivals cannot tell which throws were saved.
cons: A rival's luck is hard to judge.
Using a rescue gives away a clue.

pairs.tendency: Choices matter most and a little luck stirs things, with scores out of sight. Nobody can tell skill from luck in a rival's total.
pros: Skilled play is not easy to read.
Luck adds doubt to every guess.
cons: A skilful player cannot be sure they lead.
A lucky one may think they do.

pairs.tendency: No luck is involved, so a hidden score reflects only choices. Players can reason from each other's moves to work out totals.
pros: Totals can be worked out by reasoning.
Hidden numbers add a puzzle to the plans.
cons: Players who count carefully gain on those who do not.
Counting takes effort.

pairs.tendency: Dice are read as messages, and the points that come with them are private. The others see your throw and never learn its points.
pros: The throw gives food for thought.
Readings can stay between a player and the dice.
cons: Signs and scores can pull apart.
A reading may be shaped by a hidden number.

pairs.tendency: Players try to act at the same moment, sensing each other, while scores are private. The group feels in step but cannot see whose gains are whose.
pros: The group stays in touch by feel.
Scores do not interrupt the flow.
cons: Private points can break the feeling of acting together.
Players may start watching instead of sensing.

pairs.tendency: A roll sends you to a table that says what happens next, and each event also adds to a hidden count. The tally stays with each player.
pros: The story moves along with each roll.
Events give small, quiet rewards.
cons: A player may chase rewards over the story.
Players cannot tell whose story pays.

pairs.tendency: One player acts at a time, and the others cannot count the score from watching. Each turn shows a move but hides what it earned.
pros: Watching a turn gives a clue.
Everyone has time to think.
cons: Players spend their wait guessing.
Long waits with many players.

pairs.tendency: Everyone chooses at the same moment, then all reveal, while scores stay hidden. The gains from them stay out of sight.
pros: Reveals show choices but not totals.
No one waits for a turn.
cons: Others' earnings are hard to follow.
Fast rounds leave little time to guess.

pairs.tendency: Anyone can act at any moment and quick hands win, while points pile up in secret. A burst of play may leave no one sure who gained.
pros: Action keeps flowing.
Hidden points cannot be tracked in the rush.
cons: Fast players can score without notice.
Slow players cannot catch up on what they missed.

pairs.tendency: A clock runs on each turn, which leaves little time to guess at rival totals.
pros: The clock keeps turns short.
Players act on what they have.
cons: Guessing and moving compete for the same seconds.
A rushed move may give away a score.

pairs.tendency: The game runs over days with one move each morning, and scores stay hidden, so days pass between small clues.
pros: Each move can be thought over at leisure.
Clues arrive slowly.
cons: A rival's total stays a guess for days.
Interest may fade before the reveal.

pairs.tendency: The game slows everyone down with a pause before each move, while points stay hidden. The wait gives time to wonder who leads.
pros: Slowness gives time to think.
Players can watch each other closely.
cons: Quiet lets guesses grow.
Patience wears thin.

pairs.tendency: As the game speeds up, hidden scores make it harder to follow. Near the end, players act with little idea of the standings.
pros: Surprise at the finish is likely.
The rush adds pressure to every guess.
cons: Last moves are made blind.
Falling behind can go unnoticed.

pairs.tendency: A lucky throw gives another go at once, and the points it earns go into a hidden total. A run of extra turns may pile up unseen.
pros: A lucky run can stay secret.
Others see moves but not gains.
cons: A runaway lead may go unnoticed.
The rest of the table waits through a long run.

pairs.tendency: The game has stages with different rules, and hidden points carry from the first stage into the second.
pros: Points made early can still count later.
Each stage can change how a total is built.
cons: As the rules shift, the leader stays unknown.
Hidden totals can make a change of stage feel sudden.

pairs.tendency: The board works like a real system, and each player's points are private, so the table watches the system and has to guess who profits.
pros: The shared system is open to all.
Each player's gains stay private.
cons: A player can profit from a damaged system unseen.
Talk about who benefits rests on guesses.

pairs.tendency: Each player speaks for a group with needs, and the points that group earns are private. Others hear the argument but not the gain.
pros: Each group's case is heard.
Needs can be argued in the open.
cons: Gains cannot be compared between groups.
A group may seem to lose while it quietly gains.

pairs.tendency: Everyone draws from one limited store and each player's take is secret. Everyone watches the store go down without seeing who took most.
pros: The shrinking store is easy to see.
Who takes the most is hidden.
cons: Blame is hard to place.
A player may take more than their share unseen.

pairs.tendency: What you do now shows its effect rounds later, and the points follow the same delay, so a move and its reward are far apart and hidden.
pros: The reward for a move arrives late.
The wait builds a guess about every rival.
cons: Cause and score are hard to link.
A player may forget why a number changed.

pairs.tendency: The table tries a new rule and plays on to see what it changes, with scores hidden. Nobody can say who gained from the rule.
pros: A rule can be tested without a visible winner.
Reactions to the rule are still seen.
cons: The result of the test is hard to read.
A rule that helps one player could stay unnoticed.

pairs.tendency: After play, the hidden scores come out and the talk can start from a number that surprises.
pros: The reveal gives the talk something to chew on.
Players compare their guesses with what happened.
cons: A reveal can leave some players feeling exposed.
The talk may turn to scores instead of lessons.

pairs.tendency: Cards are torn and stickers go on the board while scores stay secret, so a change that cannot be undone may help someone nobody can name.
pros: Each change leaves a mark on the game.
The marks show what was done.
cons: The cost of a change stays hidden.
Nobody can take back a move that helped a rival.

pairs.tendency: The rules make a point about the world, and hidden scores add a second point that only the holders of those scores know.
pros: The open rules speak to everyone.
Hidden totals can stand for a private view.
cons: The message of the game can split in two.
Players may argue about a point the scores cannot back.

pairs.tendency: Real money or a promise is on the line and the scores are secret, so players risk something without knowing where they stand.
pros: The stakes make every guess count.
The reveal carries weight.
cons: A secret total can strain a friendship.
Players may feel cheated at the reveal.

pairs.tendency: Points stand in for something like kindness, and keeping them secret means nobody can see how kind another has been.
pros: The number is kept apart from the value.
Nobody can show off.
cons: Chasing hidden points is hard to check.
A player may drift from the value unseen.

pairs.tendency: The table acts out a new way of living while each person's points are private. Each person's gain stays private.
pros: The rehearsal is out in the open.
Private gains show what players do when unseen.
cons: Secret scores sit oddly with a shared way of life.
Players may argue about what the hidden numbers prove.

pairs.tendency: A throw of a certain number lets you roll again at once, so one player can cross a long stretch of the path while the rest wait.
pros: Lucky throws bring quick progress.
Big swings in a single turn.
cons: Others sit through long runs.
A lead can vanish or grow in one go.

pairs.tendency: Making a certain pick earns another pick straight away, so one player takes two cards from the row before anyone else sees it change.
pros: The row changes twice in one turn.
A double pick can finish a plan.
cons: Others lose a pick without warning.
A double turn leaves less on the row.

pairs.tendency: A winning bid carries an extra turn, so the same player can open the next sale straight away.
pros: Winning an auction leads to starting one.
A winner keeps the floor.
cons: The same bidder can win two sales running.
Others have fewer chances to buy.

pairs.tendency: Each safe round can earn an extra turn, so a player can keep going twice as long as usual. The more turns, the more there is to lose.
pros: The reward for risk grows.
A long run can pile up many points.
cons: One slip wipes out the whole run.
Others wait while a risk-taker goes on.

pairs.tendency: Taking a key area earns another go, so one conquest can be followed by a second before the rivals reply.
pros: One conquest can lead to another.
The map can change fast in a turn.
cons: Others have little time to respond.
A hold on an area may fall to a second move.

pairs.tendency: Some jobs give an extra turn, so a player can place a worker, take the reward and place another before the others move.
pros: A job can be used to reach a second job.
Order of spots starts to matter.
cons: Rivals lose the spots they wanted.
A run of placements can empty the board.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn lets a pattern builder lay two pieces in a row, enough to close a gap a rival was blocking.
pros: A gap can close before a rival answers.
Plans can finish early.
cons: A rival's block may fail.
The pause between moves disappears.

pairs.tendency: Playing certain cards gives another go, so a card played now lets you play again before the table can react.
pros: Chains of cards in one turn.
A hand can be emptied faster.
cons: Saved cards get used up sooner.
Others see a big play and cannot answer it.

pairs.tendency: Winning a trick already means leading the next one. With an extra turn on top, one player can lead several tricks in a row.
pros: Control of the lead lasts longer.
A long run of tricks can be planned.
cons: Others sit through a run of lost tricks.
The usual order of tricks loses its shape.

pairs.tendency: A trade closed on one turn can be followed by a second at once, so a player can strike two deals before the others talk.
pros: Deals can be linked.
One promise can set up another.
cons: Others have little time to bargain.
Partners may feel hurried.

pairs.tendency: With an extra turn, a player draws twice, which can finish a set that was one card away.
pros: A near set can close at once.
Sets fill faster.
cons: Rivals who watched for gaps lose time.
The pace of collecting speeds up.

pairs.tendency: Two tiles in a row let a player link roads or fields that could not be joined in one move.
pros: Two tiles can finish a link.
The map grows faster.
cons: A rival's spot may vanish under them.
Others see the map change twice in one go.

pairs.tendency: A reply that earns an extra turn lets the same person speak twice, so the exchange can lean towards one voice.
pros: The chain can take a sudden turn.
One player can lead a pattern.
cons: The back-and-forth between two voices breaks.
Quieter players are left out.

pairs.tendency: A player who acts twice without a word leaves the others with only the cards to read for a double move.
pros: A double move leaves clues.
Silence hides the reason for it.
cons: The shared timing of play slips.
Players may misread who has the extra turn.

pairs.tendency: One rule can give an extra turn on any throw or take it away, so changing the rule changes who gets to move.
pros: Rules can favour the player who writes them.
Extra turns become a prize.
cons: Rule changes may be aimed at one person.
The table argues over who can move.

pairs.tendency: A character with a moment of luck gets another action at once, so the story follows them for a second beat.
pros: The story can stay on one scene.
A player gets a moment in the spotlight.
cons: Others wait to speak.
Quiet characters fade.

pairs.tendency: A neat flick or placement earns another go, so a steady hand can run on until it slips.
pros: Skill earns more time.
A steady run can build a lead.
cons: A nervous player loses the turn at once.
Others wait while a steady hand plays on.

pairs.tendency: A second turn lets a player draw another feature, shaping a part of the map before anyone else adds to it.
pros: One person can shape a region.
A drawing fills in quickly.
cons: Others find their space taken.
The map shows one hand more than the rest.

pairs.tendency: Landing on certain spaces gives another go, so a runner can jump far ahead while the rest watch.
pros: Runs of luck bring the end near.
A trailing player can catch up in one turn.
cons: A leader can lose their place at once.
The race can finish in a burst.

pairs.tendency: Every extra turn is another chance to score, so a player who earns one can add points twice in the same round.
pros: Points add up faster.
An extra turn is worth chasing.
cons: Players who miss out fall behind.
Scores can grow lopsided.

pairs.tendency: A hit that knocks someone out earns another go, so a player can remove a second rival before any reply.
pros: One strike can follow another.
The field thins quickly.
cons: A player who is hit first has no reply.
The game can end early for most players.

pairs.tendency: The team earns the extra turn, so the group can plan two moves in a row against the game.
pros: The team gets a second move.
Planning together stretches over both.
cons: A mistaken first move carries into the second.
Talking over a second move can hold up the game.

pairs.tendency: When the group earns an extra turn, one member can move twice towards the goal. Which member moves is for the group to settle.
pros: Progress can come in jumps.
The group decides who uses it.
cons: A lot rests on one player's second move.
Arguments can start over who takes it.

pairs.tendency: Two moves in a row let a player step towards a secret aim twice, which can give it away.
pros: Double moves can finish a secret aim quickly.
A player reaches it sooner.
cons: Two moves in a row show a pattern.
Rivals can read the aim from them.

pairs.tendency: With an extra turn, a player tells two parts of the story at once, so the tale can jump forward.
pros: The story moves faster.
One voice can carry a scene.
cons: Other players may have no say in a turn.
A quick plot can skip what others wanted.

pairs.tendency: Extra turns are handed out with nothing to win, so they only mean more time to do and see.
pros: A player gets longer to try things.
The game may look different afterwards.
cons: Nothing marks a lucky run as a win.
Others may wonder why it matters.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn is worth whatever its player makes of it. One may use it to save a piece, another to try something new.
pros: The same turn serves different aims.
Players can swap what they want.
cons: Nobody agrees on its worth.
A run of turns may please one player and leave another cold.

pairs.tendency: One more move can save a player from being the loser. It can also give them one more chance to slip.
pros: A second move can rescue a position.
A second move can also cost something.
cons: Others wait with their own risk.
The game can end on a run of extra turns.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn gives more play, which suits a game meant to continue.
pros: More play for the player who earns it.
The game runs longer in one sitting.
cons: Turns can pile up for one player.
Others can drift away while they wait.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn comes in a game nobody can win, so the only reward is more of the game.
pros: A player gets more to try.
The reward has no end in sight.
cons: Extra moves lead nowhere.
A player may use them to test the game.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn changes only the player's own build, so rivals see nothing and lose nothing.
pros: Players work at their own pace.
A fast run does not hurt others.
cons: Waiting on others is rare.
Players can drift apart in progress.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn lets an attacker hit twice, with no turn for the target in between.
pros: A strike can follow a strike.
A fight can end in one go.
cons: A target can lose twice at once.
A player under attack can fall quickly.

pairs.tendency: Changing the board twice in a row means a wall or a block can be finished before anyone can step round it.
pros: A plan can be finished in one go.
Changes to the board stack up.
cons: A rival can find their route shut.
The board can look very different after one turn.

pairs.tendency: Extra turns go to the team, so the group can act twice before the game answers.
pros: A tough spot can get a second try.
The group chooses who uses it.
cons: The game answers after a longer gap.
The extra move can be spent on the wrong thing.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn helps the team, but the player who takes it also gets a small private gain.
pros: The group gets a second move.
The taker gets a private edge.
cons: Players may want the turn for themselves.
Talk about who takes it gets sharp.

pairs.tendency: One team member moves twice, so a team can answer another side's move in the same go.
pros: A team can hand a turn to the right person.
One side can build a lead.
cons: The other team sits idle.
A team-mate may miss out.

pairs.tendency: A traitor with an extra turn can make two moves against the group, and the group may not see the second.
pros: Two moves can bring a plan on.
A traitor may hide behind a lucky turn.
cons: The group may start to track who gets extra turns.
Suspicion falls on lucky players.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn sends two moves in one letter, so the reader finds the board changed twice.
pros: One letter can carry a lot of play.
Waiting is rewarded with more to read.
cons: The reply has more to answer.
A single misread can spoil both moves.

pairs.tendency: An absent player cannot take an extra turn, so the rules need to say who moves for a ghost or a far-off player.
pros: The absent player can still get a turn.
Someone else carries it out.
cons: Who uses it is open to argument.
It may look as if the ghost is lucky.

pairs.tendency: The game master gives an extra turn as a reward or a story beat, so a player acts twice because of what happened.
pros: Extra turns can be handed out as story.
The game master controls the pace.
cons: Players may feel favoured or passed over.
Others may argue about who got one.

pairs.tendency: In a street game, an extra turn lets a player go again while passers-by watch. A lucky run may draw a crowd.
pros: Onlookers see it.
A player gets more of the game.
cons: A passer-by may wait a long time to join.
Others in the group stand about.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn on a lucky throw makes luck count twice, so a hot streak is hard to stop.
pros: Luck stacks on luck.
Games can swing quickly.
cons: Skill has even less room.
A trailing player can only hope.

pairs.tendency: Re-rolls and cards can be used to earn an extra turn on purpose, so a player can plan towards one.
pros: A plan to earn a turn is possible.
Luck becomes easier to plan for.
cons: Spending a re-roll on a turn leaves less for danger.
A planned extra turn can still be wasted.

pairs.tendency: A little luck hands out extra turns, and skilled players make more of them.
pros: Luck gives skilled players a chance to show it.
Extra turns can change a close game.
cons: Luck lands on whoever happens to be ready.
A lucky novice can catch a skilled player.

pairs.tendency: In a game with no luck, an extra turn has to be earned by a clever move.
pros: Cleverness earns a second move.
Planning towards it pays off.
cons: A skilled player can run far ahead.
The gap between players can widen quickly.

pairs.tendency: A throw that earns another go is read as a sign too, so an extra turn can feel like the dice speaking twice.
pros: The dice get another say.
Readings can build on each other.
cons: Two readings in a row can pull apart.
Players may argue over what a repeat means.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn breaks the rhythm of sensing when others will act, since one player moves again straight away.
pros: A repeat move can show how closely a player senses the group.
The timing of the group shifts.
cons: A player may mistake a repeat for a signal.
The group needs time to find its rhythm again.

pairs.tendency: Another roll on the table gives the story a second step.
pros: The tale runs on.
Two events can happen close together.
cons: Others get no part of that stretch.
A string of rolls can turn into a muddle.

pairs.tendency: Every move is open, so an extra turn is easy to see coming. Players know when a rival is one throw from a second go.
pros: Everyone can see the chance.
Rivals can plan against it.
cons: Nothing is hidden about a double move.
Players can grow wary of every throw.

pairs.tendency: Two cards played from a hidden hand in one go show the others more of it.
pros: A second play can show the hand.
Bluffing gets a second try.
cons: A run of plays gives a lot away.
Others may be stuck waiting.

pairs.tendency: Two moves in a row let a player act on a secret role, and the others watch for who got lucky and why.
pros: Two moves can tell on a role.
Lucky streaks make people suspicious.
cons: A player has to cover for a double move.
Players may accuse the wrong person.

pairs.tendency: Asking a second question at once means one clue can lead to another before anyone else asks.
pros: A second question can follow a clue.
A chain of questions can crack a puzzle.
cons: Others lose a chance to ask.
A lucky player may solve it alone.

pairs.tendency: A bluffer with an extra turn can make two claims in a row, which can back up the lie or give it away.
pros: A second claim can back up the first.
A bluffer can try again right away.
cons: Two claims give a rival more to doubt.
A repeated bluff is easy to spot.

pairs.tendency: An extra turn lets a newcomer test a second move and find out more about the secret rule.
pros: A second go means a second test.
Learning the rule speeds up.
cons: Some mistakes get doubled.
The one who knows the rule has to say no twice.

pairs.tendency: The one who knows can give another hint at once, so the guessers have two hints to work with.
pros: Hints can build on each other.
Guessers gain more to work with.
cons: The answer may be given away.
A clue given too soon spoils the puzzle.

pairs.tendency: An explorer with an extra turn turns over a second area, so they learn more before the others know the first.
pros: A scout can see further.
The unknown shrinks faster.
cons: Others are left with an old picture.
A first look at danger comes with no pause.

pairs.tendency: Turns pass round the table, and an extra turn breaks the order for a moment because one player goes twice.
pros: The order has a surprise in it.
A lucky player gets more turns.
cons: Waiting players wait longer.
